tieu_de: Great Compassion mantra, Unthinkable Mystery
tom_tat: Today begins the Great Compassion retreat. In the evening, after the worship ceremony, the Great Compassion mantra will be recited. In the past, the number of all Buddhas who said this mantra was as many as ninety-nine billions of sands in the Ganges River, and Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, out of love for all...
noi_dung:
Great Compassion mantra, Unthinkable Mystery

Today begins the Great Compassion retreat. In the evening, after the worship ceremony, the Great Compassion mantra will be recited. In the past, the number of Buddhas who recited this mantra was as many as ninety-nine billions of sands in the Ganges River, and Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, out of compassion for all living beings, developed great compassion and rode the boat of compassion back to the Saha world to save all sentient beings from suffering. There is a sentence: "The ocean of suffering has no shore, turn around and find a port," As long as we faithfully recite the Great Compassion Mantra, we will surely see its inconceivable fulfillment.

In the past, in countless eons, Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva was taught the Great Compassion Mantra by the Heavenly Light King of Tranquility Tathagata, who rubbed his head with a golden hand, causing him, upon hearing it, to immediately attain Bodhisattva status at the Eighth Level. He immediately felt great joy and immediately made great vows as follows: "If I can benefit all sentient beings, then please give me a thousand hands and a thousand eyes." After making vows, suddenly the earth shook, halos emanating from all Buddhas in ten directions illuminated His body, then thousands of hands and thousands of eyes immediately adorned His body. Hands can support, eyes can illuminate. Thousand hands and thousand eyes symbolize countless magical powers and wisdom.

meaning of great compassion: Based on the sentence: "The power of compassion and suffering" Anyone who encounters all kinds of hardships, if they sincerely recite the Great Compassion Mantra, they can be at peace and turn bad things into good things. Avalokitesvara told Buddha: "If sentient beings recite the Great Compassion Mantra but are not satisfied, then I swear they will not attain enlightenment, unless their wishes are unwholesome or they do not recite them sincerely."

Reciting the Great Compassion Mantra will not only bring you freedom, but your wishes will also be fulfilled; can avoid suffering and accidents and be happy and peaceful; Overcoming all dangers, arriving at peace and safety. How can we stay away from suffering? Must recite the Great Compassion Mantra. How to escape danger? Must recite the Great Compassion Mantra. Don't consider the Great Compassion Mantra to be trivial or simple. I would like to tell you that if in your past and present lives you do not have good fate, you will not even hear the name of the Great Compassion Mantra, let alone recite it. Now, not only will you hear the name of the Mantra, but you will also be able to recite the Mantra with such sincerity. This is truly a once-in-a-million-lifetime opportunity, and you will also receive instructions from good knowledge on how to read, recite, accept, and practice. It's worth your respect! In short, the Great Compassion Mantra has unimaginable benefits.

During these seven days, we should sincerely and sincerely recite the Great Compassion Mantra with great respect and reverence, chanting until the mind is free of false thoughts. At that time, the heart calms down, or perhaps some people see a halo, some people see flowers appear, some people have their heads touched by Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, helping to open their wisdom. Or maybe you smell a strange scent, and even though you have earnestly recited it, you still don't see any strange phenomenon. Whether it is or not, don't be discouraged, just devote yourself to reciting with all your heart. When the time comes, we will definitely witness the realm of "touching the path," appears right before your eyes.

Regardless of what realm you see, or whether you don't see anything at all, the main thing is still diligently reciting. Those who see a good omen should not be attached to that good sign. Those who do not see any signs should not feel inferior and say to themselves: "A ! So I don't have good roots, why don't I see the Bodhisattva?" Sometimes good roots bear fruit early, sometimes late. If we feel like our good roots have not yet matured, we must continue to build up and make more merits. People say: "If you have not planted good roots, you must plant good roots; planted a good root, causing it to grow; has grown, making it mature; has matured, leading to liberation."

When you come to Kim Son Holy Temple for the first time, study the Buddha Dharma, practice the Buddha Dharma, you must devote yourself to studying, not afraid of suffering, not afraid of difficulties. Staying here for seven days, you should be courageous and diligent, stay away from false thoughts. If you study and think haphazardly at the same time, you won't be able to concentrate on your efforts. If the mind is not single, it will be difficult to give birth to feelings. That's one thing you must pay special attention to!

The benefits of diligently reciting the Great Compassion Mantra cannot be exhausted in words. Anyone who recites the Great Compassion Mantra will absolutely not fall into the three evil paths. If he falls into those evil paths, Avalokitesvara vows to never become a Buddha. Whoever is foolish and recites the Great Compassion Mantra, if he does not become a wise person, Avalokitesvara will also not become a Buddha. The Great Compassion mantra can cure eighty-four thousand types of diseases in the world. Whoever has an incurable disease, even doctors, Western or Eastern medicine, have to give up, but if they sincerely recite the Great Compassion Mantra, they will definitely not take medicine to be cured. The divine effect of the Great Compassion Mantra is truly inconceivable!

At Kim Son Thanh Temple, there was someone who had such a fulfillment. Treating cancer is not an easy matter, yet reciting the Great Compassion Mantra causes the disease to disappear. Divine power of

The Great Compassion Mantra is inconceivably miraculous. Just look at your efforts for seven days. Whoever is sincere will see it come true and benefit. Whoever is sick will recover. Anyone who is not sick will have their wisdom opened. Whatever you pray for, that's why the Great Compassion Mantra is called an inconceivable, vast inspiration, an unhindered great compassion dharani. The word dharani (Dharani) translated means the total retention, the total dharma, the retention of infinite meanings, also called mantras, or called mantra-words. In short, these are secret words.

The secret mantra includes the following four meanings:

In the spell, there is the name of the king of ghosts and spirits, so any little ghost who hears this name does not dare to do anything wrong and must respect the rules.

This mantra is considered a command in the army, if violated, it will be punished.

You can silently eliminate evil karma without even knowing it.

Mantra is the secret language of all Buddhas, only all Buddhas can understand it.

All of you who came to attend the Great Compassion Dharma Conference this time have good roots, are full of virtue, and have been matured by karma, so you came to Kim Son Pagoda. Hopefully once you get to "bao son" Then you won't have to return empty-handed, you will definitely have treasures to use for yourself. What treasure? It is Uncle Dai-Bi. The Great Compassion Mantra can cure illness, can subdue demons, can open up wisdom, can bring peace, or in other words, if you pray for something, you will definitely be satisfied.

This Dharma Assembly of Great Compassion is even more special because in China it is very rare to have a record-breaking session of Great Compassion recitation, lasting seven days as always. In other countries, do people recite the Great Compassion Mantra for seven days? I don't know, but in America, I think this is the first time. I hope all of you will sincerely recite the Great Compassion Mantra for immeasurable merit!

April 9, 1976, at Kim Son Thanh Tu

tieu_de: Namo Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva
tom_tat: Today, you gather here, attend the Avalokitesvara Chamber, to recite the holy name together: Namo Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. This is a precious and rare opportunity, don't waste your time. If you look down on yourself, it won't be helpful...
noi_dung:
Namo Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva

Today, you gather here, attend the Avalokitesvara Chamber, to recite the holy name together: Namo Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. This is a precious and rare opportunity, don't waste your time. If you look down on it, it won't be of any use. It's like a person who went to the mountain and returned empty-handed, which is very unfortunate. I hope that you will let go of everything to courageously recite with diligence. You will definitely feel inspired, and only then will you not miss the purpose of organizing this Avalokitesvara Chamber.

Normally, when entering the Avalokitesvara room, most people recite Buddha's name and Bodhisattva's name, then rest for half an hour before continuing their practice. In Hong Kong or Taiwan, roughly everyone recites in that way. We in this City of Ten Thousand Buddhas will recite continuously, without stopping, continuously from dawn to dusk, with no time to rest in between.

You should know that it's not right that we don't rest, or that it's wrong for everyone to rest. What does that mean? Because we have never used effort until now, we must now be very diligent and try our best to move forward. As for other people, they have been working hard for a long time, they have entered the path, whether they recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva or not, it's the same, they have no delusions, so they rest better than we diligently.

Suppose we have a conceited mind and think: "A! We in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas practice very vigorously and diligently, while other people are lazy and lazy." If we have that thought, all our merits will be destroyed. That is the complacent mind, the arrogant mind. We should understand that they have practiced diligently for countless lifetimes, and now they are resting and waiting for our people to follow behind. If you think like that, it's right, and only by working hard will you get good results. You can't use hard work and give rise to mental obstacles. The mental obstacle is complacency and arrogance, which can harm the seeds of Bodhi. We must diligently remember this point. In any case, we must avoid having a high-minded attitude, being arrogant, and avoid having selfish thoughts of self-interest, but must follow the correct sentence: "Dharma is equality, there is no high or low," That is the maxim of the practitioner.

At the beginning of our efforts, we must keep our minds right. If not done properly, no matter how diligent you are, you will become a demon. If the mind is righteous, no matter how hard one tries, one can become a Buddha. The path leading to Buddha or to ghosts is only different in one thought. Please pay special attention.

Why do we have to recite: Namo Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva? Because for sentient beings in the Saha world, He has causes and conditions. He is a Bodhisattva who seeks to save suffering and disaster. Some people think:

"When we encounter suffering and tribulation, we need to pray to Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. Now that we are neither suffering nor encountering trouble, why recite His name?" Does that mean we don't suffer at all? These are the five evil defilements - the depravity of life, the defilement of views, the defilement of afflictions, the defilement of sentient beings, the defilement of life - all sentient beings suffer, the suffering cannot be fully explained. Then within samsara, living beings go up and down, but isn't that suffering? One day, from morning to night, my mind is filled with false thoughts and urges. Isn't that a suffering? Then worry about yourself, want your own benefits, but if you can't worry, you won't be able to sleep peacefully; If you don't get what you want, you won't eat well. So you say it's not suffering? Who dares to say that he is not suffering? If they don't suffer because of one thing, they will suffer because of another. In short, they suffer without separation. Unless you let go of all things and don't pray for anything, then you won't suffer.

When we recite the sentence Namo Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, we must first understand the meaning of this sentence. Namo is Sanskrit, meaning to return to life. Quan means to observe, to use the magic of observing wisdom to observe. Who has the wonderful wisdom of observation? Lord Avalokitesvara, because He has that kind of wisdom, is able to perceive all the sounds of the world, and is not confused at all. The word That refers to the world. Sound is sound. Mr. Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva practiced the anti-text method of self-nature, so he used his mind to observe the cries for help of living beings in the world. When He hears it, he will immediately send himself to the place to save the victim from the sea of suffering, escape suffering and gain joy, so there is a verse that says:

The heavens ask for the heavens to respond,

Suffering often affects people.

Meaning:

Thousands of places to pray, thousands of places to respond,

He is the boat that rescues people from the ocean of suffering.

Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara is like a good mother. When her children pray to their mother, they will be saved by their mother, and will never be disappointed. Therefore, He has the title of Great Compassion, Great Compassion, Great Inspiration, Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva.

The word "Bodhisattva" có một nửa là tiếng Phạn, nói cho đủ là Bồ-đề-tát-đỏa [Bodhisattva], dịch nghĩa thành Giác-hữu-tình hay Hữu-tình-giác, cũng nghĩa tương tự. Enlightenment is enlightenment, sentient beings refer to sentient beings. An enlightened being is a living being among the enlightened people, or an enlightened being among the living beings. Bodhisattvas belong to the ranks of saints who are self-enlightened and enlighten others - self-enlightenment and help others enlightenment - without self-interest and self-interest, only thinking about the happiness of sentient beings, forgetting their own benefits. That is the spirit of selflessness.

As we want to ask Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva to help and bless us, we must sincerely recite: Namo Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, only then will the heart be sincere and the effect of induction will arise. At that time, Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva will hear the cry and come to save us from the ocean of suffering. On the contrary, if the calling is not sincere, or mixed with ideas of seeking fame and gain, there can be no response.

Now we recite the holy name: Namo Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, we should keep our hearts pure, recite earnestly and sincerely, not for our own personal benefit, but for the benefit of all sentient beings in this world of five impurities. We pray to Him for His compassion and kindness, so that all mankind in the world will be free from misfortune and sin, and blessings will be born, and all will benefit.

Everyone recites Namo Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva and follows the same principle, the power of inspiration is unimaginable. Any! Please bring all the merits by reciting the holy name dedicating merit to all sentient beings in the dharma world! It is:

May I bring this merit,

Toward all,

Disciples and sentient beings,

They all fully attain Buddhahood.

Opening the audience of the Avalokitesvara session at the Avalokitesvara Palace,

City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, from October 5 to 11, 1981

tieu_de: Reciting Avalokitesvara In Self-Nature
tom_tat: Now that we are single-mindedly reciting Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara, we must also recite Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara in our own nature. We must think that whatever is outside, there is also that inside, just like outside there is Quan...
noi_dung:
Reciting Avalokitesvara in Self-Nature

Now that we are single-mindedly reciting Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara, we must also recite Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara in our own nature. We must think that whatever is outside, there is also that inside, just as outside there is Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, inside there is also Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. Therefore, when reciting Avalokiteshvara, we must recite so that inside and outside are one, not two.

In our own nature, we already include all the virtues of countless Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, so when we recite the name Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva with our mouths, we must also be sincere in our hearts, all distracting thoughts will not arise, all false thoughts will be stopped, and only one mind will be focused on the thoughts. Don't wish for anything, don't be greedy for anything, and don't think: "What is the use of reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva?" We must consider reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva as a duty.

We recite to the level of "reciting but not reciting, not reciting but reciting," That is the realm of Avalokitesvara's self-nature, forming a mass, forgetting others and forgetting oneself, so where is there any more trouble? Where else is ignorance? When reaching the realm of unhindered freedom, great wisdom will be revealed, the wisdom of equality will appear, and the wonderful wisdom of observation as well as the wisdom of action will be complete. There are all four wisdoms, but only the first stage, because among the four wisdoms there are hundreds of thousands of different types depending on each stage. It's not like we've just seen the wisdoms appear and we think they're the same as the four wisdoms of all Buddhas. No matter what stage you are at or what level you reach, the ranks are not all equal.

Practitioners must clearly understand the meaning of "a difference of an inch, a mile," We must remind ourselves to work hard in the right direction, avoid turning aside, avoid entering into the realm of heresy, and mistakenly falling into a state of wrong knowledge and wrong views. We must always maintain right knowledge, right view, that is, mindfulness will appear.

When we recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, we mean reciting our own Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, not someone else's Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. What is called our Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva? It is that we and Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva are the same, reciting like that, meaning we also have the virtue of compassion, also have the joy and forgiveness of Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, and are also full of "seven tribulations, two prayers," also thirty-two incarnations like Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva.

tieu_de: Cultivation Must Know How to Reflect Light
tom_tat: People who practice must be sincere, must truly practice, must put in the effort and cannot be negligent. There are some people who say they practice the Bodhisattva way, but in reality they are just performing for their relatives to see. Every gesture, every action,…
noi_dung:
Cultivation Must Know How to Reflect Light

People who practice must be sincere, must truly practice, must put in the effort and cannot be negligent. There are some people who say they practice the Bodhisattva way, but in reality they are just performing for their relatives to see. Every gesture, every action, every word spoken, they show off for everyone to see, not for themselves. Those people need to know how to return the light and reflect, or wait for others to see them before reciting the holy name Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva - if they really have such a bad thought, they must quickly change it.

Anyone who practices but only wants others to see them practice is abandoning the roots and seeking the ends. Forgetting the roots to chase the top is impossible. Practicing is to let yourself see, to see yourself is to reflect back the light. Remember! Reflecting light, not external light. If you release light to shine outside, it means you just want others to notice, so that they can say that you are a truly cultivator. You must know that once the light is released, there is nothing left, because your light does not have much, once it is released it is gone. I haven't practiced to perfection yet, my light is weak. Wait until I practice to perfection, then it won't be too late to release the light. Now that you are in the practice phase, you should not release light.

Practicing is like studying. First, he went to elementary school, then high school, then university, and then a doctorate. Cultivation is like that, step by step, progress gradually, don't take shortcuts. Someone said: Zen school promotes sudden enlightenment and sudden enlightenment. We should understand that sudden enlightenment is about the principle - the principle of immediate enlightenment, but the truth must be practiced gradually. Sudden enlightenment is about the individual's sudden enlightenment, not about the time limit for sudden enlightenment. Once you practice, you will immediately become enlightened. In the past, for countless eons, people had practiced, planted the seeds of Bodhi, and worked hard to cultivate them, accumulating a little bit every day, until one day their efforts would bear fruit. There has never been a case of enlightenment without cultivating. Saying: "Reason is sudden enlightenment, truth is gradual practice" this is the meaning.

In this place, when we attend the Avalokitesvara retreat, we must bring all the spirit of reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva's name, and cannot be lazy to pray for peace or find excuses to procrastinate. If you let your mind wander, it means letting time pass in vain, missing the opportunity for enlightenment, what a pity! This Seven Avalokitesvara, please do your best, this Dharma conference is a rare opportunity. I hope you will cherish every moment and make an effort to recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. You will definitely have an inconceivable impact.

tieu_de: Why We Must Enter Avalokitesvara
tom_tat: We need to recite Buddha's name and Bodhisattva's name regularly. In fact, for practitioners, every day is considered to be in a retreat. As for us, because we have never used the effort, we need to define a...
noi_dung:
Why Do We Have to Enter the Avalokitesvara Seven?

We need to recite Buddha's name and Bodhisattva's name regularly. In fact, for practitioners, every day is considered to be in a retreat. As for us, because we have never put in the effort, we need to set a time for everyone to gather together, and then perform a retreat together, which is called a time to witness. During these seven days, all external conditions are let go, not a single thought arises, concentrate single-mindedly, recite the name Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. Reciting His name will be able to abandon all wrong knowledge and wrong views and at the same time increase right knowledge and right view. While reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, the mind is peaceful, breathing is regular, and the spirit is focused. There should be no sense of competition or a competitive mind. Competing and competing are the behaviors of worldly people. Practicing practice means not competing with others, not being jealous of anyone, everyone working together. Anyone who makes an effort to make an effort is the same as if we were making an effort ourselves. With that mindset, there is no competition between superiority and inferiority. Practitioners should not be careless and afraid of hardship, must be constantly diligent, always diligent, diligent every hour, every moment, every minute, every second. One minute of diligence is one minute of inspiration; Ten minutes of diligence is ten minutes of induction.

When we recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, is it sincere in our hearts? Venerable Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva above saw it very clearly. Whoever recites Him with a sincere heart will be blessed by Him with wisdom and clarity, good roots will grow, evil will be destroyed, three obstacles will be eliminated - that is, karma, retribution, affliction, in short, all evil karma will be destroyed. Therefore, when we recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, we must recite it with utmost sincerity. Whoever recites it sincerely will benefit; Whoever recites without sincerity will absolutely not receive inspiration.

In the Avalokitesvara chamber, there are people who recite sincerely, but there are also people who recite with joy, but not sincerely.

Seeing everyone chanting, I also chanted; Seeing everyone running, I also ran; Seeing everyone sitting, I also sit, before or after the true mind still does not arise (true mind means no delusions). When reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, there is no greedy mind, nor a seeking mind, meaning there is a true mind. Not fighting, not being selfish, not taking advantage of yourself, that also belongs to the true heart. Using effort with the true mind, all karma obstacles will be eliminated. If the mind is not true, karma obstacles still cling to it. Therefore, during the Avalokitesvara retreat, it is best to: "One less sentence, one more chant." There is a saying: Having attained the thought of the first death, it is promised that the dharma body will be active, meaning that by killing the impurities, the dharma body will appear (alive).

People who practice practice for the sake of ending birth and death, for the sake of saving sentient beings, not for the sake of being inspired. There is a saying: Believe in your will, believe in your true will; Thinking about clothes, there are clothes - clothes come - thinking about food, there is food, thinking about anything, that happens, this is the realm of the gods, but when the heavenly blessings are all enjoyed, they return to samsara to suffer. Cultivators should aim for the ultimate dharma of liberation, only then can they hope to escape the three worlds and end the part of birth and death.

tieu_de: Recite Avalokitesvara to Save Those in Distress
tom_tat: Buddhists Qua-Khiem (Hang Nhuong) recently recounted his experience of fleeing from Vietnam, encountering all kinds of dangerous situations, in short, ten deaths and one life. Just because female Buddhists Qua Khiem sincerely recited Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva should be…
noi_dung:
Reciting Avalokiteshvara to Save Those in Distress

Buddhists Qua-Khiem (Hang Nhuong) recently recounted his experience of fleeing from Vietnam, encountering all kinds of dangerous situations, in short, ten deaths and one life. Just because female Buddhists Qua Khiem sincerely recited Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, she received His compassionate protection, made everything peaceful, escaped the tiger's den and finally reached

The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to practice. Refugees from Vietnam

This City of Ten Thousand Buddhas has all heard about this. Hopefully they will also tell all the things they have encountered and publish them to the whole world. The day it will be published as a book, it will be titled "Victim Dan Thiep Hien Ky."

Right now, we are in America, safe and sound, not knowing what suffering or tribulation is. One must have been in tribulation to be able to fully experience the suffering. Therefore, I hope you should not follow the path of "not burning incense in normal times, but only embracing Buddha's feet when in trouble." There was no time at that time. We must be mentally ready: "Before it rains, prepare, before you're thirsty, dig a well." Suspected Yu'er's eyes, Wulin's thirsty'er woke up. Here we recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, which is to pray for the victims in the world, hoping that they will leave suffering and be happy, free from suffering. The goal of our retreat is to save the victims and pull them out of the sea of suffering, which is important for the lives and safety of humanity. This mission is so great that we must wholeheartedly recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. The more sincere you are, the more people you can help. Compassion, everyone has it. Again, the point of view of Buddhism is to save all sentient beings, so we must sacrifice our lives to recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva.

The mission of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is to save sentient beings all over the world. Because of the suffering of sentient beings, every day we recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, praying to Him with a thousand shining eyes, a thousand listening ears, a thousand hands to save and save all sentient beings. We now, in the Avalokiteshvara chamber, must try our best to recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. If one is lazy, one does not have compassion, and such a person does not have a virtuous mind, will not have merit and in the future, the achievements will be very limited. We practice according to the Mahayana dharma, we must have the spirit of self-forgetfulness to save others, pray for happiness for sentient beings, pray for peace for sentient beings; We recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, not for ourselves, but for the victims, because of their suffering we recite. With such a tone, our recitation will definitely bring great impact.

Gentlemen! After listening to the story of Buddhist Qua Khiem, I learned that Guan Yin is not only a vision to save suffering, but also protects sentient beings to be safe. He is the place where sentient beings can rely. During this Avalokitesvara That session, you must recite with sincerity. One more person chanting is one more part of the result; One more result is to have a peaceful place, that merit is really important. We do not pray for ourselves, for our own greed, but for peace, for security for all humanity. Those who are true Buddhists should act like that, should be equipped with such thoughts, they will definitely have the blessings of Buddha and Bodhisattvas.

tieu_de: The Story of a Man Who Prays for Dharma
tom_tat: Today I would like to tell a true story. About ten years ago, there was a guy who had a strange vision, neither white nor black. Dressed in a slovenly manner, with dirty clothes, about five feet tall, and as skinny as a stick...
noi_dung:
The Story of a Man Who Prays for Dharma

Today I would like to tell a true story. About ten years ago, there was a guy who had a strange vision, neither white nor black. Dressed in messy clothes, about five feet tall, body as skinny as a stick, face unchanged. That day he arrived at the big gate of Kim Son Pagoda, and there, he sat with his back against the wall. When it rained heavily, he still sat motionless. Someone told him to go somewhere else, but he remained silent and didn't pay attention. About three days later, I went to the temple gate to take a look. He never talked to anyone, yet he started talking to me. I asked him what his last name was, he replied: "The Thach family." What's the name, he replied: "Human Name" (Originally written 'human' is human). Asked again where he came from, he replied: "Down from the mountain." When asked what he came for, he replied: "Come to seek Dharma." I just said: "We don't have any dharma to pray for here. If you come like that, you will be disappointed." Guy replied: "I'm not disappointed."

After asking questions like that, he followed me into Kim-Son Pagoda, then followed the crowd, when he meditated, when he slept, but he absolutely did not eat, drink, or even urinate or defecate, what a strange guy. Every day he sat quietly meditating, not speaking, not moving. He looked like someone who had been poisoned, as well as someone who had come to sit and have fun. He hid a piece of charcoal in his body, and when asked about it, he said he used that piece of charcoal to keep warm. He stayed at the temple for a few days, working with the masses. Everyone spent time meditating, he also worked hard, when everyone went upstairs to sleep, he also went upstairs to sleep. Everyone was afraid that he would steal things, so they arranged for someone to guard him, and while he slept in the house, the guard also rested outside the door, in case he opened the door to go out and the guard could immediately detect him.

Suddenly one day, no one saw the "stone man" anywhere. The guard was very surprised. He didn't know what method he used to leave the temple without anyone knowing. How should we tell this story? Stone people still know how to go to Kim Son Holy Temple to seek the Dharma, not to mention that we, who are the spirit of all things, do not try to learn the Dharma. Isn't it a pity?

tieu_de: Migrate to the World of Ultimate Bliss
tom_tat: In China, people often hear the saying: "Avalokitesvara's family, Amitabha Buddha's family" (Avalokitesvara's family, Amitabha Buddha's family). Lord Avalokitesvara really has a special affinity with us, He is ready to take us home to live...
noi_dung:
Migrate to the World of Ultimate Bliss

In China, people often hear the saying: "Avalokitesvara's house, Amitabha Buddha's house" (Avalokitesvara's family, Amitabha Buddha's family). Lord Avalokitesvara has a special affinity with us, He is ready to take us to live forever in the land of Ultimate Bliss, without having to go through any immigration procedures. As long as we show sincerity and make a single request, we can reach it, there is absolutely no trouble. Only when there is no evidence of "one true thought" then we cannot go to the world of Ultimate Bliss.

How to have evidence of "a true thought?" It's so easy, so simple! We just need to sincerely bring our thoughts to mind: "Namo Amida Buddha," or "Namo Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva" or "Namo Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva" is enough, because Buddha Amitabha is the leader of the world of Ultimate Bliss, and Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara and Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta are the assistants standing on either side. Those people are called the Three Saints of the West. Whoever we recite the name of, chanting it until we have a single mind that is undisturbed and an untainted object, we will definitely receive karma rebirth, which means being born in the land of Ultimate Bliss even though we still carry karma, from the flower blooming we will see the Buddha or see the Bodhisattvas.

If you do not want to migrate to the world of Ultimate Bliss, then you do not need to recite the names of the Three Saints, but if you still want to return to Ultimate Bliss, you must recite the name of Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. When you are alive, you will be exempt from three disasters and seven disasters. When you die, you will be reborn in the Pure Land. There is nothing better than this.

We recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, chanting in such a way that we and Him are one, no separation, so that when we die, even if we don't want to, we will be reborn in Ultimate Bliss. Why is that? Because once the roots are solid, in the future they will have branches and leaves, bloom and bear fruit.

tieu_de: The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas Cleanses the Body and Mind
tom_tat: Reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva at the ashram is very easy to get a response. Reciting with a sincere heart, reciting without disturbing thoughts, reciting to the level of reciting Buddha samadhi, the wind will not blow, the rain will not fall, all wishes will...
noi_dung:
The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas Cleanses the Body and Mind

Reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva at the ashram is very easy to get a response. Reciting with a sincere heart, reciting without disturbing thoughts, reciting to the level of reciting Buddha samadhi, the wind will not blow, the rain will not fall, all wishes will be fulfilled. When reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, we must wholeheartedly revere and pay attention without any delusions, and we will definitely be inspired. No matter what delusions we have, Lord Avalokitesvara also knows. Whatever types of minds living beings have, Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva knows them all and sees them all. Reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva with utmost sincerity will certainly bring about an effect. If you are not sincere, there will be no response.

People in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must all be pure in body and mind, not allowing ignorance or affliction to arise, not being angry, always maintaining a gentle attitude, aiming for compassion, not being rude to anyone, not meddling in anything. Keeping it like that is truly reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva and truly worshiping Him.

Those who come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, bowing to the Buddha, cannot give rise to afflictions. If you have afflictions, not only will you not receive blessings, but you will also suffer more. No matter what situation you are in, you must practice the paramita of patience. The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a place to cleanse the body and mind. When there are afflictions, coming to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas will immediately make your body and mind pure. Why is that? Because of Him

Avalokitesvara blesses us, causing all our troubles to disappear at once.

Whoever comes to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must learn according to the spirit of compassion, joy and forgiveness of Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, must be equipped with the mindset of renunciation, self-interest and self-interest, with an open heart, tolerant of everything even if it is unsatisfactory. We met each other because we were destined to meet each other, so why would we argue with each other? There's nothing good about it! Those who are like that should try to change, those who are not should try!

The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a place to purify the habits of sentient beings. Coming here, those who smoke will not smoke, those who drink alcohol will not drink alcohol, those who gamble will not gamble, neither will drugs, toxic items will all be left behind. It's not only at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas that this happens, but wherever you go you will observe the precepts, that's because at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, the body and mind are purified, the body is healthy, the mind is healthy, the person is completely renewed. When the negative habits are eliminated, then it is truly reciting Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara and the wish to enter the Avalokitesvara retreat is not in vain.

Everyone is free from afflictions and has treasures. There is a saying like this:

No afflictions arise, no doubts arise,

Only worry about my own business, not other people's,

Be patient with what is not right, avoid arguing,

Peaceful, pure wisdom is born,

Clear mind about difficult things without hindrance,

Seeing one's nature is no longer met with sadness,

Worry, resentment, and a dark mind,

Buddha's light does not shine everywhere.

If you follow the above sentences, you will definitely have a special impression.

tieu_de: The more you recite Avalokitesvara, the less delusions you have
tom_tat: Reciting the holy name of Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva has the effect of cleansing the trash in our minds. Reciting one sentence reduces one false thought, reciting two sentences reduces two false thoughts. Reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva ten thousand times means...
noi_dung:
The more you recite Avalokitesvara, the less delusions you have

Reciting the holy name of Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva has the effect of cleansing the trash in our minds. Reciting one sentence reduces one false thought, reciting two sentences reduces two false thoughts. Reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva up to ten thousand times means that ten thousand false thoughts are cleansed. Someone said: "The magician is wrong! The disciple while reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva also felt false thoughts, the number of false thoughts that arose was more than the number of reciting the holy name." Saying so, the ability is so strong, it's inconceivable! On the one hand, chanting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, on the other, false thoughts arise! In fact, whoever said that did not recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, this is just a state of mind that is not present, looking but not seeing, listening but not hearing. Although he followed everyone to recite Avalokitesvara, he himself did not pay any attention to Her. Because he did not pay attention to Him, his false thoughts were born. When false thoughts come, the mouth chants but the mind becomes confused. While having false thoughts, the mouth also forgets to recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. Forgetting to recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, false thoughts arise again. That is a lack of seriousness and insincerity. He came here, not to recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, but just to follow everyone, so he did not recite properly, his voice was not strong, his energy was not full.

While reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, eyes look at Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, thoughts turn to Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, recognize Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva before your eyes, thousands of eyes shining on you, thousands of hands supporting you. The sound you recite is also clearly heard by your ears. Then the sound we recite is poured straight into our mind, and we receive that sound as if we would welcome the Bodhisattva himself to come and reign in our mind. If you already have Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva in your mind, there is no longer any delusion. Reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva is a miraculous medicine to cure the disease of delusion. Until the mind is pure, then there is freedom.

tieu_de: Reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva With All Six Senses
tom_tat: Reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva is not just to recite clearly with your mouth, but also to note it clearly in your mind. Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, all six senses, all recite together. Eye recitation, ear recitation, nose recitation,...
noi_dung:
Reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva With All Six Senses

Reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva is not just to recite clearly with your mouth, but also to note it clearly in your mind. Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, all six senses, all recite together. The eyes recite, the ears recite, the nose recites, the tongue recites, the body recites, the consciousness also recites, in short, all the senses recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva at the same time. That is called capturing the six senses, penetrating one door.

In the chapter on the Great World's Perfect Wisdom, the sutra says: "Taking care of all six senses, continuously meditating, attaining Samadhi, that is the best." This sentence can be explained as follows: Talking about taking control of all six senses means telling us to gather those six senses together, not letting them scatter, telling them to listen and obey seriously; What must be done to make the six enemies - the six senses - turn into six dharma protectors? Respecting the six senses means ordering them to keep the rules, not letting them do mischief; Train them to be mature and obedient. Not specializing in reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, what is the reason for that? It is because of not capturing the six senses and controlling the six enemies: eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body and mind. Because of that, they are free to roam around and cause trouble, leading to a state of wandering delusions, not being able to stay calm, and getting into trouble wherever they go.

If the six senses are all absorbed, then at that time the pure thoughts continue together. Pure thoughts are like waves on the surface of water, one after another without end. Reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva with a pure mind is the same. Reciting without interruption, reciting without stopping, reciting at a certain point immediately attains samadhi. Tam-ma-dia translated means right concentration, right feeling, that is the first Dharma door. When reaching this realm, all six senses chant the holy name of Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva at the same time.

Only by entering the samadhi realm can we realize the dharma of "Reciting Avalokiteshvara Samadhi," and only one can be called a person who has entered the Avalokitesvara retreat. If you have not yet attained this Dharma, you cannot be considered to have entered the Avalokitesvara chamber. For example, in the samadhi realm, a circuit starts from early morning until evening before resting. During that time, the mouth only knows how to chant Avalokitesvara and knows nothing else, all notions of time are gone, there is no knowing what is past, present, or future, all three are considered as nothing, that is the realm of samadhi.

Achieving this realm, reciting Avalokitesvara is reciting in a state of mental concentration, forgetting all afflictions. I haven't eaten yet or have already eaten, I don't remember anymore. Why? Because we dedicate ourselves to reciting Avalokitesvara. Clothes to wear or not to wear? Don't remember either. Why? Because we concentrate on contemplation

It's negative. Have you had any sleep yet? Don't know either. Why? Because we concentrate on reciting Avalokitesvara. If you really forget the three things of eating, dressing, sleeping, and resting, that is the realm of samadhi. In the mind there is no ignorance, no afflictions, no delusions. Reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, reciting it clearly, with joy and joy, there is nothing more peaceful, more refreshing. Is there a disease? The disease is gone. Is it painful? Also pain gone. Neither eating nor hunger, neither sleeping nor sleepy, that is the realm of the person reciting Avalokiteshvara Samadhi.

tieu_de: Examine Your Own Mistakes
tom_tat: As it says: "I can hear voices in the air," this means the realm of ghosts, not the realm of people entering concentration. A cultivator cannot say that but must follow the following sentences
noi_dung:
Examine Your Own Mistakes

As it says: "I can hear voices in the air," This is the realm of demons, not the realm of people entering concentration. Cultivators cannot say that but must follow the following sentences:

The nature of sentient beings vows salvation.

Self-nature afflictions vows to be interrupted.

The Dharma subject vows to learn.

Buddha's true nature vows to be achieved.

Practitioners must always turn back to reflect on themselves, not look outside to seek, because outside there is nothing to earn. Right in your own nature, everything is available and complete. Let's ask ourselves whether we practice or not? Is there any effort? Don't ask anything else, just ask if I am greedy? Having greed means not practicing. Not being greedy means practicing. That is the most important thing.

Ask yourself again, do you have anger? Suddenly someone hits me, will I get angry? If you get angry, it means you haven't been diligent. If you really don't get angry, you shouldn't consider yourself free of ego-clinging, that's just a partial reduction in that ego-clinging mind. We must follow the following sentences: "If you hit me, it's as if you didn't see it; scold me, treat me with reason" - Falling down, a view; If you insult me, you will be submissive - I hope you here will follow suit.

If you get angry, it means you haven't practiced and haven't let go. If we can let go, who is the one suffering? Who is the tease? If you are not bothered, you will not get angry, this is the duty of a practitioner. It cannot be said that we practice well, that is just one step forward. It is impossible to be arrogant and consider yourself good. As said: "Hey! You guys come here to watch our practice, we're number one in the world!" That is great arrogance! Great Demon King! Thousands of times, you should not have such thoughts, because in other words, it is wrong knowledge and wrong views.

Look at yourself and see if you are stupid? Is there anything that is not clearly understood or is still hindered? One thing is clear, everything is clear, and this is just the beginning of practice. We cannot say that we know enough, that everything is perfect, to say so is arrogance. There is a saying: "The vacuum has no self, the great path has no form." If it is emptiness, then what is a person? What is me? How can there be false thoughts? If one attains Samadhi, the nectar will naturally appear, there is no need to run anywhere to look for it, it is all already within the self-nature.

People who practice Buddhism cannot put on a false face, have the label of practicing but actually do not practice, that is what people say: "Hanging goat's head, selling dog meat," If you do things that are not in accordance with the Dharma, how can you attain Samadhi! A person who practices righteously and concentrates on reciting Avalokiteshvara will attain Samadhi. In the realm of Samadhi, when it's cold you don't feel cold, when it's hot you don't feel hot, when you're short of water you don't feel thirsty, when you're short of food you don't feel hungry. Such wonderful effects cannot be fully explained.

People who practice religion must practice with sincerity, focusing on the real thing and not being greedy for fake fame. Cultivation is about the real effort, putting it to the test. We cannot beat our own drums and trumpets and proclaim that we are virtuous people. Fake or real, you can tell at a glance. Practitioners cannot lie to others, lying to others is a crime that leads to hell. It's also impossible to practice a little bit and consider it full, just like a piece of cake cannot fill the stomach. Although there is a saying that "seeing an apricot will quench your thirst," But this feeling is only temporary, and does not really quench thirst. Having to follow the rules correctly is the correct path to practice.

tieu_de: Reciting Avalokitesvara During Emergency
tom_tat: Today I would like to pass on to you a crucial decision. That is the key to apply in times of real emergency. In those situations, we must stay calm, don't panic, put life and death aside for now...
noi_dung:
Reciting Avalokitesvara in an Emergency

Today I would like to pass on to you a crucial decision. That is the key to apply in times of real emergency. In those situations, we must stay calm, don't panic, put life and death aside for now, recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva wholeheartedly, then surely the danger will turn into good, and escape the evil.

In a moment of urgency, let us think: "We're going to die either way, so before we die, let's wholeheartedly recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, maybe that's hope." To act like that is to get lucky from danger.

When flying, the plane crashes in the air and is about to crash. At that moment let us recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. Because Avalokitesvara is a Bodhisattva who specializes in rescuing suffering, a Bodhisattva whose prayers are answered, if we do not recite His name, our lives will be in extreme danger and there will be no more hope. At that time, we sincerely pray and feel His compassion, and all the lives on the plane are saved. Entering the Avalokitesvara room, we must also generate such thoughts to diligently recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva.

Let's imagine again when riding a train, and suppose that as soon as we know the train derailed, that is, within that hair's breadth of time, if we do not recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, all the passengers on that train will die. Reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva means to make a cry for help. When the Bodhisattva hears the cry, even if he is thousands of miles away from mountains and rivers, he will come immediately to save us from suffering, extremely effective.

Imagine again that we are sailing at sea, unfortunately encountering a ship that is about to sink, the risk of being trapped in the belly of a fish. In the moment of danger, we recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, until the last moment, also recite. If so, it will definitely turn into evil.

Suppose we're sitting in a car driving fast on the road, suddenly the car can't control itself anymore, it flies over the edge of the road to the edge of a deep, vertical cliff. If a car falls to the bottom of a cliff, it will end its life, bones will be broken and flesh will be crushed. At that moment, if you recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, with all sincerity, the car will land safely, terrifying but not dangerous. This is the impact of the Avalokitesvara mindfulness method.

In a moment of emergency and danger, reciting one sentence of Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva is equivalent to reciting a hundred thousand sentences in normal times. Why is that? Because when there is no danger, the words I recite are not earnest enough, my heart is not sincere enough. Therefore, when reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, we must be wholeheartedly sincere, wholeheartedly truthful, then that feeling will truly be inconceivable.

Recently I told Qua Khiem: "Today in this City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, if you recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, imagine that you are on a boat and sincerely recite it, and you will definitely have an impact. Back then, in times of great waves and great danger, if one did not recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, there would be no hope for today. Only by reciting Avalokitesvara can there be some hope, or perhaps salvation, so if you pray wholeheartedly, the disaster will eventually overcome, the wind will calm down, and you will reach the shore. Now I recite Avalokitesvara and still have time to rest, because I am no longer in a dangerous situation like before." The truth is:

As the day passed, the network gradually decreased.

Like a fish without water, what's so fun about it?

The masses!

You have to be diligent and save yourself.

Think about impermanence, don't be careless!"

Recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, depending on the place and time, in other words, walking, standing, lying down, sitting, all can be recited. Whether you recite it with your mouth or your mind, your merits are equal. Don't make distinctions, always depend on fate. Remember that if you wait until you die to chant, it is too late and there is no more chance. Hence the saying: "Think about impermanence, don't be careless."

tieu_de: Reaching the Realm of Unmoved Mind
tom_tat: People who study Buddha Dharma must know Buddha Dharma and practice Buddha Dharma. It can also be said to eat according to Buddha Dharma, wear Buddha Dharma clothes, sleep in Buddha Dharma, walk, stand, lie down, and sit all in Buddha Dharma. People who know Buddha's teachings always...
noi_dung:
Reaching the Realm of Unmoved Mind

People who study Buddha Dharma must know Buddha Dharma and practice Buddha Dharma. It can also be said to eat according to Buddha Dharma, wear Buddha Dharma clothes, sleep in Buddha Dharma, walk, stand, lie down, and sit all in Buddha Dharma. People who know Buddha's teachings are always altruistic, putting everyone's interests first, and absolutely do not think about their own interests. In short, we must destroy the disease of "clinging to self." Only knowing others, not knowing oneself, to reach that level is called one who knows the Buddha Dharma.

People who practice Buddha Dharma will never be moved in any situation. Why is that? Because if you practice diligently to a certain extent, you will have spiritual power, and from there you will be able to distinguish which realm is real and which realm is false. No matter what realm is in front of you, the truth is good, the falsehood is also good, there is nothing that moves the mind. That's why we often see the saying in meditation: "Buddha comes to slash Buddha, ghosts come to slash ghosts," The meaning is not to be attached to anything. Non-attachment is liberation, liberation is freedom. Studying Buddha is a quest for liberation, a quest for freedom, that is, no longer being bound by the five desires, only then can one escape the three worlds, reach the Pure Land of Everlasting Light, and be close to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

What is the real realm? As long as thoughts do not arise in the mind, all realms before the eyes are real. Once the foolish mind is confused, the mind thinks of seeing this and that, then the realm at that time is mostly false. The realm of Dai Vien Kinh Tri is real, but the realm that appears in the mind of discrimination is fake, so there is a saying: "To have a mind is to think, to have no mind is to feel." Anyone who studies Buddha Dharma must try to remember it! In all realms that come to us, we must have eyes to investigate the dharma (choose the dharma). We perceive the realm without clinging to it. Regardless of whether it is real or fake, we are not attached to it. If you accept, the true realm will become false. If you do not accept, the false will become true. What's the meaning? Take water and ice for example, ice is originally from water, but water is not ice, the physical properties of water are like that, everyone knows. As in the sentence: "Defilement is Bodhi, Bodhi is not affliction," then afflictions can represent ice, Bodhi is water, and ignorance is coldness. Because of ignorance, water freezes; Without ignorance, ice turns into water. When it is ice, it is in the three worlds, subject to the cycle of birth and death; When it is water, it will escape the three worlds without birth and death.

Please pay attention, you must apply your efforts right here. Luc To once said: "Do not think good, do not think evil, at that moment, what is the original face of the Venerable Minh?" That's the meaning. If you think neither good nor evil, that means you don't have any thoughts; thoughtless, non-dwelling, necessarily empty, nothing at all. At that time, you will see your original face, that is, your origin.

tieu_de: Must Save The World's Danger
tom_tat: Now let's study a big problem, but any problem is not outside the scope of the four words "good and evil cause and effect." Good will win, evil will defeat, that is the law of cause and effect. People often say: "Grow melons and you'll get melons, grow beans...
noi_dung:
Must Save The World's Danger

Now let's study a big problem, but any problem is not outside the scope of the four words "good and evil cause and effect." Good will win, evil will defeat, that is the law of cause and effect. People often say: "Grow melons and you'll get melons; plant beans and you'll get beans." For that reason, our world is not destroyed. If the truth is the opposite, that is, good will fail, evil will win, then there is no longer natural law, and if there is no more natural law, then the world has been destroyed, that is, there has been an end of the world.

How to keep the world from being destroyed? Must improve people's minds. If people's hearts are good, light will shine throughout the world. Light is wisdom, and a person with wisdom is a person with the right mind, everything they create and do is with great light, without selfish thoughts. Our thoughts are all directed towards the happiness of humanity, without any distinction, this race, that country, the world is all gathered into one home of the great world. Nowadays, people's hearts are different from before, most of them are selfish, self-interested, only compete for their own interests and sacrifice the happiness of the collective, so the world is getting darker every day, every day more stupid, every day more dangerous. The day of destruction seems to be near, just a hair's breadth away, and if we don't find a way to save, everyone will share the same fate, no one will have a chance to survive. But how to save this? The scriptures teach: "Evil deeds are not done, good deeds are followed." Everyone is oriented towards good, not towards evil, from the top, down to hundreds of families, everyone uses wisdom as light to chase away ignorance and darkness. If so, the face of the world will change from yin to yang, and war will turn into peace.

Now we are living in a long night, living and dying in a drunken dream. Because the night is long, we feel the need for light; Because of darkness, people's hearts are filled with sadness and sadness. In the atmosphere of light, people's hearts will be happy. Darkness and light are only in the hearts of good and evil people. Destroying the world is in the human mind, but creating the world is also in the human mind. We are people who study the Buddha Dharma, which is to eliminate false thoughts and find the true mind, so the Buddha Dharma is the talisman that saves the world, a precious example to improve people's minds.

In life, if there are good things, there will also be bad things. For example, like a television, it can tell us about major domestic stories and international developments. A saying people often say: "Baccalaureate students are not able to graduate, they can easily understand the world's affairs," The baccalaureate doesn't go out the door and knows everything about the world. This is a good use of television, but it also has a bad side. Children who watch television are often negatively influenced, learn to cheat, commit unethical acts, destroy family happiness, cause chaos in society, become bad teenagers, and cause scandals everywhere. If that's the case, how can there be peace in the future when those people come to rule? That is one of the disadvantages of television. As we worry about the next generation and the future of the world, we should strictly forbid children from watching television, or absolutely not buy television sets, that is the ultimate measure, stopping the evil that creates evil from the root.

The world today has reached a stage where clarity has been obscured into darkness. So what to do? As a member of humanity, we should first try to use our own bodies to eliminate our habits, remove all our greed, anger, and ignorance, and use our own bodies to influence others. Our own thoughts and behavior must be truly appropriate, then we can advise everyone to be good and use it as a model, otherwise it is just talk for fun, of no use.

(Yearbook records: To pray for world peace, the two shamans Heng That and Heng Trieu brought themselves to act by example, bowing every three steps, advising people to be good, eliminating the three poisons, which are the minds of greed, anger, and ignorance. If everyone does not have those three poisonous minds, the world will be peaceful, and if there is peace, it will not be destroyed. On the contrary, if there is a nuclear war, the world will be destroyed.)

Everyone who is responsible for the affairs of the world has the thought of compassion for humanity. Like Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha in the past, when cultivating the Bodhisattva path, he endured such asceticism. Why? Because we want to make an impact on sentient beings, causing them to follow the Dharma and practice, so that we can leave suffering and be happy. I often say: "If you endure suffering, suffering will end, if you enjoy blessings, blessings will be consumed."

tieu_de: Memorial of Mr. Sadat
tom_tat: When news broke that Mr. Sadat, the president of Egypt, was in trouble, everyone in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas mourned, and the world lost a leader of the peace movement. Although he is a Muslim, with an open mind,...
noi_dung:
Memorial of Mr. Sadat

When news broke that Mr. Sadat, the president of Egypt, was in trouble, everyone in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas mourned, and the world lost a leader of the peace movement. Although he is a Muslim, with an open mind and not attached to religious boundaries, he holds the position of honorary principal of Dharma Realm University.

With the principle of serving world peace, Mr. Sadat deserves everyone's admiration. In the Middle East, he campaigned hard to reduce the risk of war, which was an extremely difficult job serving world peace.

He very much responded to the principles of Dharma Realm Buddhist University, willing to support and later willingly took on the position of honorary principal of the school. Although he was assassinated, his spirit forever remained in the world. Birth and death are inherently illusory, but the karma left behind for the world is real. Let's take for example the character Quan Van Truong in China, with his great righteousness, his spirit still remains forever. Although he was later harmed at the hands of Dong Ngo, his reputation remained for centuries and is still revered by everyone.

I think that although Mr. Sadat was unfortunately harmed, he was a man who sacrificed himself for his country, so his peace-loving spirit will be immortal forever.

To pay tribute to a peaceful leader, tomorrow (October 9, 1981) at 9:00 a.m., we will hold a dharma conference to commemorate Mr. Sadat. We chant sutras dedicating merit to him. In his Muslim world, if he understands the principle of equality of Buddhism and is not dependent on religious color, he will certainly be very pleased.

tieu_de: Greed, Anger and Stupidity Obstacles to the Path of Cultivation
tom_tat: Talking about the time we spend in this world, it passes quickly in the blink of an eye. Yet no one can let go, they just hold on tightly, clinging to the east and west, considering this world as real, from there they strive for fame and profit, and...
noi_dung:
Greed, Anger and Stupidity Obstacles to the Path of Cultivation

Talking about the time we spend in this world, it passes quickly in the blink of an eye. Yet no one can let go, they just hold on tightly, clinging to the east and west, considering this world as real, from there they strive for fame and gain, forever wandering around in the circle of profit and fame, for the sake of fame and fortune, doing crazy, unethical actions. The ultimate result is just for the sake of fame, die with fame, for profit, die with profit. In my life, I fought for you, but for the sake of fame and fortune, I went crazy, what is the reason? Because people have not yet realized the three poisons of greed, anger and ignorance. This type of poison is much more terrible than other poisons. Poison only harms the body, not the mind. The three poisons harm both the body and the mind, making us crazy. In the light of it, it destroys the family, in the worst case it destroys the country, and even destroys the world. Therefore, those three poisons are the enemies of humanity.

Why in the world are there murderers, arsonists, fornicators, and robbers? Because people are greedy, angry, ignorant, and these three poisons are favored, making people greedy without getting bored. When you encounter something you wish for but it doesn't work, you get angry. If it's light then it hides inside, if it's heavy then it comes out into action, turning into a struggle, sometimes even into war. That's why the world is not peaceful. If everyone keeps a pure heart, is not greedy in heart, and works with a compassionate mind, then the natural world will be peaceful and there will be no more wars.

If we want to completely solve the world's problems, we must target the three poisons to practice, find ways to make people not greedy, not angry, and not ignorant. Can you do that? The only solution is to believe in Buddha-dharma, according to the tenets of Buddha-teaching, that is, to use precepts, concentration, and wisdom to eliminate greed, anger, and ignorance. That is the basic measure to solve the problem. If you keep the Five Precepts, you will be completely greedy; If you have concentration, there will be no anger; Having wisdom means being free of ignorance. The three poisons are an infectious disease. The three studies - precepts, concentration, wisdom - are the medicine commonly used to treat them. When you encounter the disease, they are immediately effective, like setting up a pole and immediately seeing its shadow.

Everyone learns Buddha-dharma, everyone does not have greed, anger and ignorance, then the world's problems will be solved. However, getting there is not easy. Why? Because people's hearts are different from before, morality has degenerated, people lie to others, and to achieve their goals, people use no means. People only talk about profit, but do not talk about morality, like that crook selling wine mixed with water, trying to deceive customers for profit. People say "hang the goat's head, sell the dog meat," that is a fraudulent act. In the past, doing business, selling real goods, setting real prices, raising standards without lying to young or old. Nowadays in karma business, there is no longer any concept of morality, buyers and sellers cheat each other, no one is honest anymore. If you do business with sincerity and have a clear sign to sell at the right price, no one will have any trouble. Why lie? To summarize in one word, it is all due to greed for profit.

The farmer, who was originally loyal, is now influenced by the business world and is no longer honest. They grow cereals and vegetables using chemical fertilizers. They raise cows, goats, pigs, and chickens and mix animal food with chemicals to help them grow quickly, causing consumers to be poisoned by eating those things for a long time. That is greed for money and harms the lives of others. The law should have taken measures to punish them, but they are still outside the law, there is no other way to encourage them further. It's just that because they want to make a lot of profit, they ignore the life and death problems of others. They are even more cruel than the merchant who mixes water in wine. Nowadays, cancer is increasing day by day, mainly because of the farmers and businessmen mentioned above.

Therefore, wise people strongly encourage the use of natural foods, not processed foods. However, for people who are greedy for food, even if these things reach their ears, they will not listen. They just eat until they have a full stomach. It is like swallowing a slow detonator. At the right time, it will explode and cause blood vessels to burst. Mild cases are symptoms of stroke, severe cases can be fatal. Yet, even though the mirror of the front car was far away, the car behind was still following the same track.

This is enough to see the harmful effects of greed, anger, and ignorance, which cannot be counted. Not only for ordinary people, even monks, if not careful, can also receive the above mentioned harm. As soon as the effort brought a little concentration, it was completely burned by the fire of ignorance. How to avoid that fire of ignorance? Must practice the paramita of patience, and absolutely not get angry is a prerequisite. Not being angry means having wisdom. With the light of wisdom, the darkness of ignorance will be dispelled. Out of darkness, all actions are clear and righteous. So how should we practice? First of all, observe the precepts, if you keep the precepts, you will have concentration. Having concentration means having wisdom. If precepts, concentration, wisdom, and the three studies are complete, greed, anger, ignorance, and the three poisons will self-destruct.

tieu_de: Premonition Avalokitesvara
tom_tat: Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva's compassion and inspiration are truly inconceivable. If we all sincerely recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, then karma obstacles will definitely be eliminated and good roots will grow. There are many stories…
noi_dung:
Premonition Avalokitesvara

Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva's compassion and inspiration are truly inconceivable. If we all sincerely recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, then karma obstacles will definitely be eliminated and good roots will grow. There are many stories about His inspiration, now I would like to tell a story that happened in America. There was a woman who went to the hospital to give birth. This was a case of difficult birth, so the doctor had to perform surgery to remove the baby, but during the surgery, the woman's urine pipe was cut without realizing it. After surgery and stitches, the pregnant woman went home for several days without even urinating, while her body swelled up. Seeing that something unusual happened, this woman went to the doctor to ask about the illness, but the doctor did not understand what the illness was. After seeing that his whole body was swollen, the patient had to have his condition re-examined. At that time, his blood pressure had dropped to as low as 18 degrees, the toxins had accumulated with him, there was no way to treat him, he had to lie down and wait for death. Some friends of the victim called Van Buddha Thanh for help. When people reported to me, I told them to sincerely recite Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. They were very sincere in chanting Guan Yin, and just two and a half hours later, the edema gradually disappeared, blood pressure increased, the urinary tract became clear again, the victim recovered his health very quickly and was discharged from the hospital. The stories about cases of people coming back from death's door, or being reborn from dangerous illnesses, or stories of overcoming disasters and overcoming disasters, in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, are too numerous to tell, now I will only tell that one story.

tieu_de: Transmission of Wisdom Opening Mantra
tom_tat: The Heart Sutra of the Prajna Paramita, called the Heart Sutra for short, can open up wisdom, helping to stay away from madness and dreams.
noi_dung:
Transmission of Wisdom Opening Mantra

The Heart Sutra of the Prajna Paramita, called the Heart Sutra for short, can open up wisdom and help to stay away from madness and delusion.

Kinh says:

Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, when he deeply contemplated the perfection of wisdom, saw that the five aggregates were empty, overcoming all suffering. Hey, Sariputra, form is no different from emptiness, emptiness is no different from form, form is emptiness, emptiness is form, feeling, perception, and consciousness are all the same. Hey, Sariputra, all dharmas are empty. . .

If we can see that all dharmas are illusory and floating, then we can let them all go and achieve liberation.

In the Shurangama Mantra, there are also two sentences that can open up wisdom. I will pass them on to you tomorrow evening. Want money? Don't want. There is a saying: "Thousands of taels of pure gold do not sell the Way. At the crossroads, we bid farewell to the negative" (Thien Luong golden does not trade, the cross chews the head and sends the sound of wisdom). If wisdom is opened, freedom will be realized, all afflictions will be gone, and Bodhi will appear before your eyes.

tieu_de: Six Paths samsara
tom_tat: Why are we crazy? Because there is no wisdom. Why do you betray the sense of union with the world, union with the world, and turn away from enlightenment? It is also due to lack of wisdom. Why does it circulate in the six realms? Also because there is no…
noi_dung:
Six Paths samsara

Why are we crazy? Because there is no wisdom. Why do you betray the sense of union with the world, union with the world, and turn away from enlightenment? It is also due to lack of wisdom. Why does it circulate in the six realms? It is also due to lack of wisdom. Therefore, cultivating the path must take wisdom first. Buddha must cultivate blessings and cultivate wisdom, blessings and wisdom together, then he will attain Supreme Enlightenment.

"Do not think that good deeds are small and do not do them," tu blessings is like that. "Do not see a small evil and do it," that is cultivating wisdom. "The evil do not do," this is cultivating wisdom. "All good deeds are done," so tu blessings. Therefore, cultivators should not be greedy for small comforts, take little to be enough, and must remember that everything is an illusion, like bubbles like a shadow, and cannot last. This necessary awareness must be clearly understood, not to be confused by worldly gain and fame. Like the sentence: "To see sobriety is to transcend the world, to see delusion is to be damned" (seeing awakening from the world, seeing delusion and falling into hell), so we must quickly overcome the six paths of samsara.

What are the six paths of samsara? That is, gods, humans, asuras, animals, hungry ghosts, and hell. Although the six paths are not the same, they rotate and circulate together. Our fate is like a speck of dust in space, one moment in the sky, one moment a human, one moment an animal, a hungry ghost, nothing is certain, we cannot control ourselves. Practicing practice is to end birth and death and escape the bondage of samsara. Heaven's blessings are all enjoyed and then come down, so there is a saying:

The six desires of the gods and the five declines,

Three meditations, heaven and earth, wind tai,

Renjun cultivates phi phi phi think,

Unlike the West, returning to the past.

Translated means:

The heavens of desire have five declines.

In the sky of the three meditations (of the Rupa Realm) there is a storm.

Even if one can cultivate to the heaven of non-perception (of the formless realm).

It's not as good as going to the West.

I thought I was out of samsara, but it turns out I'm still stuck in circulation, through the above sarcastic sentences. Practice diligently.

We humans do not know suffering, so we do not know how to practice. Don't think that the status of animals is very far away from us. In fact, animals also have flesh and bones like us. If we do not practice, in just a blink of an eye we will be reduced to being animals. Each individual has his or her own hell. Having afflictions means having hell. Therefore, you should quickly cultivate the path and escape the six realms of samsara to achieve liberation.

Dharma Master Hang Tai

Gentlemen! "The hard-to-obtain human body has now been obtained, the difficult-to-find Buddha Dharma has now been heard, the hard-to-find good knowledge has now been found," I am truly fortunate to have all three of these conditions. My reason for leaving the home life was because I witnessed my mother's pain when she was sick. I felt impermanence in life and didn't know where to go. I don't know if I will be a human in this life, and will I still be a human in the next life? So in 1979, I went to Thuong Nhon, praying to Him to let me leave the home life. Thuong Nhon asked: "Why do you want to leave the home life?" I replied: "When I saw my mother suffering from a painful illness and then suddenly passing away, I felt the suffering of birth and death, so I made up my mind to leave the home life." Leaving the home life to practice religion means wanting to end birth and death, leave the three worlds, and no longer be entangled in the six realms of samsara.

tieu_de: Dharma Master Hang Doan
tom_tat: That time was the first time I went to Hong Kong, a place with the beautiful name "Pearl of the Orient." Looking at the scene, the people, the crowded and crowded vehicles, life on this island is definitely very urgent...
noi_dung:
Dharma Master Hang Doan

That time was the first time I went to Hong Kong, a place with the beautiful name "Pearl of the Orient." Looking at the scenery, the crowded and crowded people and vehicles, life on this island is definitely very tense, unlike in the vast United States, where people live more leisurely and freely. But, once residing on this island, and wanting to have a peaceful mind and peaceful mind, there is a way to recite the names of Bodhisattvas, such as Namo Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, or Namo Amitabha Buddha. The reason is that reciting Buddha's name can eliminate evil karma, eliminate dangerous diseases, or unsatisfactory events and increase our good roots. Just like in my case, in 1978, the first time I went to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to attend the Avalokiteshvara retreat, Thuong Nhon told me to regularly recite Namo Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. So from that time on, I learned to recite the name of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva according to circumstances, when driving, when walking, and when I chant the Great Compassion Mantra. I believe that as long as we sincerely and earnestly recite, Buddha and Bodhisattvas will constantly be by our side to help us, so that we can have all things as we wish, with a peaceful mind and body!

tieu_de: Seven Enlightened Bodhisattvas
