tom_tat: The person who studies Buddha Dharma must have enough right knowledge and right view. Only by having right knowledge and right view will you know how to practice. Only by having an accurate Dharma method can you have an accurate Dharma circuit, so first of all you must understand that...
noi_dung:
Seven Enlightened Bodhisattvas

The person who studies Buddha Dharma must have enough right knowledge and right view. Only by having right knowledge and right view will you know how to practice. Only by having an accurate dharma door can you have an accurate dharma circuit, so first of all you must understand what the seven Bodhisattva perceptions are.

Perception part: To be aware means to clearly understand the path of practice.

Tracing the dharma of enlightenment: You must know what is right, what is evil, what is good, what is bad, you must have a selective eye, so as not to get lost on the wrong path. If you don't know how to choose, you will easily be led down winding alleys and won't be able to find your way, so investigating the dharma of perception is extremely important. If you want to know how to choose correctly, you must have wisdom, otherwise you will keep choosing over and over again, and still make mistakes. Mistakes are due to lack of wisdom, due to lack of wisdom in choosing the dharma. If you don't know how to choose, it's easy to take a turn.

Diligent awareness: If you clearly understand Buddha's teachings but then put it aside and don't make the effort to practice, it's no different than talking and eating all day long without ever actually tasting the taste of the Dharma. This perception is about diligence. As you know how to choose the dharma, grasp the essence of the dharma accurately, and practice diligently, day and night in the six periods of time, body and mind, do not be lazy; Diligence in the body means reciting the Buddha, bowing to the Buddha, chanting sutras, repentance ceremonies, etc., diligence in the mind means constantly reciting without forgetting, without giving rise to false thoughts.

Only by knowing how to choose the right Dharma can we avoid blind practice. Practicing blindly without encountering a good wise man to guide you will result in not following the Buddha path but going to hell. Thinking you are following the Bodhisattva path, you will end up following the demon path. Why is it so serious? Because of the wrong view, wrong cause and effect, the more you practice, the farther you go from your pre-determined goal, meaning "one inch wrong, one mile away," or as people often say:

Butt dong transmits butt dong

One story, two different stories

Master descends to hell

Disciples go back to work

Translated means:

Foolish people pass on to foolish people,

One transmission and two do not understand,

Master went to hell,

The disciples also came down to serve him.

Joyfully aware: Having the eyes to choose the dharma, one must have a joyful mind and diligently practice. It's not that three times I'm diligent, three times I'm frustrated with myself; You should not be troubled all day long, frown and grimace, what is necessary is not to be lazy, know how to be happy and diligently apply your efforts.

Except for perception: However, a joyful mind is not the end. We must return to peace in the mind, get rid of ignorance and afflictions, and eliminate bad habits. After eliminating it, you will feel the fullness of the source of Dharma joy.

Releasing awareness: When the mind has returned to calm, we need to let go of that calm, which means not being attached to anything. Must "sweep away all dharmas, leave all appearances," When you reach the inner realm, you don't feel the body or mind, and the outside world doesn't exist.

Right concentration and enlightenment: Once you have completed the method of letting go, you will have the power of concentration. Only with right concentration can there be right feeling. Right concentration here is not the kind of confused concentration, it is not the mindless concentration, or the mindless concentration of heaven, that is not ultimate.

Mindful awareness: Entering right concentration, the mind will have mindfulness, meaning accurate mindfulness. When you have mindfulness, you will no longer fall into trouble, morning and night you will no longer have false thoughts, and only then will you realize the three non-regressions: Thoughts do not retreat, taste does not retreat, actions do not retreat.

When it comes to concentration, practitioners immediately know that it is meditation, or "meditation-na," a Sanskrit noun (dhyana) meaning "meditation," that is, stopping all delusions, and is also called "thinking practice." Good thinking is "greed," As in the first dialogue, refer to the question "Who is the Buddha?" or greed for "original appearance from before the parents were born."

Now, I would like to explain the realm of the four meditations.

Initial meditation, Rebirth of joy and happiness: Breathing stopped. There is no breathing on the outside, but on the inside the breathing is still active. This is an inconceivable realm that only cultivators have and know, outsiders cannot understand. This type of meditation leaves the worldly joy but enjoys the fullness of Dharma joy, lives through meditation (happy meditation) and also achieves a little state of insight and enlightenment.

Second meditation, concentration gives birth to joy and happiness: The level of happiness here is higher than in the first stage of meditation, the meditator is always in a state of joy and that joy is born from concentration. Cultivating to this level will stop the meridians in the body from moving.

Three meditations, wonderful joy and happiness: Reciting steadfastly, stopping reciting joy, because still having joy means still having attachments. Now let's get rid of all the thoughts of joy and happiness.

Four meditations, pure discharge of thoughts: Let go of all thoughts, no more thoughts. At that time, there was no longer any obstacle in my mind, but I still hadn't gone beyond the Three Realms. This is a progressive result of the practice of concentration, not yet a high realm, to the point where there is no need to practice anymore, thinking that one has enlightenment leads to arrogance. At this point, I need someone else to prove it to me, I can't confirm it for myself. People who cultivate the Way must be like that, they cannot be arrogant or speak false words, otherwise they will fall into hell. Anyone who studies Buddha cannot create karma that is both good and unwholesome in such a mixed way, and cannot have such selfish ideas.

If someone claims to be a good intellectual, let us use the following six criteria to judge whether they are truly a good intellectual or not:

Observe whether that person is greedy, is he greedy for fame, profit, money, or lust?

Good knowledge does not argue with others, so see if that person has a competitive heart?

See if they are greedy? Is it true?

See if they are selfish?

See if they are self-serving?

See if they lie or not?

If all of the above criteria are met, then that person is not a good intellectual but an evil intellectual, or perhaps a demon or a pagan. On the contrary, if we consider that all of the above things do not exist, then that person is truly not greedy, not competitive, not seeking, not selfish, not self-seeking, not lying. We can believe that that person is truly a wise person and we can feel secure in studying without fear of going down the wrong path.

The evening of December 11, 1981

tieu_de: In America, Buddha-Dharma is at the Beginning
tom_tat: In America, Buddhism is very new. However, Buddhism in America is not unique to America but common to the world. True Buddhism is not limited to any nationality, any locality, the issue of self and others...
noi_dung:
In America, Buddha-Dharma is at the Beginning

In America, Buddhism is very new. However, Buddhism in America is not unique to America but common to the world. True Buddhism is not limited to any nationality or locality; there is no distinction between self and other people.

In Asia, some people admit that this is the age of the end of dharma, but dharma is not divided into true dharma or end of dharma, only when people refuse to practice, it is truly the age of end of dharma. There is a saying: "People spread the dharma, not people spread the dharma." Don't ask haphazardly, try to practice, then naturally the Dharma will stay with the world forever. If people do not practice, the dharma will come to an end. I have been in Hong Kong for over ten years, and there are many young people following me to study Buddha Dharma. The reason is that I like young people. Later, when fate ripened, I went to America. From 1961 to 1968, I was in the "graveyard," That's why I took the title "The Middle Monk's Tomb," a monk in the tomb, implying that I am not competing with anyone. Tell me I'm right, I don't argue, tell me I'm wrong, I don't argue either. At first I lived in a basement, it was very damp, then I moved to a relatively better place, and spent several years accomplishing nothing. In 1968, a few students from Seattle came to attend the summer camp. I lectured the crowd on the Shurangama Sutra, then taught them meditation and practice at night and in the afternoon. Back then, they didn't understand anything, so I had to take care of everything by myself: preaching the sutras, preaching the Dharma, lighting the stove, taking care of the water, washing the dishes, cooking, all by myself. After I finished teaching the Shurangama Sutra, these students left Seattle and moved to San Francisco to live. In 1969, there were five leaving the home life people who went to Taiwan to receive ordination, and since then there have been truly leaving the home life people in America. After that, I preached the Lotus Sutra of the Wonderful Dharma, then the Dharma Jewel Platform Sutra

The Sixth Patriarch, the Dai Phuong Quang Hoa Nghiem Sutra, the Avatamsaka Sutra alone taught for nine and a half years, for so many years of preaching the sutra without any day off. I have returned to Hong Kong several times, but rarely meet Hong Kong people. That time I brought ten people back to Hong Kong. I realize that Hong Kong people have a deep affinity with Buddha's dharma, so I want to bring out the true meaning of Buddha's dharma to preach. Van Buddha Thanh has a university, secondary school and primary school. If there are any compatriots in Hong Kong who want to come here to study, I wholeheartedly welcome them.

A long time ago, layperson Ta Quan Nhu from Hong Kong went to America to look for Dharma Master Do Luan. When I was in Hong Kong, my dharma name was Do Luan. When I came here, I changed it to Hsuan Hua, but he didn't recognize me. When he saw me in the lecture hall, he asked: "Where is Master Do Luan now?" I replied: "Do Luan passed away." Hearing that, he seemed very sorry. He asked again: "How long has it been since you passed away?" I said: "He passed away a long time ago." Ask: "So what is the magician like to him?" I said: "It can be said that I am his disciple, but also his master, because I teach him English so I am the master, and he teaches me Chinese so I am the disciple." Yesterday this layman came to visit me again, I suddenly remembered this quite interesting story.

We who study Buddha Dharma must have the eyes to choose the Dharma to receive Buddha Dharma correctly. We must have clear knowledge, not be confused in a state of blind practice that wastes time. Studying Buddha Dharma must have an upward direction to do better, not sometimes studying Buddha, sometimes creating karma, and then going down. Aiming upward means studying Buddha Dharma. We must be clearly aware of what is true and false, and not imitate what others say, and then people say whatever we say. Only then can we truly believe in Buddha.

The evening of December 12, 1981

tieu_de: Induction of Buddha Dharma
tom_tat: Wherever I go, I want to guide those who come after me, because among young people there is an enthusiasm that we need to warm up to promote. Luckily, young people often have new, scientific minds, not old-fashioned like the first...
noi_dung:
Induction of Buddha Dharma

Wherever I go, I want to guide those who come after me, because among young people there is an enthusiasm that we need to warm up to promote. Luckily, young people often have fresh, scientific minds, not old-fashioned like our minds. Yesterday, many people had wrong thoughts such as: "We came here to listen to the old magician lecture, but it turns out that we only met a few young magicians and took up all our time. What a waste." Thinking like that is not right. Young masters speak different dharma, so everyone can enjoy different flavors of dharma. Now we invite these monks to teach, please all pay attention and listen to the lecture.

In this City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, there are all kinds of people. There are good people, there are evil people, both good and bad exist. However, when we come here, it's the same with dragons or tigers. Dragons don't always cause rain, tigers don't always cause storms.

On June 19, 1968, the Kim Long bloodshed incident occurred in San Francisco. Later, the Hoa Thanh gang wanted to cause a second or even a third bloodshed, caused by the competition for the operating area of ​​the two gangs Hoa Thanh and To Phuong, but later they all asked for refuge in the Three Jewels, took refuge in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, then they brought all their weapons and dumped them into the sea. From then on, they changed their ways, read the sutras, did meritorious deeds, and did not dare to do bad things anymore.

At that time, there were eight people who asked for refuge, and at that time no one knew their background. While taking refuge, I told them: "Whoever takes refuge with me will not kill, not steal, not burn, not lie." When all eight people heard that, they all broke out in cold sweat, and one of them was carrying a pistol. I asked again: "Who among you is the leader? Raise your hands!” The leader among them immediately raised his hand to acknowledge himself.

About these matters, I do not tell outsiders. Because if I spread this news outside, it would be no different than inviting people in San Francisco to come and thank me. I don't need anyone to be grateful to me, my only wish is that wherever I go, I hope that place will be peaceful and prosperous, and at the same time, I vow to use compassion and not to use force to suppress anyone.

After the Kim Long bloodshed, San Francisco's Chinatown became a dead city for a time, but now its prosperity has been restored to its former state.

December 13, 1981

tieu_de: Four Things Ananda Asked Buddha
tom_tat: The four foundations of mindfulness (or the four areas of mindfulness) are among the thirty-seven teachings supporting the path, including: body, feeling, mind, dharma. When Buddha was about to enter Nirvana, Ananda asked these four questions
noi_dung:
Four Things Ananda Asked Buddha

The four foundations of mindfulness (or the four areas of mindfulness) are among the thirty-seven teachings supporting the path, including: body, feeling, mind, dharma. When Buddha was about to enter Nirvana, Ananda asked Buddha these four things:

For all sutras, what words should be used to begin the sutras?

When Buddha is in this world, Buddha is our teacher. When Buddha enters Nirvana, who do we respect as our teacher?

When Buddha is in this world, we stay with Buddha. When Buddha enters Nirvana, who should we stay with?

When the Buddha was in this world, the bad monks were controlled by the Buddha. When the Buddha entered Nirvana, how can we control them?

Unfortunately, when the Buddha was preparing to enter Nirvana, even though he had attained the first stage of Arhatship, the Venerable Ananda was still crying like a child, struggling with his arms and legs. The Venerable A-na-lau-da recently advised: "Don't cry anymore, crying is useless. You must bring four things to ask Buddha." Ananda asked: "What four things?" Venerable A-na-long-da just revealed the four things mentioned above. Seeing that what he said was correct, Ananda immediately went to Buddha to ask for advice. "World-Honored One! The World-Honored One preached the Dharma for forty-nine years, and gave more than three hundred Dharma conferences, but when it came time to compile the sutras, what word should we use to begin the sutras?" Because pagan scriptures also exist, they begin with the letter "A". (no) or "Pros" (yes). Buddha replied: "For any sutras that I speak, use the words 'This is what I heard'. to begin." Nowadays I see a lot of pagans and scholars arbitrarily taking the words "This is what I heard". to begin their text, these words are everywhere at times. There are even people who do not understand anything and say that the Shurangama Sutra is fake. In fact, if you want Buddha Dharma to flourish, you must first study the Shurangama. Shurangama is to destroy evil and reveal righteousness, because there is nothing more righteous than the Shurangama Sutra. That's why all the devils, ghosts, demons, and leftists have found every way to fight against the Shurangama Sutra. If this sutra no longer exists in the world, then the Buddha Dharma will be destroyed. If no one in the world knows how to recite the Shurangama mantra, demons and demons will appear to harm humanity, causing everyone to turn into demons and demons and their relatives. This is a very important issue. If you know how to reciting the Shurangama mantra, then at least within seven lifetimes you can become a great rich person, for example, that oil king, or the car king, maybe in your previous life you recited the Shurangama mantra, so now you can enjoy such honor and wealth. However, they are still in delusion, only enjoying themselves without knowing how to practice. The fate is that in previous lives they created mixed karma of both good and evil. The good karma was ripe, they enjoyed wealth, the evil karma matured and then they had the sin karma. If karma is not clear, we will go astray, so each of us absolutely cannot ignore the Shurangama Sutra and Mantra.

Buddha entered Nirvana, we must take Paramoksha (Pratimoksha) - that is, precepts - to be our teacher. Precepts are "stop evil, prevent wrongdoing," is "all evil deeds are not done, but good deeds are followed." We must serve the benefit of humanity, contribute our own to society, so people leaving the home life should not wait for others to make offerings for themselves. In America, people leaving the home life should wear robes, because wearing robes is a sign of the spirit of observing the precepts, a symbol of the appearance of a Bhikkhu, not an eccentric intention. In today's world, people take the fake as the truth, take the truth as the fake, right is wrong, wrong is right. Now I would like to tell a true story as an example: During the time of chaos in Mainland China, many students fled to Taiwan. During an urgent situation, most people forget to bring good karma qualifications, and only a few people can bring documents. Their hearts are still young, so they lend their diplomas to others to imitate and make some fake ones. The new diplomas look clean and clear, you pass the exam easily, but the result is that people with genuine diplomas are not accepted because the old diplomas are bad and tattered. It turns out they accepted the real thing as fake.

When Buddhism was newly transmitted from India to China, Chinese monks also wore robes, with full majesty. The cassock at that time was similar to the cassock worn by monks of the Southern school today, meaning it had no hook or loop. However, because of the cold Chinese climate, people have to wear another shirt underneath the robe, so sometimes the outer robe slips off without even feeling it. At that time, monks were very devout, some people maintained the precepts and did not keep money, so if they lost their kashāya, what could they use to replace it? Faced with this situation, everyone gathered to solve the problem. One person suggested using a hook to hold the robe so that the robe would not slip off again. This proposal was immediately applauded and approved by everyone, and from then on, the cassock robes of Chinese monks had hooks. Later, Chinese Bhikkhus often went to the fields to grow crops. Wearing robes and walking around was really troublesome, so they normally did not wear robes, except when they were on the road or over the road. After that, everything went through the roof, even when it came to electricity or traffic, I didn't wear clothes anymore. People say, "Once you get used to it, it becomes a habit," Nowadays, people consider not wearing a robe normal, but wearing a robe is strange.

The monks of the Dharma Realm Buddhist Association still follow the old style, so they wear their robes as often as before. The Bhikkhus and Bhikkhunis criticized us for being eccentric. We don't argue with anyone, you say we're right, we still wear the robe, but you say we're not right, we still wear the robe.

Ananda asked Buddha: "When Buddha is in this world, we are with Buddha. When Buddha enters Nirvana, who should we be with?" Buddha replied: "After I have entered nirvana, all my disciples must reside in the four foundations of mindfulness." The four foundations of mindfulness are four places: body, feeling, mind, dharma.

Contemplate the impurity of the body. If the human body is left unwashed for a long time, it will give off a foul odor. Even though we bathe, the body has nine holes, specializing in excreting unclean things, such as mucus in the eyes, mucus in the nose, phlegm in the mouth, wax in the ears, and things related to urination and defecation, which means our body is extremely unclean. So why do people consider it as a precious thing, wearing jade, gold, silver, and other jewels on their bodies, or applying perfume or scented powder? Is it any different from using floral scents or precious objects to decorate a toilet? You should understand that the body of each of us is a latrine, the intestines are full of excretions related to bowel and urine, is there anything that we have to miss so much? When we are young, the body and its organs still know how to listen to us. When we are old, they all strike, the head is dizzy, the eyes are dizzy, the mouth and tongue are difficult, the limbs are shaking, and hundreds of diseases arise. So is this body still a pity? Therefore, we should clearly realize that this body is impure and not eternal, so as not to go crazy because of it.

Contemplation of feeling is suffering. Tho means feeling. Don't think that enjoying life is a pleasure, in fact there is nothing good about enjoying life, "when you feel pain, suffering will end, if you enjoy blessings, blessings will end." It is better to experience suffering. Once we have enough suffering, then suffering will end. If you are indeed enjoying blessings, then you should regret the blessings but not enjoy the blessings.

Contemplate impermanence. Mind is impermanence, thought and change.

Contemplate the selfless Dharma. Contemplate that all dharmas have no essence, no self-nature, no "self" in it.

If we practice according to the Four Foundations of Mindfulness, our ego-clinging will gradually be destroyed, our Dharma-clinging will not be possible, and we will easily reach enlightenment. Why can't we become enlightened? It's just because I'm still attached, I haven't let go, I see that everything has me there, this big house is mine, that plane, that motorboat, that bank is also mine, from morning to night everything is mine, mine, mine. . . At the moment of death, both hands hang down, there is nothing to carry.

Human life is the ultimate dream

Nhan Tu dreams of the best school

Dream of honor and glory

Dreaming of waking up in the same hometown

Trieu trieu in dreaming

Unconsciously dreaming of royalty

Dream is weak and unconscious

The best dream in vain.

Translated means:

When living, a dream

When you die, dream a dream

In the dream, I saw glory

Waking up from a dream in a poor neighborhood

Soon I'll dream again

Don't know about yellow millet dreams

In a dream I can't wake up,

What a waste of a golden dream.

Therefore, we should not be overly attached, we must quickly practice, study Buddha's teachings, and seek the method of escape from birth and death. There is a saying, "The sea of suffering has no shore, but turning around is a port," Therefore, we should not sink forever in the ocean of suffering, knowing when we will be liberated.

Finally, Ananda asked Buddha: "When the Buddha was in the world, the bad monks were controlled by the Buddha. When the Buddha entered Nirvana, how should we treat them? Will we detain them and punish them?" Buddha replied: "No need! After I entered Nirvana, with the bad Bhikkhus, you used the method of 'indifference'. to convert them. Why is it called wearing? It was silent, there was no further explanation to them. What is tan? This means that people are not allowed to communicate or have any relationship with them. Use "silence" of the masses to neutralize them. Whenever you encounter bad Bhikkhus who do not know the moral principles, take right for wrong and evil for right, or do not distinguish between right and wrong, do not understand the Buddha's teachings correctly, do not communicate with them, do not talk to them, do not pay attention to them, you should consider them as non-existent, so over time they will self-reflect, they will realize that what they have been doing for a long time is not in accordance with the Buddha's teachings, and from there, they will reform and follow the teachings.

When Buddha was in this world, there were also unwholesome Bhikkhus. Now our time is far away from the day Buddha entered Nirvana, so I don't understand whether the number of unwholesome Bhikkhus is large or not. We should not argue with them, because they do not talk about cause and effect, and even oppose cause and effect. We cannot fight with them, we must use patience to deal with them, and if we are patient, we should leave them alone, thus practicing exactly the meaning of Buddha's fourth testament to his disciples.

Previously, I lived in Hong Kong for 12 years (1948-1962), and in 1962 I went to America. I've been in Hong Kong for so long, but I haven't done anything useful. Now that I have returned from America, I vow to establish a dharma relationship with my elders and fellow brothers and sisters in Hong Kong. Therefore, I want to truly dedicate the Buddha Dharma to you wholeheartedly, only then will I feel at ease. Moreover, young people in this era, living today without knowing tomorrow, are very nervous in spirit, so they must worry about standing firmly on their feet, not just being clever, greedy for small conveniences, temporary pleasures and letting their minds drift. Wherever we are, we should be calm and follow the rules, not let loose. We must clearly understand cause and effect, not mistake cause and effect, as the ancients said: "Sow good causes, reap good results; sow bad causes, reap evil results," "If you kill your father, you kill your father; if you kill your brother, you kill your brother." and "plant melons and get melons, plant beans and get beans." It sounds simple, but cause and effect are like that. I hope that our young people should strive to go to school, and in the future, they will pursue happiness and security for society, and not listen to some crazy, confused-minded, and unintentionally adventurous people. Must become a good individual, if there is a good person, the world will be a little more pure. Why hasn't this world been destroyed yet? Because there are good people. Good people are the light, the righteous energy, the life, the source of energy of the world. Because the world is currently in an extremely dangerous position, if we cannot change our crazy behavior, the world will become more and more corrupt, and human thinking will become more and more biased every day. I hope that all of us young people can find the compass of our lives and not follow the trend and wander around to become society's sinners.

During the six days of preaching, if I say anything incorrect, I hope you will forgive me. I also hope that the elders in Hong Kong and the noble monks will give me advice. If what I say is true, please test it. If you think I said it wrong, just pretend you didn't hear anything, because I am an uneducated and unskilled person. The things I said have offended many people. Please forgive me. I also hope that the layperson who invited me to preach the Dharma will be in good health, encounter all good things, all things will be as desired, increase Bodhi, and soon attain Buddhahood. I originally wished that: "For those who come to participate in the Dharma Assembly, their families will be at peace, their relatives will be in harmony, and everything will go smoothly. Those who are not sick will never be sick, and those who are sick will be eliminated after listening to the Dharma." I hope all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas fulfill their vows. I also hope everyone is healthy and soon attain Buddhahood.

In 1968, I was in San Francisco. At that time, there were a number of scientists, geologists, future research experts, etc.

They all predicted that on April 4, 1968, there would be a major earthquake in San Francisco, the land would sink into the sea,

"Strawberry fields turn into blue seas," Residents here will have the opportunity to visit the Dragon King under the sea. Many people have moved to other states. Some of my disciples came and asked me what to do? At that time I told them: "If I'm in San Francisco for just one day, I won't let an earthquake happen here." Therefore, since 1968 until now, there has not been any earthquake. Said there was, but it was just a small earthquake. But I've already left San Francisco, so I don't care anymore, because my prayer is "wherever I go, that place will definitely be safe."

One time, I went to New York. It happened at the right time of heavy snowfall, which forced us to go to Mahayana Pagoda. I then told a disciple the following: 'On the way, I will not allow snow to fall. If it does snow, I will have to punish you by kneeling before Buddha for forty-nine days, not allowed to eat, not allowed to drink, not even allowed to defecate and urinate,' made this disciple extremely scared. Sure enough, on the road we passed, there was no snow falling in a circumference of about three miles, but outside of those three miles it still snowed steadily.

As for me, virtue is not enough to admire people, morality is not enough to educate people, and I am not qualified to be your teacher. But now that you have taken refuge in the Three Jewels, you must definitely make vows to become Buddha. "Whoever has taken refuge with me, if he does not become a Buddha, I will not become a Buddha either." That is my prayer. You are a disciple of the Three Jewels, whoever hits us we must be patient, whoever scolds us we must also be patient with, your master does not dare to do anything but bow his head, everywhere is inferior, and does not take advantage of others. Therefore, as a follower of Buddhism, you should not cause trouble or let your master become a Buddha.

tieu_de: Dharma Master Hang Lai
tom_tat: Buddhism in America is just beginning to flourish, so at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, each of us must think of the responsibility to make Buddha dharma flourish. I specialize in construction materials. One day I drove a car…
noi_dung:
Dharma Master Hang Lai

Buddhism in America is just beginning to flourish, so at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, each of us must think of the responsibility to make Buddha dharma flourish. I specialize in construction materials. One day I drove an old cargo truck more than 160 miles to buy oil. On the way back, the oil tanks were filled up in the car, amounting to more than 150 gallons (600 liters). Carrying oil is very fire-resistant. If it encounters fire, it will burn everything. The mountain road I drive on is very narrow, bumpy and difficult to travel on. Unfortunately at that moment, the battery of the old shopping cart suddenly caught fire, flames shot up all over the oil tanks, and a grenade-like explosion reached my ears. I turned back to look, and it was clear that it was extremely dangerous. If you accidentally touched it too hard, both you and the car would explode. I quickly stopped the car on the side of the road. During the emergency, a park manager saw this and immediately brought me a fire extinguisher, which immediately put out the fire so it did not lead to panic. The incident happened, from start to finish, in no more than 30 seconds. I feel that it is true that Buddha and Bodhisattva protected me to avoid a dangerous accident. Many of these miraculous events were recorded at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, truly an inconceivable mystery!

tieu_de: A magician
tom_tat: Today we went to Hong Kong to shop for things. The bus we were hitchhiking on almost got into a crash. At Van Buddha City, there were many people who had car accidents, but all of them were lucky. Layman Guangzhou…
noi_dung:
A magician

Today we went to Hong Kong to shop for things. The bus we were hitchhiking on almost got into a crash. At Van Buddha City, there were many people who had car accidents, but all of them were lucky. Layman Guozhou (David Rounds) once had a car crash, the car was crushed but he was safe, the reason was because he recited the Shurangama mantra.

Once again, layman Guo Zun was driving in the suburbs and hit a deer. At that time, he thought that the deer must surely die, and the car was damaged. Unexpectedly, the deer was under the car, so it immediately stood up and ran away, but the car was still running fine. The reason is that at that time he recited Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. He is the savior of suffering. At the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, we specialize in worshiping Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, practicing the Dharma of Great Compassion, and the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is also his headquarters. However, Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva does not only save a particular locality, but throughout the dharma world Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva hears the cry and comes to save.

December 14, 1981

tieu_de: White Universe
tom_tat: Ice, snow and earth, countless offerings, floating piles of coins, quiet observation, moving in the middle of the emperor, fighting between dragons and tigers, wandering around, ghosts and magicians, magical illusions, true meaning, no words, no thoughts, moving forward...
noi_dung:
White Universe

Ice sky and snow, countless worms, piles of coins fluttering, tranquil observation, Dong Zhongshei Emperor, dragon fighting tiger fighting often traveling, ghostly and magical magic, true meaning, no words, no thoughts, Duong Tien Xu, Dai Tieu Minh, internal and external concubine, Vi Tran Nhat, Dharma Realm Pearl, Gathering Luan Fish into harmony, each other is unhindered, two fists smashing the void, one mouth swallows the sea of origin, great compassion is universal, flowing with blood, unrelenting breath.

Today I want to lecture you on Cosmic Bach. Why is it called the White Universe? "Vu" symbolizes the four directions and the two directions, upper and lower. "Pillar" covering from ancient times to present, the universe combined is the world, called by another name. This song is along with the song "Man Giang Hong" of Nhac Phi are also similar to each other. In the past, Yue Fei fought with the Jin army, blood stained the Yangtze River, so he wrote the song "Man Jiang Hong," still passed down to this day. As for the song "White Universe" made at Kim Son Pagoda in San Francisco. This white universe is not just white rivers and white rivers, but the entire universe is white. Why do you say the universe is white? Unfortunately, Golden Mountain Holy Temple is like a large, icy box of snow. On a small scale, the whole temple is a cold building, but on a large scale, it can be said that the whole world turns white, without any black, and from there comes the topic of this article.

In 1972, Kim Son Pagoda held its first Dharma assembly, reciting the Six Dai Minh Mantra. Pháp hội kéo dài liền bảy ngày đêm, có chừng hơn sáu mươi người tham gia, ngày đêm 24 giờ thay nhau niệm sáu chữ "Án ma ni bát di hồng." What is the purpose? Pray for world peace, reduce or eliminate accidents in the world. Luckily, at that time, rumors spread that San Francisco would be hit by a major earthquake, so everyone very sincerely recited the Luc Dai Minh Mantra, praying that no accident would occur. So they continuously chanted it day and night, determined to fight with the pagan demons without hesitation. Everyone was extremely diligent. Even though I didn't participate, I was just behind and urging everyone on, but I felt extremely satisfied. Everyone practices seriously, tirelessly, and their spirit is excited, which makes me extremely satisfied. For me, the happiest thing is that everyone practices and what makes me most dissatisfied is that my disciples, especially those leaving the home life, do not put in the effort, just to cover their eyes with lies. This is what I despise most, what I will never forgive.

Therefore, when the seven-day Dharma Assembly was completed, I wrote the article "White Universe". As a souvenir, I would like to bring it up for you to listen to. Good or bad, I don't care, I don't know, I just know that I wrote it, that's all. The first sentence is:

Ice Heaven and Snow Earth - Ice Heaven and Snow Earth: Although Kim Son Thanh Tu is not famous in the world, everyone in America knows it. Golden Mountain Holy Temple is a snow tower, snowy ground and icy sky, cold and icy; Not only is the temple cold, people are also cold. Everyone who comes to the temple complains: "-! The people at Kim Son Pagoda are so cold, I don't feel anything warm at all." Therefore, everyone who comes to Kim Son Thanh Tu is disappointed, and there is truly nothing for people to hope for, because everything here is cold and icy. Insects also die from cold. That's why we use the word "ice". i.e. cold. "Snow Land," Because snow represents the coldest.

Countless sacrifices are piled up - countless small insects die in the cold: It is unknown how many small insects die from the cold. Small insects include bacteria in our bodies. They live on vitamins A, B, C, but in this place, not only do people not have vitamins A, B, C, but they also have to work hard in the cold air. Why not freeze them to death? However, they are not destroyed, so there is a saying: "Let go of sleep," Just hid and slept. In the cold winter, insects temporarily hide and lie still underground, sleeping in the winter called dormancy.

Quiet observation - in quiet observation: Chính trong thời gian mà mọi thứ đều lặng lẽ, đầu óc cũng tĩnh lặng, không có thất tình lục dục quấy động, chỉ nhất tâm chuyên chú niệm Án-ma-ni bát di hồng, Án-ma-ni bát di hồng... If you let go of your thoughts, in an instant, you will awaken, observe, observe.

Intermediate Verdict - In the cave, consider carefully: When reciting mantras, there are times when you chant, and times when you sit and recite. While meditating continuously, when encountering movement, the mind clearly and carefully evaluates the meaning of Buddha's teachings. The realm at that time will appear. -! The dragon has arrived, the tiger has also arrived!

Dragons fighting tigers often travel for fun - dragons fighting tigers often have fun: Dragons fly in the clouds, tigers move through forests and mountains. It's really fun to go to these places and have fun. Realms like that that appear before our eyes can make us dizzy, that's why we say "dragon fighting tiger fighting often du du." This is the realm that appears in silence.

The magic of ghosts and magical magic - The magic of ghosts crying and screaming of virtual magic: There is a ghost crying there, crying: "A! I died so unjustly! Quickly chant Buddha for me! deliverance, deliverance give me! Please have mercy! Don't get angry with me!" Demons cry like that. "Divine pride," That is, there the god also screamed and shouted: "Let it go, it's guilty of a lot!" Oh! Look at that! Both sides fight like this, knowing which side is right and which side is wrong, making us confused. However, ghosts cry, gods scream, such strange things are just illusions, falsehoods, not real, so it is said "illusionary period." So, what is real?

The true meaning of the uttermost words - the true meaning of all words: There is nothing that can be said about the true meaning. Like the sentence: "Originally there is nothing, what is there to cling to the dust of the world?" This is the true meaning, so it is said "absolutely."

Unthinking - without thinking: It can't be imagined, the mind can't think of it, words can't talk about it.

Moving forward - must step forward: However, you still have to move forward courageously to practice diligently. You can't stop walking, you get lost in the "good" place. I said that I don't have anything, so I don't have to think about it anymore, and that's it! If you're sleepy, just sleep, if you're hungry, just eat, and then when you die, it's gone! alas! That is a mistake, letting the days pass in vain. We still have to move forward, courageously.

Great and small indifference - large and small, destroyed: Big and small, everything is destroyed, nothing remains.

Internal and external non-internal and external are not: Neither inside nor outside, nor in between, that is the true meaning.

The complete Dharma Realm: Let's try, the dharma realm is so huge, but there is nothing that does not represent reality. The Dharma Realm Chau means the complete Dharma Realm.

Kho Luan fish pellets dung-the raw dung pellets: Hot Wheel is pure, the pure essence is not lacking anywhere; Perfect content is complete content without hindrances, complete without damage or ugliness.

Mutuality without hindrance - both sides without hindrance: are not obstacles to each other, the true meaning is that they are one, also immeasurable, immeasurable is one, one is immeasurable, one and plural, both sides are not obstacles to each other.

Two fists destroy the void, two fists destroy the blanket of the void: Use two fists to punch through the blanket of emptiness. Do you think space also has a veil? Even though space does not cover it, let's destroy it so that space is shattered and even space is no longer there. If emptiness no longer exists, then where would there be a veil? Why do you still say that you use two fists to break through the blanket of void? This is also the meaning in the above sentence: "Originally there is nothing, nothing clings to the dust of the world."

One mouthful swallows the sea of origin - One gulp swallows the sea: Open your mouth and swallow all the worlds as many as there are motes in the sea of death, this world, that world, this country, that country, countless countries. So have you turned into a monster? If a monster could do that, it would be great, I'm afraid I won't be able to do it. The meaning of this sentence is to say the ability to let go of anything, complete liberation, no longer hindering anything, swallowing the whole world, that's why it is said "two fists destroy the void, one mouth completely destroys the ocean."

Great universal compassion - great and universal compassion: Giving joy is kindness, removing suffering for others is compassion. Arousing compassion unconditionally, applying compassion in the spirit of oneness - the spirit of self and others is one body (hanh ungainly is the part of love, the body is the part of compassion), that's why we say "great compassion." Now use that great compassion to save all sentient beings, not just one individual, nor just those who have a predestined relationship with us. For those who are ungrateful, dark and stubborn, also show compassion, use all methods of education, bring utmost sincerity, use the spirit of unity and compassion to save, give love generously, do not stop until you can save, then say: "Great universal compassion."

Blood circulation - bleeding, sweating: Dedicate all your heart and soul to teaching and transforming sentient beings.

Non-retirement means no rest: That means day and night, dedicated to exhaustion, never resting. Don't be afraid of suffering, don't be afraid of difficulties, just know how to step forward, don't know how to retreat.

Above are the comments on the teachings of Universe Bach.

February 7, 1982 at Kim Luan Thanh Temple, Los Angeles

tieu_de: If you lose your body, you won't be able to get it back for thousands of lifetimes
tom_tat: Today we will talk about the meaning of repentance in Buddhism. All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas do not look at the mistakes of sentient beings. If sentient beings have errors and ignore them, Buddha also does not pay attention. But I have created my own karma...
noi_dung:
If you lose your body, you won't be able to get it back for thousands of lifetimes

Today we will talk about the meaning of repentance in Buddhism. All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas do not look at the mistakes of sentient beings. If sentient beings have errors and ignore them, Buddha also does not pay attention. But if you yourself have created the karma of sin, when the karma is ripe, you will receive the full retribution. Enlightened beings are few but confused are many; There is little wisdom, there is much ignorance. Therefore, sentient beings who are wise and keep rules will not do crazy things. True enlightenment sentient beings also do not have wrong knowledge and wrong views, meaning wrong understanding and perception. In the vast sea of suffering, not knowing where the shore is, sentient beings are born and die, die and are born again, circling around in the six paths, just like today talking about chemical factories: A large spiritual nature can be divided into small spiritual natures and vice versa, small spiritual natures can combine to become large spiritual natures.

For the above reason, when an individual is reincarnated as an animal, he is not only a type of animal but can also be divided into horses, buffaloes, goats, chickens, dogs, pigs, animals that are relatively small in size, and their spiritual nature also has some intelligence. An individual can transform into seven types of animals. During the process of physical separation, there will be the phenomenon of "spirit separation," Once the spirit is divided, the spiritual nature becomes less and less, the more it is divided, the more it is reduced. For example, a horse reincarnated into a chicken and duck, then became even smaller. A horse can turn into seven ducks and seven chickens, etc. The less spiritual nature becomes, the more stupid it becomes, and it will not be easy to recover for hundreds of thousands of eons. For what reason? Because there is a separation, as in the analysis done in a chemical laboratory, there is a separation of each part, each component. An individual is reincarnated as a mosquito because his mind is too cruel, his greed is bottomless, he only wants to suck the blood of others. That thought still exists, so it turns into a mosquito, specializing in sucking blood. Even though the spiritual nature has been transformed, there is still a little bit left. Only then will they know how to follow people and suck blood, but other than that, they don't know anything else. Mosquitoes act out of greed, using that to maintain their lives, that is the fate of mosquitoes.

What about claw ants? This type is naturally greedy for food. If an individual transforms into an ant, it must turn into eighty-four thousand children. You have seen mosquitoes, flocks and flocks like that. The more glass, each drive, each drive, the more crowded it is. According to the principle of "nature turns into spirit and dies," Therefore, the status of ants is very small and their strength is not much.

Speaking of honey bees, they are very good at stealing, their crimes of stealing are many, the reason is because in their previous lives they were at fault for not observing the precepts prohibiting theft. As for mosquitoes and ants, their previous lives were the same, not maintaining the precepts of robbery. However, bees are heavier, so they are very good at stealing honey. If people's honey is left unattended, there are no worker bees or honey bees there to guard it, then flock after flock of honey bees will come to suck the honey until it runs out. Bees like sweets, so bees take honey, build nests, and store honey in their banks. The beehive is the bee's bank.

Because bees only know that bees live on honey and sugar, they have to build nests to store honey, just like people have to save money. However, they just kept hoarding honey, hoarding it a lot, and eventually the honey was taken away. For what reason? Because they violate the precepts of theft, if what they take in is not good, then what goes out will be the same. If they don't take it back with great clarity and greatness, it will eventually be lost.

Taking examples of these three types of tiny animals to study, i.e. mosquitoes, bees and ants, we can clearly see that we should not violate the precepts against killing, stealing, adultery, and lying. The same is true for the prohibition of drinking alcohol. Unfortunately, drinking alcohol often causes confused actions. What is the map like? There was originally a person who had received the five precepts, and he observed the precepts very carefully, but one day he had the urge to drink alcohol. He told himself: "Among the five precepts, killing, stealing, adultery, and lying are all important, but the precept about alcohol is too common, so why observe these precepts? This precept is redundant. Stop! From now on, don't observe the precepts about drinking alcohol anymore. Let's go drink some wine." Having said that, he went to buy a bottle of wine and poured it out to drink alone. He felt that drinking like that without something to drink would be tasteless, so he went out to find something to make alcohol. At that moment, he saw a neighbor's chicken running past, and he had the following thought: "This is probably Bodhisattva helping me with this snack!"

You see! His thoughts are indeed nonsense, wrong knowledge and wrong views! He caught that chicken and killed it to eat, which means he broke the precepts of killing and stealing. After that, the neighbor who was looking for chickens passed by. He was drunk and answered in a haphazard manner: "I don't see any chickens!" So he broke the precept against lying. He saw that this woman was quite beautiful, so he committed the crime of rape.

Please pay attention! The reason is just because he drank a little alcohol that he broke all five precepts like that. Look at the retarded children, they all have just been reincarnated as humans from the animal world, so they have no wisdom. Although a small spiritual nature transformed into a large spiritual nature, restoring human life, but because of being in the animal realm for too long, wisdom was obscured, so in this life not only did not know how to speak, nor listen, let alone keep the rules.

For these reasons, it is essential for everyone to clearly understand the Five Precepts. Each world has five good gods supporting it. If you don't observe the precepts, the gods will leave, making room for five evil spirits. If you violate the precepts, evil spirits will come. If you do not violate the precepts, evil spirits will not come. Why don't ghosts come? Because there are good angels protecting us, we should especially observe the precepts carefully. Not observing the precepts means not practicing, knowing how to observe the precepts means being able to follow the teachings, which means we can have true wisdom, never go crazy, never eat salty food and break the precepts. Therefore, cultivators must be able to overcome themselves in every hour and moment, skillfully control their body, and base their efforts on the six senses. For example, when the eyes face a form, the physical object is changed - that is, it is shaken, the ear hears the sound is changed, the tongue tastes the taste is changed, the nose smells the scent is changed, the body is touched, the mind is turned, the mind is turned by the dharma - which means being dragged away by the six enemies at the six doors, causing the spiritual energy inside us to be robbed. If you are not transferred, your spiritual nature is not lost, that is said to be wisdom.

The verse says:

May the three hindrances eliminate afflictions

Pray to attain true wisdom

Universal vows that all sins and obstacles will be eliminated

In this world, we often practice the Bodhisattva path.

The three hindrances are karma hindrance, retribution hindrance, affliction hindrance. Karma obstacles include good and evil karma that we have created in previous lives, now appearing as obstacles that we encounter in this life; Unsatisfactory events that come to us all arise from those types of karma obstacles. Retributions are types of suffering including hell, hungry ghosts, and animal birth. There is a sentence: "Suppose that in hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, the karma caused is not lost, but when the causes and conditions meet, they will receive full retribution," No matter what karma we create, we will receive retribution for that karma. There is no way to escape that karma. So there is a saying: "You can't carry anything, only karma can take care of yourself." In the previous life we did wrong cause and effect, in this life we receive the result, that is called karma. The afflictions include lust, anger (anger) and ignorance. Each individual has their own afflictions, some have little, some have much. If there is no affliction, that is, there is no greed, anger or ignorance, then one is worthy of being a saint. If ignorance has not been completely eliminated, the root of affliction still exists. It will arise at any time and depending on circumstances. At that time, people will forget everything, causing people to do immoral and immoral things that go against their conscience. Afflictions that are not eliminated will hinder the Bodhisattva root, hence the saying: "The rolling fire burned down the Bodhi forest," No matter how much you practice, if afflictions are not eliminated, everything is temporary. Therefore, at the door of the six senses, we must not let the external environment change, but we ourselves must transform the external environment, we must turn afflictions into Bodhi, and birth and death into Nirvana. We must be aware of the "stinky leather bag" Behold, the physical body combined with the spiritual mind means that the marriage will last forever; But, at the last minute, it will leave me and separate from me. I also don't know where I will go. What is religious practice for? Precisely to prepare for the time when our physical bodies are about to separate, we know where we will go, without being controlled by this foul skin bag, we can go home in freedom. Because of that, we practice religion. If we want to achieve the path of karma, we must collect our body and mind regularly, step by step according to the rules and regulations, and not let the external environment at the doors of the six senses entice us. At that time, you already have concentration. Having concentration means being able to develop wisdom. However, you must remember that concentration is born from the power of precepts, and precepts are "the evil ones act, the good ones serve them," Sacrificing the small self and completing the merit of cultivating the spirit of the big self, that is the true Buddha Dharma, my guiding principle. Please try to study with me.

tieu_de: Duties of a Buddhist Follower
tom_tat: We are not lucky, being born in the Dharma Ending Age, far away from the Buddha's time. Now leaving the home life, if we only wear Buddha's clothes, eat at Buddha's door, use Buddha as a guise, sing along to Buddha's tune, collect disciples, accept making offerings,...
noi_dung:
Duties of a Buddhist Follower

We are not lucky, being born in the Dharma Ending Age, far away from the Buddha's time. Now leaving the home life, if we only take the Buddha's clothes, eat at Buddha's door, use Buddha as a guise, sing along with Buddha's tune, collect disciples, receive making offerings, and then present under any leaving the home life goods, lay people, promote their reputation as Buddha's disciples, in fact, those are just people who are greedy for fame and profit, let Buddha's religion fall, ruin Buddha's religion, are sinners of Buddha's religion!

Why did Buddha's teachings decline? Because we do not practice, do not seriously keep the precepts, do not sincerely practice to purify our body and mind. Dharma is inherently a formless, formless, impossible thing. It is all due to human behavior that all things good, evil, ugly, and beautiful are manifested. If the minds of sentient beings are directed towards goodness, if everyone keeps the five precepts and practices the ten virtues, the face of the world will become gentle and lush, that is the true Dharma. As for the minds of sentient beings oriented towards evil, a whole atmosphere of greed, anger and ignorance will pollute the void, causing the Dharma to be trapped in darkness. Then there is no Dharma left to talk about. The nature of the dharma has no beginning or end. It is only because of the right and wrong behavior of humans that it is said that there is a beginning and an end. Can this situation be saved with just a shameful mind? The risk must be corrected. Regardless of whether we are leaving the home life or lay, if we are disciples of Buddha, we must set an example for ourselves, refuse to stay behind everyone, and try our best to save Buddha's teachings. We must all work together to make Buddha's teachings shine and flourish, to awaken the world so that humanity can understand Buddha's teachings, believe in Buddha's teachings and revere Buddha's teachings.

Dear believers! In the past, the Buddha was revered by both humans and heaven for making offerings. Seeing this, we should feel ashamed of ourselves. Nowadays, there are some, including lay people, who do not regard monks at all, they consider people leaving the home life as "gods and ghosts." That is also a phenomenon of today. Even some people in society who are relatively knowledgeable, let alone intellectuals and scholars, look down even more on people leaving the home life. They realized that the monks did not firmly grasp the Buddha's teachings, did not have true wisdom, and spoke idle and deceitful words. Now we use that to be alert, make great vows, establish firm will, wholeheartedly study the teachings, strictly keep precepts, strive to practice, and transform the time of the end of Dharma into the time of correct Dharma. As long as we take steady steps on the path of practice and practice, then there is no need to worry that we will not achieve results! Having attained the results, we can erect Dharma flags everywhere, blow Dharma whistles, beat Dharma drums, and then be able to propagate Buddha teachings even in places where Dharma does not exist, enough to make people believe in Buddha. Therefore, we must be diligent and determined to practice precepts, concentration, wisdom, and extinguish greed, anger, and ignorance, and realizing Buddha is the goal of all of us.

What is the result of experiencing? A person who has attained enlightenment does not have greed, anger, or ignorance. The three poisons of greed, anger and ignorance are all destroyed. At any time, no matter what adversity, whether they are slandered, or gloriously praised, they still maintain a peaceful and at ease look, as if they are not pulled by external conditions, their attitude is as it is, innocently living in the purity of morality. For them, all precepts no longer seem forced, because their actions were once in harmony with the pure world. People who have attained true concentration have true concentration, so vain fame and profit do not attract them, even if others beat and scold them, it will not make their mind agitated and produce unwholesome words. Don't expect to hear their cruel voices, because the three evil snakes (greed, anger, ignorance) are no longer there. People who have proven to have true wisdom, they understand everything they hear, whatever problem comes to them, they solve it head-on. Whoever comes to them, immediately looks at them and knows their true nature. Even if you want to deceive them, you will not be able to reach their intelligent eyes. A person who has achieved enlightenment and attained fruition can be compared to the morning sun in the pure sky, can be compared to the clear moon floating in the vast cloudless sky, like the water in a spring lake, like blue lotus flowers in the morning dew. In their hearts, in the corners of their eyes, in their words, they never contain anything evil, evil deeds, or evil words; Just by meeting them, being close to them, without needing to speak, good people become saints, evil people become good people. People who have attained enlightenment, they have the power to attract such inspiration, but they are no different from us in our daily activities.

We are called disciples of Buddha, we cannot shirk our responsibility but must take responsibility to revive the Dharma. Don't use the excuse that the Dharma is ending and refuse to practice! So why do we follow Buddhism? Are you going to cut off your love and leave your family again? Isn't that self-deception? Do you look down on yourself? This is truly a confusion, a madness, a corrupt class in Buddhism, a sinner! I used to make vows like this: Wherever I go, the Dharma must exist there, not the end of Dharma. Although Buddha at that time lamented that in the future there will be an end of dharma, but the reason is that the end of dharma is created by the creator, so of course it is possible to use human strength to transform the end of dharma into true dharma. If indeed, every disciple of the Buddha, leaving the home life, follows the teachings, diligently practices the Dharma methods, lives within the precepts that the Buddha created, practices according to the Buddha's scriptures, clearly understands the meaning of the Buddha's teachings, practices the words that the Patriarchs have promoted, and consistently follows the three canons of Sutras, Vinaya, and Treatises as instructed, then where can the end of the Dharma come from? What's the point of not being able to achieve enlightenment? Suppose we don't follow the things just mentioned, go against the religion, for example, are lazy, follow whatever we do, are greedy for fame and profit, build a big pagoda for enjoyment, it would be strange if it doesn't turn into an end of dharma.

We dare to give up our lives to seek the unsurpassed path, to sacrifice our lives to brighten Buddha's teachings and improve Buddha's teachings. Buddhism has gone through many eras of trends, it is difficult to avoid the situation of not adapting to living beings in a certain place, so we must skillfully use means to imitate and improve, each Buddha disciple must actively embark on it, especially for those leaving the home life must clearly understand and cannot be underestimated.

Having said this, I think that there will definitely be people who question why anyone who is not greedy, angry or ignorant is the one who has achieved the results. Now mentioning the importance of greed, anger and ignorance, let me take some very common but easy to understand images and tell them to you. That greedy mind is lustful thoughts, a lustful mind. Not having greed in mind means being free from thoughts of desire; There is no lustful thoughts, which means there is no lustful mind anymore. Men and women meet each other and come into contact with each other. At that time, false thoughts will not arise. Not only will thoughts of desire not arise, physiological reactions will no longer arise, the identities of men and women will not fluctuate. Only then can thoughts of desire be truly stopped, and greed will no longer exist.

Don't be surprised to see me say it all so blatantly, because thousands of volumes of scriptures, three collections of twelve scriptures, in the end, they only talk about this issue. If there were no problem of "sex," then any sutras are not necessary, all dharmas are "empty," all dharmas are "like." Because of that problem, we have to practice. If you cannot give up craving and abandon desire, then even if you leave the home life and practice for eighty thousand great eons, it will be a waste of your efforts, wasting your days and days, staying in a religious place to eat at the temple and create karma. If you stop craving and eliminate lust, then you will truly end your greed. Without greed, there will be no afflictions. So when can we get rid of greed? Of course, ignorance must be destroyed to eliminate greed. The reason why Bodhisattvas practice courageously and diligently is to destroy part of their ignorance, attain part of their Dharma body, and only then can they destroy all ignorance to attain Buddhahood. Greed is one of the three poisons that is very difficult to eliminate. When we first develop the mind to practice, the thing that hinders our efforts is the mind of lust, men lust after women, women lust after men, a fundamental problem. The Shurangama Sutra says very clearly: "The lustful mind is not eliminated, no one who is exposed to it can escape," If you don't want to get rid of the lustful mind but still hope to attain Buddhahood, it's no different than boiling sand to make food, something that can't happen.

Now I talk about anger again. Anger is also affliction, not having anger does not mean there is no affliction, but with practice, we can transform afflictions into Bodhi mind, use the fire of ignorance to turn it into wisdom water, use wisdom water to water the seedlings.

Bodhi, then in the future there will be a Buddha who attains Bodhi. If the fire of ignorance cannot be destroyed, the water of wisdom will not be born, and Bodhi cannot be achieved. Gentlemen! I hope everyone will pay special attention to listen and remember in their field of alaya consciousness to use at any time. At the same time, you also go back and review the years of studying Buddha Dharma, listening to sutras, bowing to the Buddha, chanting mantras, meditating, and being diligent every day, so why haven't you achieved the practice of ending desire? If you have not yet achieved it, you must urgently practice the precepts of concentration and wisdom. If you have reached the level of cessation of desire, you still have to practice precepts, concentration and wisdom. Have you heard the Avatamsaka Sutra, in each chapter there is mention of Bodhisattvas in the void throughout the Dharma world who specialize in practicing the Bodhisattva path, without forgetting to practice the precepts of concentration and wisdom, these three trainings of no-outflows. Bodhisattvas, not sparing their own lives, go everywhere to teach and transform living beings. They do not get tired, do not rest, and do not turn back. We have only left the home life for a few days, and we are already thinking about enjoying ourselves. It is truly a pitiful thing, a madness, the seed of the end of dharma. All Buddhist disciples must take the rise and fall of Buddhism as their responsibility, especially monastics who must take on great tasks. Everyone thinks like that, so why worry that Buddha Dharma won't be widely spread? It's just that because one person pushes the other person, then on his own, he closes the door to expand and develop his own power, all the rise and fall of Buddhism is put aside, he speaks irresponsibly, you look up to me, I look up to you. This is a common situation where no one cares, you look at me, I look at you, or, it's not my business, just throw it out and someone will worry. Everyone thinks about stepping back, causing Buddhism to be immersed in an atmosphere of death. How come Buddhism is not at its end? In fact, the reason is that everyone is selfish and full of self-interest. If you don't practice, you don't seek Buddha's teachings above, you don't seek Buddha's teachings below, you don't save sentient beings, you don't put in the effort to do Buddha's work, but you're also lazy and withdrawn, which will cause Buddha's teachings to reach the end of time and perish. Dear believers! We know the story clearly, so I hope that all of us will wholeheartedly protect and protect Buddha's cause. To save ourselves, we must be brave and diligent in studying Buddha's teachings. We all work together to make Buddhism flourish and grow stronger and brighter every day, making the Dharma remain forever in the world, as radiant as when Buddha was still in the world.

When it comes to practice, I realize that for monastics, the first point is not to hang around in places of power and wealth. The second point is that you should not always look outward to create karma. Third, you should not pray for fate from people in all events. At Kim Son Thanh Tu there is a parallel sentence as follows:

The group of children has no fate,

The hungry death does not transform into fate,

With death and no fate.

Depending on the immutable fate,

Immutable depending on fate.

Translation:

Die cold and have no fate,

Starving to death without becoming fateful,

Die poor without praying for fate.

Fate does not change,

Doesn't change depending on fate.

Those are our three principles, and I hope all monastic disciples also agree with them, and encourage each other to follow them properly. Furthermore, we make three great vows together:

Giving up one's life for Buddha's sake-Because of Buddha's self-forgetfulness: As Buddhists and monastics, we cannot stand idly by and watch Buddhism degenerate and let people despise us. It is better to give this life to spread the light of Buddhism, use the Dharma to save the world in this cruel time, allowing all sentient beings to live in peace and happiness.

Create a network for your duty-Creating a network is a duty: We are inherently ordinary people, but we can transform our ordinary roots to become saints. The ancients said: "A gentleman has the ability to learn how to create a life. The network is created by oneself, blessings are sought by oneself, misfortunes and blessings have no door, only those who invite them to take them," Those are Lao-tzu's words. If we find that sentence reasonable, we can take it for reference. If what is said is not ethical, we do not accept the person who said it.

Right Livelihood is Enlightenment. Master Thai-Hu said: "Right livelihood is the job of monks;" called right livelihood, is not talking about life, as when people shed blood to sacrifice, but the meaning here is reform. Traditionally, the pine forests still leave behind all the clear turtles. Of course we must preserve what is good, but there are also rules that are out of date, or no longer suitable for today's world, so we can boldly modify them depending on actual needs. Dharma is a hard death, people are alive, so why do we have to defend ourselves to prevent it from changing? If we see something wrong in the past, whatever needs to be eliminated, we must abandon it. Any argument that is inaccurate, we must correct. In short, everything related to the prosperity of Buddhism must be done and cannot be careless or hesitant.

That means clarity,

Understanding reason means truth.

It means that when you encounter a situation, you understand the reason. If you understand the reason, then implement that reason. Take that as a principle

The bloodline inheritance of the Patriarchs.

Everyone should practically start working, there should only be two parts of words and three parts of concrete actions. If you can believe in yourself, others will definitely imitate you. If the person leaving the home life does all his duty like that, Buddhism will then revive, and the end of the dharma will turn to the true dharma. I want to confirm that: "Golden Mountain Holy Temple has one day left, then there is also one day where the Dharma is with the world." Nowadays, when Buddhism has just arrived in Western countries, it is necessary to have the Dharma and to have saints, so we must quickly create conditions for the attainment of saints. All disciples of the Buddha should not just lay down or leave the home life, they should all establish their will to practice and become saints.

When I first came to America, I had great wishes: I wonder why I came to the West? I want to come here to be a statue maker, I want to shape a living Buddha, a living Bodhisattva, a living Patriarch. In the past I couldn't accomplish anything, now I want to do charity work and save people. I also want to turn all living beings in this world into living Buddhas, living Bodhisattvas, and living Patriarchs. Some people say I can't do it, that making such a wish is too extravagant, I think I can definitely do it. If I cannot transform all sentient beings in this world into living Buddhas, living Bodhisattvas, and living Patriarchs, I vow to never become a Buddha. Right now I am actively doing that work. Whether you believe it or not, that's still my goal. Don't you see that I have converted quite a few Western young men and women into Buddha's door? It's difficult for young American men and women, don't you see they've shaved their beards and cut their hair leaving the home life? This is just the first step, nothing strange. Then all living beings followed each other to Buddha, into Buddha's house.

I think there must be some skeptics: Without afflictions, can one become a saint? That's right. But, afflictions are not easy to eliminate, so Bodhisattva Samantabhadra once said: ". . . Even if my sorrows cannot end, my great vows will also not end." However, we can make vows: "Endless afflictions vow to cease," sentient beings are endless, emptiness is endless, afflictions are endless, but our vows can also be endless. The purpose of our practice is to seek omniscience, omniscience, like the mystical wisdom of the Buddha, using prajna wisdom to destroy ignorance, the three poisons, transform afflictions into Bodhi, into great wisdom, at that time we truly have no afflictions anymore and become saints.

What exactly is the fire of ignorance? To put it very simply, very neatly, it is the lustful mind of male and female desire. Once that kind of thought starts, no one can speak it well, there is no method to control it. So how many people are caught in confusion, creating confused things, it can be said that one mistake, it becomes eternal hatred, there is no way to save. When two men and women are in love, if anyone asks them, why do they love him? Why do they love her? Surely they will respond: "don't know why." That's because of ignorance. I hope that all of you leaving the home life can stop craving, eliminate lust, and practice diligently, please try your best!

tieu_de: Hung Khoi Van Buddha Holy City
tom_tat: Dear believers! The Bodhisattva diligently practices, is not lazy day or night, accumulates the merit of the three pure karmas, dignifies his body and mind, so he is always diligent and not tired, may all sentient beings diligently practice the three karmas,...
noi_dung:
Hung Khoi Van Buddha Holy City

Dear believers! The Bodhisattva diligently practices, is not lazy day or night, accumulates the merit of the three pure karmas, adorns the body and mind, so he is always diligent and not tired, praying that sentient beings diligently cultivate the three karmas, purify the body, speech, and mind, only then will they have the merit of pure good roots, and their bodies will be adorned and perfect. We, who study Buddha and cultivate the path, cannot be careless at any moment, especially we must pay special attention to the three karmas to seek improvement, and from there gradually accumulate good merits, plant great good roots regardless of the time of life. If we are diligent like that, naturally the karma will be achieved, and the dignified appearance will also be perfect. Talking about generals: Although it is due to cultivation, if we are born with an ugly appearance, whoever sees it will not be happy and try to stay away, then it will be difficult for us to teach and transform sentient beings. When Patriarch Dharma came to China, the Chinese saw the Patriarch's face full of whiskers, big eyes, thick eyebrows, and scary appearance. Therefore, Bodhisattva had to face the wall for more than ten years, only being able to teach a very few sentient beings. Luckily, one of them was the Second Patriarch Than Quang, who came to seek the Dharma, knelt for nine years, and then cut off an arm. Only then was Bodhisattva transmitted from his heart, from then on, the meditation sect was born, which has been passed down to this day. Now I have come to the West to propagate the Dharma, guide you to practice and study Buddha Dharma, and instruct you to practice good merit blessings, to dignify your own body.

What is cultivating merit and blessings? Where to go to practice? That's right, practicing and doing religious work also requires a safe place to live. This opportunity is also due to the karma that has matured, so we are now staying at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. Here, tens of thousands of Buddhas are needed to adorn this city. Saying ten thousand Buddhas, does not mean that one has already achieved ten thousand Buddhas, but by becoming ten thousand Buddhas, one has developed the Bodhi mind, is currently developing the Bodhi mind, is generating the Bodhi mind of Buddha's disciples.

City of Ten Thousand Buddhas,

City of Ten Thousand Buddhas,

Ten thousand Buddhas all come true!

The project at Kim Son Thanh Tu in recent years has been to pan for sand to find gold. Fortunately, many golden Buddhas have been filtered out. All the seven people who came to Golden Mountain Holy Temple did not lose heart, because they were part of the Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. Therefore, we must cherish those predestined conditions and work together, making vast vows:

May the Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas be our community of life; In order for our lives to be maintained, the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must be a safe place, without danger, so that our lives can have enough vitality and development.

May we consider the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas as our head, so we must protect our heads so that the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas will forever lead sentient beings under the Buddha's halo, and sentient beings will enjoy peace in life.

May the Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas be our eyes, and as our eyes are preserved, they will be able to observe all the causes and conditions of sentient beings thoroughly, forever not being separated from sentient beings. All of us, please wholeheartedly adhere to the vows to develop the Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, and definitely achieve the vow of Ten Thousand Buddhas to adorn this city, taking the prosperity of the entire City as our own responsibility and vocation. Hope everyone does not take responsibility lightly and neglect their duties.

Things in the world always follow the trend of ups and downs. When one thing goes up, the other goes down. There is nothing that is eternally up or down. Currently, Buddhism in Asia is in decline, while Buddhism in America is on the rise. The history of a people or a country is the same.
