Today I teach this koan to demonstrate that seeking the Dharma is not an easy thing. One must have the heart to dare to let go of this body in order to find the right path.

Patriarch Bodhidharma arrived in Guangzhou, then went overland (People from India took a boat to China). When visiting Kim Lang (Nan Kinh), the Patriarch passed by the place of Dharma Master Than Quang, while the Dharma Master was lecturing the sutras.

The team came out and asked: "What are you doing here?"

Than Quang replied: "I'm preaching the sutra."

The team asked: "What's the point of preaching the sutras?"

Answer: "To escape birth and death."

Team said: "Dharma cannot be said, there is no dharma to say. What you preach is that black is the word, white is the paper, so how can we escape birth and death?"

After hearing this, Than Quang was very angry and said: "This Demon King! You dare to come here to blaspheme the Buddha, blaspheme the Dharma, and slander the Sangha. Is there any reason?"

Having finished speaking, the Master picked up the iron beads and threw them hard at the Patriarch's face. Bodhidharma did not have time to take precautions and was hit by a rosary, breaking his two front teeth. The team has the idea that: "If I pull my teeth into the ground, this area will be in drought for three years (it is said that if a saint's tooth falls to the ground, the gods will punish him and punish him so that no rain will fall on that area). The Patriarch felt impatient and could not bear to let the people suffer because of the drought, so he swallowed two teeth into his stomach. Later in the dictionary, the sentence was recorded: "Breaking front teeth and swallowing them with blood" (defeat the village's maid of honor).

Practicing the paramita of patience, the Patriarch did not say anything, left the lecture hall of Mr. Than Quang, crossed the Truong Giang River and headed towards Tung Son mountain in Ha Nam. At that time, the King of Hell sent the impermanence demon to invite Magician Than Quang to attend the banquet.

The impermanence demon said to the Master: "Are you Divine Light?"

Answer: "Yes!"

Demon impermanence says: "King Yama invites you to drink tea."

After hearing this, Than Quang said: "While I was preaching the sutras, flowers from the sky fell and golden lotuses sprouted from the ground. Should I die?"

The impermanence demon replied: "Of course you must die!"

Than Quang asked: "Who can not die?"

The Devil then said the following: "Only the black monk whose front teeth you just knocked out were the only ones who didn't die."

At that time, Than Quang immediately begged the impermanence demon: "Impermanence layman, please have compassion and grace for me, so that I can follow that black monk and learn the immortal dharma, is that possible?"

The impermanence demon accepted this request, and Divine Light immediately headed north day and night to chase Datma. Finally, Than Quang came to Hung Nhi mountain, saw the Patriarch in the mountain cave facing the cliff in meditation, the Master bowed to the Patriarch in repentance, knelt for nine years, and then learned the immortality dharma. Later, he became the second Patriarch of Zen school.

The word "self" The above mentioned means to be self-reliant and not discouraged, one must try one's self and practice diligently to be able to reach the truth. So, on the right side of it there is the word "pipe," represents the meaning of practice, only then will there be inspiration, only then will there be achievement. If you don't practice, even understanding the principles will be useless. It is true: "Talking a word is not as good as doing a word."

I often say: "The way is done, no action becomes the way. Virtue is established, and virtue is not established." same meaning.

Seven Emotions and Six Desires Obstacle the Mind to Cultivate the Way

We, as practitioners, must wipe out all the delusions of love, lust, and lust, and eliminate them all. We must understand that broken love is the rock that binds our feet. Delusional thoughts about lost love will prevent our concentration in cultivating the path, causing us to be distracted all day by delusions, when we encounter situations, our mind will be moved, whatever concentration we have gathered will be wasted. Isn't it a waste of all the effort we have spent so long engaged in silent meditation?

Any man or woman must destroy the Seven Emotions. What is called That-love? These are joy, anger, guilt, love, hate, desire - joy, anger, sadness, fear, love, hate, lust; introduced simply as follows:

Hy: You shouldn't be happy, if you're happy then your feelings will be moved.

Anger: Don't be angry, anger will cause anger.

Ai: Don't feel sorry for anyone, everyone who is sad will be emotional.

Instrument: Don't be afraid, fear is also emotional.

Ai: You should not give birth to craving, because craving makes emotions move.

Oh: You should not have hatred in your heart. Disgust makes you emotional.

Sex: You should not have thoughts of desire, thoughts of desire will make your emotions move.

If you have strong feelings about the seven types of love mentioned above, the practitioner will be influenced by circumstances. If the Seven Emotions can shake us, then our concentration will be destroyed, we will be blown away by the wind of all kinds of circumstances, our mind will be shaken, we will no longer be able to control ourselves and, when there is no control, we will become crazy.

Whatever the sentient beings in hell do, they do in madness, because they are too ignorant and lack wisdom. Doing anything is wrong. If we in this world do wrong, we are no different from sentient beings in hell, that is, if we do things that are not in accordance with the dharma, with selfish purposes for self-benefit, that is hell. Happy about this, happy about that, sad and angry about this, sad and angry about that. To work with those kinds of feelings is to live in hell. Please pay attention! Remember! Must eliminate Seven Emotions and Six Desires. Luc-desires means six types of desires brought about by the six senses. The six senses are also called the six enemies, because they specialize in robbing our precious nature. Therefore, we must carefully guard the doors of the six rooms so that our treasures are not stolen.

In the Nine Dharma Realms, sentient beings are all crazy

What does crazy mean? That is seeing suffering as happiness, seeing right as wrong, seeing impermanence as permanent. It also means that the mind is uncertain, the mind is confused, when you see the right thing to do, you don't do it, when you see the benefits, you run after it. In short, not distinguishing between black and white, not knowing what is true and what is false, is called madness.

Saying: "Initiate confusion, create karma, receive retribution" is the law of cause and effect. First is delusion, giving rise to a wrong mind and then creating karma. After creating karma, you will receive the results - retribution, that is natural. Retribution is inconceivable, and sentient beings creating karma is also inconceivable. At first, delusion is born, which is also inconceivable. The reason is that all kinds of things are inconceivable, thus making all sentient beings dizzy and confused, not knowing what is the clue or what is appropriate.

Among the living beings in the nine dharma realms (i.e. the dharma realms of Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, Sravakas, gods, asuras, humans, animals, hungry ghosts, and hells), there are intelligent beings and there are stupid beings. Only Buddha, because he has great wisdom, is completely intelligent and has no ignorance.

Looking down from the perspective of the Buddha dharma realm, the beings in the Bodhisattva dharma realm are very crazy. The actions that Bodhisattvas do and consider to be right are just crazy in the eyes of Buddha.

Looking down from the dharma realm of Bodhisattvas to the Pratyekabuddha dharma realm, they see that they are like a group of children, their actions are not righteous, they are all crazy. Looking up, Bodhisattvas do not know anything about the Buddha Dharma Realm, they only know thoroughly about the Pratyekabuddha Dharma Realm, so there is a saying: "The first level does not know the second level, the tenth level does not know equality," It means not knowing the dharma realm higher than yourself. It's called knowing, but just understanding the situation in a brief, detailed way is not enough.

In the Pratyekabuddha dharma realm, if you look at the level of the Sravakas, the sentient beings here are crazy. But looking at the levels of Buddha and Bodhisattva, they do not know clearly. Why? Because they don't have enough concentration. The power of Pratyekabuddha's concentration is only enough to observe causes and conditions within the scope of eighty thousand great kalpas, but they cannot observe causes and conditions beyond eighty thousand great kalpas.

In the dharma world of Thanh-literature, looking at the gods here is crazy. The gods enjoy heavenly blessings, but from a higher perspective, they still act in a crazy way.

In the dharma world, when the heavens look at the asura scene, the asura goes crazy. The sentient beings here do not practice virtue, they only know how to fight. If fighting is not madness, then what else is it?

Looking at the gods from the Dharma world of the asuras, they do not understand much, but looking at the human world, they know thoroughly. Asura saw humans going crazy, floating in life and death without knowing suffering, taking suffering for fun, being attached and not wanting to give up, looking so pitiful.

In the human dharma realm, no one knows what the realm of the asuras is like, nor does they know anything about the lives of the gods, or the dharma realm of the Four Saints, but in the dharma realm of animals, they know clearly. They see that animals are so confused and crazy that they do not know anything other than delusions about food and desire.

Animals look at hungry ghosts and see that hungry ghosts are crazy, they suffer for food, but when they eat, the food is fire, they cannot swallow.

In the dharma world, hungry ghosts look at the dharma world of hell and see that the beings in hell are crazy. The sentient beings here have created evil karma and must receive evil retribution, but do not know how to change or change evil into good.

In the Dharma world of hell, sentient beings have absolutely no understanding, live in delusion, die in delusion, only know themselves, do not know anyone else. Hell is a vast sea of suffering, with no clear path left.

All living beings in the nine dharma realms are crazy. Only Buddha can reach the end and achieve Buddhahood, so there is no more confusion. For these reasons, we practice Buddha Dharma to attain true wisdom, to avoid having to go up and down within the nine dharma realms mentioned above, and to go beyond, to the Pure Land of Eternal Light, to be able to reside in the same place with all Buddhas.

In the dharma world of hell, every day tens of thousands of sentient beings are born and die, hundreds of thousands of insanity and suffering cannot be described in full. Why is that? Here, evil karma is overwhelming, so sentient beings must pay for their sins. In a world of complete chaos, there is no half-way that is not crazy, so leaving this dharma realm is extremely difficult.

Compared to the hungry ghost scene, although the hungry ghost cannot eat enough and is always hungry, hell is much more miserable. Among the hungry ghost's ten thousand inversions, there may be half a part, or one part that is not inverted (these numbers are given for comparison, not absolute meaning).

In the Dharma world of animals, among the ten thousand crazy things, there is one or one and a half percent that are not crazy, for example, goats still know how to kneel down when nursing, crows still have the meaning of suckling their babies, and animals know how to be filial. Any animal that is completely free from madness can have the opportunity to move up the path of goodness. Furthermore, like dogs that guard the house, roosters that crow, silkworms that produce silk, bees that produce honey, horses that pull carts, and buffaloes that pull plows, they also help humanity. With a little merit, they can escape the animal life in the future.

In the dharma world of humanity, there are ten or fifty parts, maximum no more than one hundred parts, which is not crazy. While not going crazy, people do meritorious deeds, or bowing to the Buddha, or chanting Buddha's name. When you are crazy, your thoughts are wandering around, you are greedy for fame and fortune, and you fight steadfastly. Why is there only one hundred percent that is not crazy among all the crazy things? Roughly like when bowing to the Buddha, for example, at that time it was not crazy. But there are times when the body is bowing to the Bodhisattva but the mind prays to the Bodhisattva for help, hoping that the Bodhisattva will win the lottery and bless him with peace; There are even people who refuse to study but still pray to Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva to bless them to pass the exam, which is crazy.

In the Dharma world of the asuras, there are about a hundred living beings who are not crazy, maybe a little more or less that number, because although the asuras enjoy the blessings of heaven, they consider themselves not enough, and because of their greed, they often fight to harm the freedom of others.

In the dharma world of the gods, there can be a thousand points of freedom in the world. They have the practice of meditation, an upward direction, when they think about eating, they get food, when they think about wearing, they get clothes to wear, when they think about something, there is that thing, so there is little confusion.

In the Sravaka world, among the ten thousand inversions, there are about two thousand non-inversions. Because these people practice the Four Truths - suffering, origin, cessation, path - they understand the principles of impermanence, emptiness, and non-self, so there are fewer inversions here.

In the Pratyekabuddha dharma realm, among the ten thousand perversions there can be up to three thousand non-inversions. Here, the Pratyekabuddhas attained enlightenment by contemplating the twelve causes and conditions, understanding that everything is an illusion, so they are completely not attached to anything.

In the Bodhisattva Dharma Realm, among the ten thousand things that are crazy, there can be five thousand that are not crazy, so there are still five thousand that are crazy. Bodhisattvas specialize in cultivating the six perfections of ten thousand actions, but still have a portion of ignorance so they have not yet reached the ultimate level.

In the Dharma world of all Buddhas, there are no inversions, because Buddha has perfected the three enlightenments, and all virtues are complete; There is no delusion, no confusion, the Buddha is supremely enlightened.

You must study carefully! Why have we not been able to eliminate afflictions in this world, but are still in a mixed place waiting to die? Those who leave the home life don't act like they're leaving the home life, and those who leave the home don't practice! When should we wait until we practice? This life is full of five evils, what is the benefit of lingering on life and death?

Gentlemen! Be serious about the issue of life and death, quickly develop the mind of Bodhi, don't create more crazy things. Turn around! Try your best, "The sea of suffering has no shore, turn around and find a port."

Learning Magical Powers for Revenge?

Milarepa is a Tibetan. His motive for practicing Buddhism was not to save sentient beings but to avenge his parents. Because at the beginning the goal was not right, he got lost on the difficult path, causing his thoughts and behavior to be no different from that of an asura. His constant desire is to destroy everyone, except himself, which is completely contrary to religion. A cultivator cannot harbor anger or a desire for revenge, otherwise he will become a relative of the Demon King.

Later, because his practice brought some achievements, he used secret mantras and supernatural powers to avenge his hatred. As a result, the revenge has been paid, the hatred has been washed away. However, his actions not only hinder religious practice, but also betray the spirit of compassion of practitioners. Everyone who cultivates religion must take compassion as the root and act accordingly. He is the exact opposite, in his heart there is only pride and arrogance, no respect for anyone, not only for lay people but also disdain for those leaving the home life. That's because he only knows himself and doesn't know anyone else. He had those kinds of ideas and no one told him anything to make him understand.

If you try to cultivate the path with a resentful mind, no matter how long you practice, you will still have hateful thoughts. He uses secret mantras and supernatural powers to do the work of retribution and revenge, but who knows, he may have made a mistake in cause and effect and will have to suffer retribution in the future. Such actions are based on misconceptions, and I think he also knows that. However, knowing is knowing, but his mind is already dominated by anger, he can no longer control himself, so he acts crazy, and the result has brought him into the realm of the devil, which is really dangerous.

Everyone knows that doing good deeds is right, but no one wants to do it. Why? Because doing good deeds doesn't see anything good. Like observing the precepts, for example, is a good thing, but no one observes the precepts. Following the rules is good, but everyone doesn't follow them. Everyone knows clearly that not observing the precepts, not keeping the rules is not right, but making mistakes all the time, everything is like that, it turns out that you know it. It's just that it's caused by poor mental health and laziness. That, to put it bluntly, is nothing noble or moral. There is a saying: "A gentleman is superior, a petty man is inferior," The type of people mentioned above do not want to go up, but only want to go down (lower attainment), there is truly no cure.

I often say:

Cultivating the Dharma is like posting hundreds of red canes

The future is simple, the upper is difficult.

Meaning: Cultivating the Way is like climbing a hundred meter high pole. Climbing down is easy, climbing up is difficult. Today I point out Milarepa's wrong knowledge and wrong view for us to be wary of. In short, cultivating the Way must have a heart of "unconditioned love," have the thought of "uniform great compassion," Learning the spirit of Tien Nhan Nhan (one of the Buddha's predecessors), being tolerant of everyone, is worthy of being a Buddha disciple.

tieu_de: The Four Aeons of Creation, Persistence, Destruction, and Emptiness of the World
tom_tat: The world is countless, immeasurable, boundless. Each world (planet) goes through four kalpas: creation, existence, destruction, and emptiness. It's just that our wisdom is limited, not yet at the level to know the depths of emptiness and all dharmas...
noi_dung:
The Four Aeons of Creation, Persistence, Destruction, and Emptiness of the World

The world is countless, immeasurable, boundless. Each world (planet) goes through four kalpas: creation, existence, destruction, and emptiness. However, our wisdom is limited, not yet at the level to know the depths of nothingness and the entire dharma world. We only know this world and do not know countless other worlds.

Nowadays, although science has made many advances, it has brought people to the moon, another world, but it still does not fully understand its situation. The lunar world and our earthly world are not the same. Our world experiences four signs of creation, existence, destruction, and emptiness, and other worlds also have four signs like that, the only difference is that those four signs do not arise at the same time. In this world, the current appearance is formation, in that world there is the appearance of stability, in the other world there is the appearance of destruction, or the appearance of emptiness; Therefore, because they do not share the same appearance, we do not know the situation of other worlds clearly.

Not only do we not know clearly what other worlds are like, but we also do not have a clear understanding of this world. When Khalunbo had not yet discovered the "New World," That means no one knows about this Western Hemisphere, for example, people just think that the sky is round and the earth is square. After discovering the New World, people proved that the earth is round, so people called it the globe.

Now, whoever sits in a spaceship and admires the earth, sees it just like a ball floating in mid-air, it's interesting to see!

Called "New World" but it's not "new" (new) but "old" (old). If you haven't discovered it yet, you think it doesn't exist. When you discover it, it's called new. That's just because of people's attachment to discrimination. People, in their thoughts, in their vision, have a distinction between new and old. In fact, everything is in the transformation of the four signs of creation, persistence, destruction, and emptiness.

The world has formation, stability, destruction, and emptiness, so humans also have formation, stability, destruction, and emptiness, with all four characteristics. From the moment of birth, to the moment of going to school, that is the period of maturity. After learning, practice according to your will, that is the period of stability. Later, when you get old and weak, that is the period of decay. The end of old age is death, death is the period of nothingness. Creation, existence, destruction, and emptiness mean birth, illness, old age, and death.

After the birth period comes the illness period. Everyone has their own illness. Someone said: "Sorcerer! It cannot be said in such generalities. Some people's bodies are not healthy, they have diseases, but some people's bodies are healthy, they don't have any diseases?" You see that their bodies are not sick, but in their minds they are sick. In short, there is no one whose body and mind are not sick. Let's say that both body and mind are not sick, but that's not always the case. Physiologically, we may be sure that we are not sick, but psychologically, is it certain? More or less there must be, if there is no small illness, it is still the type of illness born from habits, attachments, things that do not recognize them, cannot let them go, then that is illness. Not being able to receive, not being able to let go means liberation is not possible.

Going home without control, birth and death without freedom, means illness. Not being able to control yourself, not being able to keep yourself forever young, never old, never die, that is also a disease. If you can control yourself, it means you can ensure that this body must always be young and healthy, never have dim eyes, deaf ears, gray hair, or loose teeth. Can you do that? If you can't do it, you will get sick.

Someone said: "I exercise every day, my body is very healthy, my arms and legs are nimble, I walk as fast as flying, and I don't have any illnesses." So do you dare to guarantee that you will be forever young, will live forever without aging? I'm afraid I can't keep it that way! Why? Because you have a disease in your heart. What disease? The disease of greed, the disease of anger, the disease of ignorance. Greed is insatiable, the more the better. When you are greedy for something but cannot get it, you get angry. At that time, your wisdom cannot overwhelm your emotions, your mind becomes confused. Murders and burning of houses also come from that place, so isn't that a disease?

Adolescence signals the beginning of old age. Likewise, illness is the beginning of death. In general, humans are a small universe, so they also have four appearances. Understanding this meaning means you will no longer be attached to this smelly leather bag, and will no longer cherish it like it is a precious thing. If you truly do not cling to this body, then it is true selflessness, then the world is peaceful, there are no more troubles.

People in this world only know this small world, so they want to find out what it is like to the end. But, after studying again and again, it's the same thing: when you arrive you're confused, when you leave you're confused. As soon as I understand the transparency, it's oh well! Departure! Waiting for the next life! In the next life, he continued to research, but he couldn't research much more when the impermanence demon came and invited him to meet the King of Hell. In this life, if you don't worry about studying the matter of birth and death, how long will you wait? I hope you take this issue seriously and research it, don't let it go in vain, remember:

Personality is difficult and difficult to overcome

Buddha's dharma is difficult to write, golden text is written

Test the body's direction of the golden life

Wings facing the planet to test the body?

Translated means: The difficult human body has now been obtained, the Buddha Dharma, which was difficult to hear, has now been heard. If this body cannot be saved in this life, in what life will it be possible to save it?

We must consider it as something to be wary of, and often use it as a mirror to look back at ourselves.

Speaking further, there are countless worlds that we cannot know clearly, this does not need to be repeated. Particularly between people, there are so many problems that we do not understand. Why is that? Because there are too many delusions. Why are there so many false thoughts? Where do delusions come from? No one knows. Even anger, greed, anger and ignorance, where do they come from? In general it is impossible to know. What problems do we have ourselves, are there more or less? How much do you understand? All are unknown.

The above things are not easy to know thoroughly, and we ourselves do not want to know them thoroughly. For what reason? Because all day we only know how to compete for fame and fortune, we have no time to research those issues. Sometimes people wake up and want to study where they came from and where they will go when they die, but because they cannot meet good and knowledgeable guides, they only practice in blindness, not grasping the principles of practice, so in the end their efforts are wasted, and worse, they become possessed by demons. So cultivating religion is not an easy thing.

There's no need to talk about other worlds, this world alone, between people, is full of issues we don't understand. We have not researched our own problems clearly, so how can we study other people's problems? If our problems and those of others are not transparent, how can the problem of the worlds be made transparent? How can that be resolved? So it's not resolved anymore? Not so! It definitely has to be resolved! Otherwise, the world will be destroyed. How to solve? The only way is to concentrate on cultivating the path, attaining the fruit of the five eyes and six powers, then you will naturally understand all the mysteries of the universe, once and for all. Once you clearly know the internal situation, you can improve your human mind, eliminating the three poisons of greed, anger, and ignorance. At that time, all problems will be resolved directly, the world will be peaceful, there will be no more conflicts forever, the world will not be destroyed. If anyone doesn't believe it, please close your eyes and ponder. If a third world war breaks out, what will be the consequences? Everyone will understand that the result is a state of "final convergence," to the end of destruction. That time was the period of no life.

leaving the home life - giving thoroughly

Among the Bodhisattvas, there is the Great Bodhisattva, who is rich and luxurious, has a splendidly decorated house, with all kinds of exquisite items to serve life. Despite being so rich, if anyone wanted to come and ask for something, the Great Bodhisattva would give it without hesitation. Bodhisattvas who practice the giving method do not pay attention to their family at all, because in their minds they have long abandoned the concept of family. The Bodhisattva understood the concept of family emptiness, because family is simply a harmonious relationship between causes and conditions, but when the relationship ends, they separate. What is there to be attached to? The Bodhisattva was already bored with all the wealth in the house, from movables to real estate, along with everyday items. In daily life, we do not desire to satisfy the five desires, do not wear nice clothes, or eat delicious food, so our mind is not bound by material needs. Understanding that the family will eventually disperse and cannot last forever, the Great Bodhisattva often shows cold feelings towards the family, only wanting to completely separate from worldly life, to leave the home life to practice religion, to seek liberation from the three worlds. When it comes to family members, like the wife, she is considered a shackle around her neck, and her child is a chain to tie her feet. A woman's lover is a handcuff. Once her hands are locked, how can she move? Each individual's body is so bound, they can't even breathe freely, what can they say about the desire to be free? In such a situation, what else is there for us to regret?

Bodhisattva discovered that, then let go of everything, and in order to escape the oppressive situation of his family, he stayed away from worldly life and practiced Bodhisattva conduct. The eighty-four thousand dharmas that the Buddha taught the world to practice are the path to Bodhi, and to dignify oneself. Throw away external objects such as money without regret. Such behaviors of Bodhisattvas are praised and praised by all Buddhas of the ten directions as follows: "Very good! Great! Good man! He was so diligent, developed such a vast Bodhi mind, did things that other people could not do, threw away property and houses, things that people cannot throw away, gave everything he had to others without regrets, without regrets, without attachments, things that are really difficult to do. Bodhisattva saw someone coming to beg him and felt extremely happy in his heart, thinking that he was extremely lucky to have the opportunity to perform the great giving.

Leaving the home life is a difficult task. Xa told me about cutting my hair, shaving, putting on the robe, saying a few words "co phong", Open your mouth to talk about Buddha and the Dharma, speak the principles in the scriptures, or sit still and close your eyes to meditate. Those acts can be called wearing Buddha clothes, eating Buddha rice, performing the role of someone leaving the home life. If it is true that words are matched with actions, a sincere and compassionate heart when treating people and things, always doing the same in front and behind without going wrong, then such a person is truly leaving the home life.

Leaving the home life has three types:

Body leaving the home life, mind not leaving the home life.

Tam left the home life, body has not left the home life.

Body and mind are leaving the home life.

Among leaving the home life, there are also three types of levels, depending on the practice and practice that can be determined.

Out of the secular world: This is generally about disciples leaving the home life; Bhikkhus, Bhiksunis, novices, novices.

Out of ignorance and afflictions: This is talking about your spiritual state of leaving the home life, how far you can practice by yourself, but through your speech, silence, movement, and stillness, outsiders can also know. An individual leaving the home life who practices will gradually reduce his habit energy, and the manifestation of greed, anger, and ignorance will also gradually decrease, as the ancient saying goes: "Part by part, breaking through ignorance, each part of the dharma body is realized." All of you seem to be trying to break free from ignorance and afflictions and move towards the path of Bodhi.

Exit from the three worlds: This is the ultimate goal of the person leaving the home life and also of all seven people on the path to study Buddhism. The goal to be achieved is to permanently eliminate birth and death, and then, through the power of one's own vow, freely return to the nine dharma realms to save sentient beings, achieving the ultimate peace of leaving the home life.

Bodhisattva also makes vows that all sentient beings can escape the bondage of family, to enter the family of all Buddhas, to study the dharma taught by Buddha, and to diligently practice the holy life. The Bodhisattva vows that all sentient beings abandon their greedy, greedy and dirty minds, transform into a joyful mind that loves giving and giving, take the gift of wealth as joy, and never give birth to a regressive mind. Furthermore, I pray that all sentient beings will leave the notions of worldly family, not care about the so-called promotions, fame and reputation, and the worldly dharmas of continuing the family line, and even more so, not being dishonest, hoarding houses full of valuables, filling warehouses with valuables, all of which are the seeds that give rise to evil karma. The ancients said: "Multiple treasures must lead to death." The more you store, the worse you lose. There is another sentence: "The body is bounded by no objects of desire, it is born of no afflictions," If you don't have precious things with you, afflictions will not arise. The old saying is true, at the end of the day, you leave with empty hands. Bodhisattvas teach living beings to reduce their desires and live innocently and honestly, joy will naturally arise.

The Bodhisattva vows that all sentient beings quickly overcome the afflictions caused by worldly life, learn the Buddha's pure practice, so that in the future they can integrate into the Buddha's house and live in the same place with the Buddha. Again, I pray that all sentient beings will learn the ultimate dharma that is perfect and unobstructed, eliminate all the obstacles of impure dharmas, and become pure and free. Again, I vow that all sentient beings, separated from the love and affection of their family, may still be shaken in their bodies, but their hearts will no longer be attached to the feelings of kinship. Again, I pray that all sentient beings will know how to skillfully advise and guide those who are still immersed in family love, making them understand that family is just a temporary combination created by causes and conditions so that their hearts will be less attached. The Bodhisattva raised the principle of human birth that Buddha taught to guide those who are confused and unable to escape the worldly dharma of family, making them believe in Buddha dharma, study Buddha dharma, understand Buddha dharma, and no longer be entangled in the bondage of family. Again, I vow that all sentient beings, although their bodies remain with their families, their minds always obey the wisdom of all Buddhas, practice religious work, and abide in immobility. Again, I pray that all sentient beings, although they have not yet left the home life and are still living a lay life, their wishes have been placed on all Buddhas, and can be spread to countless and boundless sentient beings, so that all of them can develop a mind of joy and a vast mind of Bodhisattva. That is the great Bodhisattva in the Bodhisattva class, when giving houses and houses, he has done dedicating merit and good roots for sentient beings. It is the hope that sentient beings can achieve the great vows of the Bodhisattva, along with all kinds of supernatural powers and wisdom.

Summary excerpt from the Sixth Avatamsaka Sutra dedicating the merit of Preaching From

Bodhisattva's heart is like a mother's love for her child

You are faithful! Think about it, is it difficult or not difficult to be a Bodhisattva? Bodhisattvas live in the realm of supernatural powers, sacrificing themselves, using their skin, flesh, bones, and bone marrow to make internal wealth giving, and taking strongholds, wives, children, and other treasures to make external wealth giving. That is not an easy thing to do. Not to say that people in the world consider sharing money as difficult as cutting one's own flesh, but Bodhisattva also voluntarily sacrificed his life and willingly became a servant for others, that's really difficult. If, wherever we are, we do not take advantage for ourselves, and every action comes from compassion, not from greed, anger, or ignorance, but purely for the benefit of others, then that is the work of living Bodhisattvas. Isn't this easy? But, some do not want to do such easy things, and even more difficult things do not want to do. Do you think, is the Bodhisattva pitiful or not? They make hundreds of thousands of great vows, exhausting all the good organs of the head, eyes, and brain, to completely dedicating merit to sentient beings. Every day and every moment, they hope that we will receive the benefit of that dedicating merit to become Buddhas and saints. Yet we are still calmly enjoying ourselves in the fiery house of the Three Realms, in the ocean of worldly suffering. So do you think Bodhisattva is pitiful or not? However, the Bodhisattva is still determined, not discouraged, still working to save sentient beings, educate sentient beings, give life and wealth to sentient beings, bring merit and good roots to dedicating merit to sentient beings, with the hope that sentient beings can become Buddhas, Saints, and Patriarchs.

Gentlemen! If you have ever been a mother, you can understand the Bodhisattva's heart, as well as the care, earnestness, and tact of mothers when pleasing their children. Whoever is a mother does not care that she is weak; When I have to worry about my children, I still wholeheartedly and determinedly commit myself to the benefit of my children. During pregnancy, the mother begins to calculate and dream about her future child with all the good things, that it will be more intelligent and intelligent than others, that it will make the family and ancestors glorious, surpassing hundreds of thousands of other people. When the baby is born, hear its first cry, then see its small, red face, right in that painful moment of having to fight against the life-or-death danger, that single cry can erase all the images of the mother's hardships during the ten months of pregnancy. After that, the days and months changed, three years of breastfeeding, holding and taking care of the child, fearing that the child would be difficult to raise, then prayed to God, worshiped Buddha, burned incense and prayed, praying for the child to have no troubles or pain, hoping that it would soon become a human. When the child grows up, the child who does not disappoint his or her parents will be a happy family. However, there are also disobedient children who are unfilial, blasphemous, assault their elders, are evil, break the law, and leave their parents at the mercy of their parents. Yet, as a mother, you always love your children, are not disappointed in them, and still consider your children to be good, not inferior to other families' children. Gentlemen! Such is the heart of a mother! The Bodhisattva's compassion for living beings is the same. Buddha said that the kindness of parents is difficult to repay, so how can Bodhisattva's kindness to us be repaid in full? Each of us must remember these two layers of grace every moment. Anyone who leaves or leaves the home life must learn to practice compassion first, and treat others with kindness. If you cannot do these basic things, then you are afraid that on the path to Bodhi, no one will see your footsteps.

tieu_de: Zero: The Great Bright Treasury of Self-Nature
tom_tat: From beginningless kalpas until now, living beings have been circulating in the cycle of samsara, going up and down without ever leaving the cycle of birth and death, just like a small speck of dust, drifting uncertainly, sometimes flying up in the sky, sometimes falling...
noi_dung:
Zero: The Great Bright Treasury of Self-Nature

From beginningless kalpas until now, living beings have been circulating in the cycle of samsara, going up and down without ever leaving the cycle of birth and death, just like a small speck of dust, drifting uncertainly, sometimes flying up in the sky and sometimes falling to the ground. Living beings are sometimes human, sometimes asuras, sometimes animals, sometimes hungry ghosts, with no beginning and no end.

Only when one attains Buddhahood can one escape the suffering of samsara. When you have not yet become a Buddha, you still have to rotate through the six paths. Bodhisattvas still have to overcome the delusion of "warmness," Arhats are still delusional because of "pregnancy", Great dharmakaya monks manifest in the world, saving all sentient beings. Sometimes they are entangled in birth and death, their minds are in a coma and they don't know the way out.

No beginning means there is no beginning - no beginning, no end means no end. For example, the letter O, this letter has no starting place or ending place, it is just like that. If you cut out the letter O, then it becomes the letter one (-), and this letter has a beginning. Start what? Start item number. The first is one, one more dash becomes two, one more dash becomes three. Just like that, it will reach ten, then one hundred, then ten thousand. From tens of thousands to billions, from billions to millions, to endless numbers.

Now in the age of science, every day, every month is different, changing very rapidly with acceleration. People use rockets to shoot satellites into the air and put them into orbit so they can operate without stopping. Then this spacecraft meets the other spacecraft in space. Isn't this a progression from the beginning of the number? Only with numbers can we calculate, with calculations we can have assembly techniques, and with numbers we can calculate to coordinate the assembly times. If we keep growing the number of items like that, it will never end in the future.

When is it time to end? Currently no one knows. At the end of the cycle, we must wait until all four kalpas of formation, abiding, destruction, and emptiness have passed, that is, we have reached the emptiness of kalpas. Success is the beginning, failure is the end. There are twenty small kalpas in formation, twenty small kalpas in life, twenty small kalpas in destruction, and twenty small kalpas in nothingness. Eighty small kalpas become one great kalpa. The life of the earth lasts only one great eon.

Among the sentient beings from time immemorial, did men come first or did women come first? We just assume that men came first, for example, so if there were no women, where would men come from? For example, women came first. If there were no men, where would women come from? Beginningless is like that, don't know where to start.

Or, for example, did the chicken come first or did the egg come first? No one can think of this, so how does it end up? Its meaning can be summarized in the letter O. Therefore, this letter O has no beginning, no end, is neither inside nor outside, neither big nor small. Compact it, it is a microscopic particle, let it expand, it is a dharma realm, until the end of space, the entire dharma realm does not exceed the scope of the letter O. The letter O is the source of endless birth and transformation, it is the true emptiness of beginningless and endless existence. The enlarged letter O is the vacuum, the smaller is the wonderful existence.

The true emptiness of wonderful existence is the true emptiness of non-emptiness that gives rise to wonderful existence. Wonderful existence and non-existence have no obstacle to emptiness.

Emptiness and existence are not two, emptiness is existence, existence is emptiness, that is the meaning of the ultimate middle path, and also the true meaning of Mahayana dharma.

At beginningless time, this letter O was the true emptiness of wonderful existence. True emptiness is not emptiness, and wonderful existence is not true existence, but perfect harmony without hindrance, is the meaning of the middle path without favoring either side. Gentlemen! If anyone understands this principle clearly, he will understand the true dharma. Anyone who does not understand is a confused person, not a person with true wisdom.

For enlightened people, the letter O represents great luminous wisdom; If you are not enlightened, that word is great darkness. Ignorance is also O, and wisdom is also O. The letter O is sometimes very big, to the point that there is nothing outside it, the big child has no outside, sometimes very small, so small that there is nothing inside it, the little child has no inside. Talking about big, there is nothing bigger than it; Talking about small, there is nothing smaller than it. If this letter O becomes large and transforms into an invisible one, then it is the source of purity, the nature of wonderful true suchness; If it is small and hidden, it is an ignorant thought at the beginning. That is the meaning of beginningless.

Why do living beings keep samsara in samsara? Because it is impossible to attain the true Dharma. Therefore, all Buddhas saw that sentient beings were very pitiful, and because of their compassion for sentient beings, they developed a mind of great compassion and appeared in the world to teach sentient beings to leave suffering and reach a state of peace. To develop the mind of Bodhi, above, seek the Buddha's way, below, to save sentient beings, that is, cultivating the unsurpassed path of enlightenment.

We receive karma in the six realms of samsara because in our minds we have created karma, whatever type of karma we create, we will receive karma of that type. Broadly speaking, if you have false thoughts about the heavens in your previous life, you can be born in the heavenly realm; If you have false thoughts about hell, you will fall into hell. If you create bad karma, you will be born in the three evil realms. If you create karma with merit, you will be born in the three good realms. That is such a general outline. If you want to talk about it in detail, you can't even talk about the next life.

This world is created by the delusions of sentient beings. If living beings do not have false thoughts, then this world is empty. It is also because sentient beings cannot perceive the true form of the dharma, the truly emptiness of dharma, that the world exists.

The Dharma of true emptiness and wonderful existence is the letter O. The world exists from the letter O, living beings are born from the letter O. Everything is born from the letter O, because the letter O is not in the number of items, when it is magnified, it is complete, and when it is contracted, it is hidden. That is also the realm of no beginning and no end, of nothing inside and nothing outside, neither big nor small.

This true Dharma is the true emptiness of existence. Emptiness but not empty, why is that? Because there is no magic existence in true emptiness. Wonderful existence but not existence, why? Because it has a vacuum. So there is a sentence: "Emptyness does not hinder wonderful existence, wonderful existence does not hinder vacuum." All of the above meanings provide answers to the problems of whether male or female came first, whether the chicken came first or the egg. Only the letter O can directly answer the difficult problems mentioned above.

Why can emptiness give birth to wonderful existence? Does it show everything? Meanwhile, the wonderful friend has never left the void? Not everyone can reach this kind of realm, unless they have been enlightened to the mind-seal method of all Buddhas.

This type of true dharma is already inherent in our own nature, there is no need to search anywhere outside. If you keep searching outside, even eighty thousand great tribulation swords will not come out. If you know the light is reflected, that's it, that's why there is a saying: "The sea of ​​suffering has no shore, turn around and find a port." Simply put, if you run out looking for it, it will be a shoreless sea of suffering. If you know how to turn inward and apply effort on your own nature, then right there, when you turn around, you will see the destination.

From morning till night, we go up and down, chasing after false predestined conditions, wandering after the six senses, because we do not understand the true magic dharma. Meanwhile, in the Pure Land of Everlasting Light, all Buddhas were in the cross-legged position, looking at all sentient beings, seeing that they were so stupid, so pitiful, all day long clinging to east and west, taking suffering for pleasure but not knowing how to return to the path of enlightenment, not knowing how to use the false to cultivate the real, not knowing how to give up illusions and returning to the truth, not knowing how to return to one's own. Therefore, from within concentration, all Buddhas, filled with compassion, appeared to the predestined worlds to show sentient beings their confusion and teach sentient beings to quickly return to enlightenment. Unfortunately, we have chased false fate without realizing the true dharma. Buddha preached the Dharma out of compassion for us, educating us without being boring, but because of our ignorance we refused to listen, not only did we not practice the Dharma, but we also faltered and retreated, not following the golden teachings. Buddha even thought of ways to follow us, block the footsteps of stubborn and stubborn beings, and try to tame those who are difficult to teach. That is the reason why Buddha appeared in the world.

This true Dharma can never be destroyed, and pagan demons have no way to destroy it. Why? Because the Dharma is as solid as diamond and indestructible. If it can be destroyed, it is not a true dharma.

This kind of great self in great light can manifest all over the world. The great dharma at the storehouse is a dharma that will eliminate birth and death, destroy ignorance, and is a dharma door that can manifest the light of dharma nature.

Gentlemen! If you don't believe it, try it out. There will come a time when you can't help but believe, if you don't believe you will believe it, because the dharma is like that, there is no way to not believe it!

This great enlightenment treasure is inherently available to you, not given to you by others, nor given to you by all Buddhas. The great luminous treasure is the true nature of suchness. If you practice this true Dharma, the alaya consciousness (eighth consciousness) will transform into Great Complete Wisdom, which means ending the path of birth and death. If we do not practice seriously, the seeds in alaya will, depending on causes and conditions, turn into birth, endless birth, without time limit, so liberation will not be possible.
