tieu_de: Fellow "Greedy" Friends Must Encourage Each Other to Cultivate
tom_tat: People with deep roots of good will do good deeds wherever they go. Their motto is to do good and be happy, to take good deeds as joy, and they often remember this. On the contrary, those with deep karma obstructions...
noi_dung:
Fellow "Greedy" Must Encourage Each Other to Cultivate

People with deep roots of good will do good deeds wherever they go. Their motto is to do good and be happy, to take good deeds as joy, and they often remember this. On the contrary, people with deep karma often want to listen to unwholesome stories and unethical stories, which they consider to be models to follow. Even if there are good intellectuals who tell them good and reasonable things, they ignore them, but when the evil intellectuals incite them to do unreasonable things, they listen. Why is that? Because what is reasonable goes against their thoughts, and what is unreasonable meets their wishes. Such is the illness of this class of people.

In general, for anyone, just look carefully at what they like and we can know what their nature is like. Lazy people love to hear people talk about lazy tricks. Diligent people love to listen to stories about diligent practice. There are cases where people do not practice diligently, just waiting for an opportunity to lazily seek peace of mind, but next to their fellow practitioners who practice diligently, they are also influenced and diligently follow. There are also cases where people are diligent but because of the influence of friends around them, they become lazy. Therefore, friends who meditate together must encourage each other and encourage each other so that we can all be diligent towards the goal - which is to develop great Bodhi mind, practice the path of unsurpassed enlightenment, and attain Bodhisattva status.

The ancients said: You must be careful when living together, you must be careful when making friends, you must choose your neighbors, you must be careful with your playmates. When choosing friends, we must also find good friends, and cannot hang out with dishonest people indiscriminately. Otherwise, you will join the low-class people in doing bad things, causing you to lose your reputation, be unable to save, and eventually fall into hell. That is an extremely dangerous thing, you can't be careful!

At the ashram, the worst thing is not to practice, the most precious thing is the seriousness of practice. Whoever does not practice will have a bad future; Whoever practices practice will have a better future. People say: "A gentleman is superior, a petty man is inferior," Therefore, when we practice at the ashram, we must be careful every hour, every moment, and get rid of wrong thoughts, wrong knowledge, and wrong views like speculators who only know tricks to secure themselves. Cultivation must rely on one's true effort to have true value, that is, to open wisdom. If the practice is not genuine, then nothing can be achieved, no matter who it is.

At the ashram, whoever relaxes, whoever is diligent, whoever has sharp eyes sees everything. Anyone who is lazy will have no hope of achieving anything, because he or she does not pay attention to practice. If at that time someone else joined in, it would be very disastrous. Good intellectuals do not follow other people's tastes, but are ready to criticize and correct mistakes when they notice someone doing something wrong. It's the same between friends, if you see a friend doing something wrong, you still have to use words of wisdom to advise and hope that you will change your ways. People say: "The medicine is bitter, it hurts to tell the truth," That is the true duty to a friend, not to love you but to let you be confused and not realize the truth. We are all practicing together, so we should encourage each other, advise each other, and not show jealousy and hinder each other. That must be remembered! From now on, we will never get this bad disease again, otherwise we will all fall together into hell.

Our responsibility to our friends is to advise us to do good and avoid evil. Seeing that you are wrong, trying to advise you, so that you can change, not follow along and let you do the wrong thing, causing you to fall more and more every day. You are brothers and sisters together, like a family, you should take care of each other. Whoever does something wrong with the precepts must sincerely advise you to return to order. If that's not the case, then you are "greedy". What does it mean? As Dharma friends, it's not like we group together to deceive each other. Having those thoughts is extremely wrong.

We as practitioners should treat each other honestly, advise each other to do good, follow the righteous path, and cannot tolerate lies. Like the bad habit of flattering and following other people, they all have disastrous effects. When not, people don't dare to be bold and do things that are too unruly and break the rules. Because we follow and make friends with them, they think we have a place to rely on so they dare to act arrogantly, disregarding cause and effect, which is a pitiful thing. Companions must help each other on the path of practice, encourage each other towards Bodhi, not you pulling me, I pulling you down together, harming each other, that is not helping each other.

Fellow "greedy" friends How should we help each other? By talking about the scriptures together, studying the doctrine together. If you don't understand something clearly, I'll come talk to you; I have something unclear, please come and point it out for me. We research and study together faithfully. Please remember this carefully! Avoid anything rude! Eyes do not see, ears do not hear, mouth does not speak, body does not do anything rude! At the gates of the six senses, you must control delusions, must regularly, hour by hour, moment by moment absorb your body and mind, eliminating distracting thoughts. How to eliminate? It's very simple, just practice precepts, concentration, wisdom, and extinguish greed, anger, and ignorance.

tieu_de: To practice Buddhism, you must learn the basic Dharma
tom_tat: In Buddhism there are exoteric and esoteric teachings. Explicit teachings are clear teachings. Anyone who has a Bodhisattva mind and practices the unsurpassed path can become a Buddha. Tantra is a secret teaching, if you tell me I won't know, if you tell me you'll...
noi_dung:
To practice Buddhism, you must learn the basic Dharma

In Buddhism there are exoteric and esoteric teachings. Explicit teachings are clear teachings. Anyone who has a Bodhisattva mind and practices the unsurpassed path can become a Buddha. Tantra is a secret teaching, I won't know if I tell you, you won't know if you tell me, you and I don't know each other. The esoteric teachings advocate enlightening the mind and realizing the nature, while the esoteric teachings advocate the body becoming a Buddha. In general, in our previous lives we planted good roots, so in this life we have the opportunity to practice Buddha Dharma. In this life, practice diligently, hoping that in the next life your vow will come true.

In the teachings, there is a division into Mahayana and Hinayana. The Hinayana is also called the Second Vehicle, which means Sravaka Vehicle and Pratyekabuddha Vehicle. Mahayana is the Bodhisattva vehicle. Now, I would like to briefly introduce the dharmas of the three vehicles for your new practitioners to refer to.

I. The Four Noble Truths of Arhats.

Sravaka, these two words mean to listen to Shakyamuni Buddha's preaching about the Four Noble Truths and attain enlightenment (voice is sound, text is hearing). Sravaka or Arahantship, includes four fruitions. The first is the first stage of arahantship, this fruit has eliminated the delusions of the three worlds, entering "the stream of dharma nature of saints, contrary to the stream of six senses of ordinary people;" This result requires seven more births and deaths.

The second result of Arhat has eliminated the illusions of the three realms, and also eliminated the first six levels of delusions of the three realms. This result requires two more births and deaths, one birth in heaven, one birth in the world.

The third result of Arhat is to eliminate the following three chapters of thought and desire of the desire realm, and there is still one more birth and death, but not being born in the desire realm but being born in the form realm or the formless realm.

The fourth fruit of arahantship eliminates all eighty-one qualities of the three worlds and is no longer subject to birth and death; Strictly speaking, it is not divided into birth and death, but is still in the transition of birth and death.

Although the Sravaka class is called enlightenment, there are different types of enlightenment, shallow and deep, some ultimate and some not ultimate, meaning the level is uneven. The Sravaka practice is suffering, origin, cessation, and path. Contemplating suffering, everything is suffering. Suffering is divided into three sufferings and eight sufferings. Their practice is to cut off habits, destroy them, and cultivate the path (cut off habits, love Nirvana, and cultivate the path). These three factors are closely related to each other, such as suffering gives birth to afflictions and afflictions must be eliminated. How to eliminate? We must get rid of delusions, delusions and afflictions that have accumulated for a long time. You must admire the Nirvana dharma, i.e. its four natures: Permanent, Bliss, Self, and Pure (Nirvana's four virtues). From the shore of birth and death through the stream of afflictions to the other shore, it is a whole process of cultivating thirty-seven levels of path to be successful. Among these dharmas are the eightfold path, including:

right view,

right thinking,

right speech,

main karma,

right livelihood,

right effort,

mindfulness,

right concentration,

These dharmas are common to the entire Mahayana.

II. Dharma contemplation of the Twelve Causes and Conditions of Bich-chi Buddha.

There are two types of Bich-chi Buddha: Pratyekabuddha and Pratyekabuddha. When the Buddha did not appear in the world, there were people who enlightened themselves, sitting quietly in deep caves and mountains, watching flowers bloom in spring, seeing yellow leaves falling in autumn and enlightenment, this type is called Single Enlightenment. When a Buddha appears in the world, there are people who meditate on the Twelve Causes and Conditions to enlighten, then this type is called Pratyekabuddha. The first is contemplation of ignorance. What is ignorance? It's not being clear about anything. To put it bluntly, it's stupid. To put it bluntly, it's the lustful mind, the mind that makes a boy want a girl, a girl want a boy. Ask him, ask her why she wants that, then, either answer that I think she's beautiful, or answer that he's handsome. Ask again why you love her, where is her cuteness? Asked back and forth, neither she nor he knew. Not knowing but still running after it is ignorance, a strange thing that no one can understand. No one understands, so why do we still have to get stuck in? Why is that? Because humans are born because of lust, they must also die because of lust, in accordance with the saying:

Birth and fall, the gate of death and death protect

Ky fish to Tinh Ky fish satu?

Da Lai Thiet Han Tu Tu Luong

Buddha became the Patriarch due to factors.

Translated means: The door we enter life is also the door we leave life. How many people live soberly, how many people become enlightened? A good man lies down at night thinking; Becoming a Buddha or becoming a Patriarch is also a leader (a creator).

Buddha or Patriarch also comes from people who practice. As one is born, so one will die. Do not wish to cut off samsara, do not wish to end the path of birth and death, but on the contrary, wish to follow the flow of life and flow, do not wish to go against the flow of birth and death, therefore there is ignorance.

After ignorance comes action. What behavior? It is an act that belongs to male and female characteristics. Because he was not wise, he created karma, then went crazy. From the insanity, action arises, action arises, then consciousness arises. When there is consciousness (with the father's semen and mother's blood to form the fetus), there is name and form (name is psychological, form is physiological). After name and form there are the six senses (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind). Having all six senses, after ten months it is born, and from this moment there is contact - the feeling of contact, knowing how to distinguish cold, hot, hard, soft. Emotions cause the effect of receiving, and receiving in favorable circumstances causes pleasure, in adverse circumstances it causes pain, so depending on the time and situation, there are feelings of love and hate. If you have a mind to receive, you will have a mind of love. If you have love, you will have a private mind to possess for yourself. People are greedy for wealth and beauty, so they have desires. Having a loving mind means you will find every way to take it back (attachment), make it your own, that is, existence. Because the goal must be achieved, there is a tendency not to give up any means, thus creating three impure karmas, that is, the karmas of body, speech and mind.

Because of creating karma, there is the fruit of life in the next life, then old age, death, and living beings continue to flow like that without stopping, with no way to escape the samsara cycle of birth and death. If you want to overcome birth and death, you must first eliminate ignorance. If ignorance is resolved, there will be nothing left to give birth to the following eleven causes and conditions. That is the true method to eliminate birth and death.

Cultivators must eliminate love and desire to be able to resolve their life and death problems. Otherwise, cultivating for all future lives will not achieve liberation. If you destroy the root of ignorance, then you will be able to eliminate lust, then there will be no more desires, no more afflictions, that is liberation.

Through the Pratyekabuddha Dharma, practitioners must live alone, should not have friends or form cliques. There is a saying: "Sweep all dharmas, separate all appearances," Only by destroying all attachments can liberation be possible. If you become a monk but are still afraid of loneliness, you cannot practice. Cultivation must stand up for oneself, not following others, that is the identity of a cultivator.

Practitioners must remember carefully, they cannot mingle with polluted elements, let gold and brass mix together, that will only cause them to fall. Practitioners must also solve problems for themselves. Whoever eats will be full, and cannot rely on others. Of course, practitioners also need good knowledge to enlighten and guide them on the right path, otherwise the blind will lead the blind and cannot find the way.

Cultivators must know how to endure things that are difficult to endure, give others what others cannot, eat things others cannot eat, wear things others do not want to wear, in short, practitioners must try to endure what others cannot bear. A practitioner must observe the precepts and keep the rules, otherwise he is not a practitioner.

III. The Bodhisattva's practice of the Six Paramitas.

Chữ Bồ-tát là tiếng Phạn, nói cho đủ là Bồ-đề tát-đỏa, dịch nghĩa là giác hữu tình hay hữu tình giác. Enlightenment is enlightenment, sentient beings are sentient beings; So the above noun means enlightenment of all sentient beings, and also means an enlightenment among sentient beings. Sentient beings achieve enlightenment, then use enlightenment wisdom to guide all sentient beings to enlightenment and this is also the meaning of sentient beings.

Bodhisattva is self-benefiting others, self-saving others, self-enlightening others, meaning benefiting oneself, benefiting others, helping oneself, enlightening others, enlightenment for oneself, enlightenment for others. I have been enlightened, I have led others to enlightenment, I have achieved liberation, and I vow to lead others to liberation. That is the spirit of Bodhisattva. The Bodhisattva's mind is open, unlike the mind of an Arhat, as in the sentence: "Maha-sattva is unforgiving, Amitabha Buddha and his ancestors," Mahasattva also wore it, Amitabha Buddha also wore it. The Bodhisattva's mind is compassion, "unconditioned great compassion, great compassion," single-mindedly concerned for sentient beings, not tired of worrying about how all sentient beings can be happy and free from suffering.

No matter what method we practice, we need to put effort into it honestly, don't be greedy for shortcuts, to go quickly, to try to choose a better or easier way, those are just tricks. Cultivators need to truly practice, not practice today, rest tomorrow, never achieving anything, but must work hard every day, try diligently every day, to get results. To put it bluntly, even though you work hard every day, progress is not necessarily guaranteed. People say: "Cultivation of the Way is like climbing hundreds of red branches, the bottom is simple, the top is difficult," Cultivating the Way is like climbing a hundred meter high pole. Going down is easy, going up is difficult.

What is called six degrees?

giving

maintaining the precepts,

patience,

diligence,

meditation,

wisdom.

Giving the power of greed, maintaining the precepts of mistakes, patience of anger, diligence of laziness, meditation of distraction, wisdom of stupidity. Everyone who develops the Bodhi mind and practices the Bodhisattva path must practice these six methods; When merit is complete, you will reach the other shore (the shore).

giving: Giving money and Dharma to others is called giving. giving has three types: One is the gift of wealth, two is the gift of Dharma, and the third is the gift of fearlessness. Giving is also divided into internal and external finances. Internal resources are the head, eyes, brain, and marrow. Foreign wealth is a stronghold, a country and a wife and children. Like our body, any part of this body, given to those who need it; Your country, your beautiful wife, your smart children, also give to others, give up your internal wealth, and give up your external wealth, this is called true giving. True giving is giving up one's own things to create good merit, called "rejoicing merit," that is talent.

Dharma giving is giving Buddha Dharma, such as preaching sutras and preaching, printing sutras, circulating sutras, translating sutras, these kinds of merits. Like us, if we are not lazy to pray for peace, we can use the giving method. If we do not have enough strength for wisdom, we use our labor to give, such as giving our strength to do things to help the needy, that is also considered Dharma giving. In short, if you have money, then help with money, if you have strength, then help with strength, to contribute part of your contribution to the general development of Buddhism.

Fearless giving is helping those who are in a state of fear, or are oppressed by circumstances, and cannot eat or sleep peacefully. At that time, it is necessary to help them find a bright path, to help them escape from fear, perhaps through comforting words, or through intervention to directly solve the problem that causes fear.

Knowing giving means not having greed. Greed is dirty glue, not daring to let go of anything. People say: "If you let go, you will have it; if you don't let go, you won't have it." Look at how many rich people and tycoons there are in the world, why do they have so much money? Because in their previous life they gave and helped others in poverty, now their merits have accumulated so in their present life they enjoy wealth.

In the past, Patriarch Maha Kassapa, every time he went begging for alms, he often went to poor houses to create karma. For what reason? Patriarch said: "For poor people, it is necessary to teach them the practice of giving. Give them the opportunity to sow blessings fields so that in their next life they will enjoy rich rewards." The Venerable Subhuti specialized in going to rich people to create charms every time he went begging for alms. Why? The Venerable's reason is as follows: "For rich people, we must help them continue to sow good roots. If not, their blessings will decrease and their next life will be poor. If they keep making offerings the Three Jewels, their precious blessings will never end." The two Venerable Ones just mentioned each had a different opinion, so each had their own method to educate sentient beings. In short, when you have no intention for yourself, it is true giving.

maintaining the precepts: Practitioners must strictly adhere to precepts. Precepts are five precepts:

Don't kill. People who do not kill will receive the reward of long life and less illness.

No robbery. If you don't steal other people's things, others won't steal yours. That is the law of cause and effect.

Bodhisattva Manjushri had a pair of shoes, and one day he said to everyone as follows: "For countless eons, I have never taken from anyone a blade of grass, a tree, a needle, or a thread. So, no one can touch anything we have. If you don't believe me, leave these shoes outside the city gate for three days. If anyone takes them away, this will prove that I lied." Sure enough, three days later, the shoes were still intact outside the city gate. Thus, we see how pure the Bodhisattva's maintaining the precepts of robbery is!

No adultery. A practitioner cannot have thoughts of adultery, that is

lustful thoughts. If you still have a little thought of lust, you will never go beyond the three worlds, you must still circulate forever in samsara of birth and death, because thoughts of lust are the root of birth and death. If we can eliminate it, then we can leave the three worlds and attain Buddhahood. Therefore, practitioners must definitely stop having lustful thoughts. How can it stop? First of all, you should not eat things rich in nutrients, because the practitioner's body is not lacking in nutrients, so there is no need to absorb more nutrients. Eat more, desire more; If there are too many nutrients, it gives rise to lustful thoughts. If you want to not have lustful thoughts, you have to moderate your food, don't crave good food, don't crave too much food, and practice enough to maintain your life. That's the secret of a practitioner. If not, we bring delicious dishes including mountain and seafood to make offerings to the temple of the five internal organs, then this is truly a disaster that leads to breaking the precepts of lust.

Don't lie. If you don't say anything, don't say anything. If you do say something, you must say the truth, absolutely do not lie or deceive others. No matter what situation we are in, we must speak honestly and constantly control our words so as not to lie.

Don't drink alcohol. Monks cannot drink alcohol (including poisons, narcotics, and tobacco). The reason is that alcohol has the effect of losing reason, making people unable to control their emotions, creating crazy karma. Toxic drugs also have the effect of making the mind foggy, that is, losing right knowledge and right view. That is the harm of alcohol and smoking.

The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a place that offers many means to help people practice the Way. If there is no greed, there will be no suffering. If you don't fight, fight for fame, fight for profit, fight for money, fight for beauty, don't fight for anything, then there will be no afflictions. If you don't pray, don't ask for anything, then there will be no false thoughts. Human desires never stop, the more they want, the more they want. If you reach the level of "don't ask, don't worry" How peaceful it is! as in the sentence: "Humanity does not seek pride." If you don't take care of yourself and take care of yourself, then any action you take will be taking care of others. If you are not selfish, everything will be for the benefit of others, not for yourself, and if you use such effort to cultivate the path, you will attain Buddhahood in the future.

You must follow those dharmas and practice diligently! Don't abandon the roots and follow the branches, running to search for magical dharmas and secret dharmas. The more you search for the dharma, the farther it goes, meaning "apostasy, child holding on," Turn your back on religion and run. The Dharma is right in front of you, so why should you leave the close and go looking for the far away? If you know, then right there, anywhere, at all times is a wonderful dharma, also a secret dharma. If you don't practice, no matter where you search, you won't be able to find the true Dharma. It's just a waste of time and won't bring you anything useful.

Ancient Duc said:

Personality is difficult and difficult to overcome

Buddha's dharma is difficult to write, golden text is written

Test your body's direction and balance

How to direct Ha Sinh to test the body?

Translated means:

A human body that was difficult to obtain has now been obtained.

The Buddha's Dharma was difficult to hear, but now it is heard.

This life does not care about saving this body.

So when will I be able to save this body?

Now we have a human body, if we don't borrow this body to practice, then when will we wait? Wait until you lose your human life, then it will be too late to practice. We must truly practice, practice seriously, with all our passionate attachment, our mood must be as urgent as if our bodies were at the bottom of an abyss, like the feelings of someone who feels each step on thin ice. Before birth and death are finished, there is no time left for laziness to sleep; When not enlightened, anyone has no right to arbitrarily let loose and abandon all regulations. Not keeping the precepts means going against Buddha's regulations. When preparing to enter Nirvana, Buddha told his disciples as follows:

"After I enter nirvana, all my disciples must take Paradita as their teacher."

If you don't strictly adhere to your precepts, you won't be able to achieve anything! We are determined to keep the rules every hour, every moment, we cannot laugh or talk, we cannot be careless in our behavior, we cannot be arbitrary, we must take the precepts as our teacher.

People in this world create evil karma because they do not observe the precepts. If you don't keep your precepts, you won't be afraid of anything, you won't be afraid of cause and effect, you won't be afraid of retribution. They even believe that there is no cause and effect of retribution, so they are free to do reckless things, creating evil karma, such as arbitrarily killing, stealing, committing adultery, lying, drinking alcohol, all without restraint, creating many karma sins, and then finally receiving the full retribution.

Why do people create evil karma? Due to the lure of society in the flashy outer shell. Seeing people being rich and living a life of enjoyment, immediately gives rise to greed and desire. Who knows that wealth comes from people's cultivation, but greedy people don't cultivate, don't plant good roots, only think wrongly and want to enjoy it. From the desire to enjoy, there is no trick to appropriate, thus giving birth to karma. When you have caused karma, not only will you not enjoy anything, but you will also receive full retribution, even when you receive retribution, you still do not know how to repent. It's okay to have no shame, but instead blame God and others, say God is unfair, people are unfair, and blame all the sins on others. These types of people, who do not know how to reflect, do not know how to examine themselves, are pitiful!

Those who uphold the precepts, "the evil ones do not act, the good ones serve them," And people who do not maintain the precepts do the opposite. Good and evil are there. Going against the rules, ignoring cause and effect, not believing in the Three Jewels, undermining the Mahayana - these are karma sins caused by not maintaining the precepts. Looking at it this way, we see how important maintaining the precepts is. A practitioner, no matter how he practices, if he does not maintain the precepts, there is no need to discuss it, because then there is no hope of attaining enlightenment.

Patience: At any time, in any place, we must maintain patience. With anyone, about anything, you must be patient. Patience means not being angry, not giving rise to afflictions. Regardless of the situation, you must keep your mind free from attachments and follow nature.

Rings come in three types:

Birth ring: Whether you encounter favorable or unfavorable circumstances, at any time, do not be moved. This is possible thanks to the power of concentration. If you reach the level of being motionless and ever-clear, then the practice of patience has reached the state of pure fire (burning green fire).

Dharma ring: To study Buddha Dharma, you must have patience. Didn't you just hear that the Buddha Dharma is very broad and then complain that the Buddha Dharma is as wide as the ocean? How long will it take to study it? Then because of that, he became discouraged and refused to learn any dharma. Actually, no matter how much or how little the method, we should be patient and learn gradually. "Immeasurable teachings of Dharma" That must be it! Don't think that the sutras have three collections of twelve sutras and eighty-four thousand dharmas, then from then on you won't learn any dharma, and you'll miss out on the opportunity to become a Buddha. This is the manifestation of a mind without dharma patience. It should have the following spirit: No matter how many or few Dharma methods there are, learn as much as you can, learn as much as you can understand, as much as you can understand. You must follow it with all your might, not do it reluctantly. No one tells us to study everything, no one tells us to understand everything, so what is there to be afraid of? If you don't study or abandon the Dharma without mercy and are doomed to fall, it's truly a pity!

Non-birth dharma forbearance: Not seeing the birth of the dharma, not seeing the cessation of the dharma, in the mind is patience, facing the mindless environment, facing the mindless dharma, that is to attain the patience of the non-birth dharma. Dharma is neither born nor destroyed, Buddha is neither born nor destroyed. We practice to reach perfection, liberation, that is, to the place of neither birth nor death, so we need to practice patience. The method of patience is used to test how well our patience is practiced. People who cultivate the Way not only have the ability to be patient, but are also able to endure in situations where they cannot be patient, and that is called true patience.

Diligence: It means not being lazy, not being lazy. People cultivating the path must constantly be diligent, every hour and every hour. Be diligent day by day, be diligent by night, be diligent day and night in the six times. The body is diligent, the mind is also diligent, absolutely do not relax, nor be sometimes enthusiastic and sometimes depressed.

Most people in the world do not have a positive spirit and often waste time. Each individual, from early morning, starting from the moment he wakes up, has to work hard until evening, just to take care of three meals. If that were all, then life would have little value, life would have no meaning, and there would be no distinction between life and death. It is truly "execution of humiliation," just corpses and piles of meat walking around. Think about it! What do we live for? To use our wisdom to help those who do not have wisdom; use our strength to help those who have no strength; Use our six complete faculties to help those whose six faculties are not complete. We must not only love sentient beings of the same kind, but also love sentient beings of different species. We must first be wise, we must educate those who are not wise, so that they do not do foolish things. To serve sentient beings we live this life. Oh! That spirit is truly great!

The mind is diligent, to seek Buddha's way; Be diligent to save sentient beings. People cultivating the Way must be diligent like that! As for diligence for self-interest, diligence for self-benefit, you cannot attain Buddhahood. Please remember carefully! We cannot arbitrarily let time pass by indifferently, nor should we feel guilty and admit that we cannot reach our destination, but must understand the meaning: "One part plowing, one part harvesting."

Practitioners do not talk about comfort, do not talk about enjoyment, just focus on practicing courageously, diligently, being very positive towards everyone, never showing negativity. Don't be greedy for enjoyment, but must shoulder hardships and make efforts for the sake of Buddha's teachings. Therefore, the Golden Mountain Temple is a refrigerator, the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is an ice warehouse. The refrigerator is small, the ice storage is large.

Practicing in the ice warehouse, uplifting the spirit, leading everyone, not lagging behind. If you are lazy at the ashram, all your merits will be wasted. Wrong knowledge and wrong views are a sin. Knowing clearly that you are wrong but still finding a way to justify it is truly unforgivable. Having wrong knowledge and wrong views is simply due to lack of diligence, so much precious time turns out to have been spent cultivating false thoughts!

Diligence, that is not telling you to eat to be diligent. When eating, you eat more than everyone else, when working, you lose to everyone! This is diligence, not telling you to sleep to be diligent. They haven't gone to sleep yet, you went to sleep first, they woke up, you woke up last! Nor do we tell you to be diligent in seeking fame and diligence in seeking profit. True diligence is diligence in developing the mind of great Bodhi, diligence towards the unsurpassed path of Bodhi. You must be diligent in the right places. You can't arbitrarily and only strive for what benefits you. That's a huge mistake. Regarding this point, let's make a clear assessment so that we don't regret it for the rest of our lives.

meditation: The Sanskrit word is meditation-na, translated as meditation. Stillness means quietness, stopping, hesitation means contemplation. Meditation is to calm down the delusions of consciousness, restoring the inherent purity of the true mind. meditation-na is also translated as practice of thinking; Thinking means thought, the cessation of thought is called concentration. meditation is Sanskrit, concentration is Chinese, it is a noun compounded from two original words Sanskrit and Chinese.

Our false thoughts, thoughts shifting, thoughts continuing continuously, if not good thoughts, then evil thoughts; If it's not right mindfulness, it's wrong mindfulness, the two things contradict each other. So if there is war inside, it will inevitably affect the outside, becoming war between people, between one family and another, between one country and another, even between this world and that world, between this planet and that planet. More broadly, there can be war between this galaxy and that galaxy. Analyze carefully, war is caused by our delusions. Those false thoughts are thoughts, "the thoughts that arise are all things accomplished, the thoughts that point to all things are nothingness," Or as the ancients say: "The mind only contemplates true wealth, desire destroys the true field of blessings," That's clearly the case, it comes from experience.

Why do we give rise to false thoughts? Because the "self" it's evil. Having a self gives birth to the idea of self-interest. If there is self-interest, there should be self-interest, these two are equal in class, they are a perfect pair. Because of self-interest and self-interest, the mind of desire arises. When there is a need, greed immediately arises, and following it closely is anger, following anger is ignorance, they keep following each other without leaving a step. They are the things that cause storms, clouds of smoke, and create an extremely chaotic and confusing situation that is difficult to save.

As practitioners, we must stop the thoughts of competition, greed, desire, selfishness, self-interest, and lying; we cannot let them operate freely. At that time, wisdom appears, its radiance shines to eliminate ignorance and darkness, that is, the state of clear mind and enlightenment, the purpose of our practice.

Calm meditation is to calm down the impurities of the mind. Cultivation of thinking means not leaving thoughts, not forgetting to study. Like greed in the first line, every hour is every moment of greed, there is no hour or moment that is not greed. Hua Dau is not used for reciting but for greed. For example, greed for the sentence "Who is Buddha?", is greed for the word "who." Finally, who is it? Find the "who." When to find "who" then enlightenment occurs. If you can't find it yet, don't be discouraged, just keep trying to find it. When finding "who," Then the inside no longer knows this body and mind, the outside no longer knows the world, everything is empty.

In the end, nothingness no longer exists, so where is there still attachment? At that time, I suddenly understood everything, had great enlightenment, flowing water and rocks appeared, seeing the true nature of all things. Remember this well! Don't let the situation happen in the middle of the road and give up, refuse to move forward, but must step forward, diligently diligently until the mountain and water end, at which time a transformation occurs, bringing the practitioner back to his eternal homeland.

Taking meditation is "taking" the root of birth and death. Suddenly the roots are cut off, the practitioner immediately crosses the threshold of life and death to return to freedom. During meditation, even though the wind blows and the rain falls, the practitioner is still single-minded, concentrating all his spirit on "greed". the word "who." If you push your efforts to the extreme, you will reach a state of immobility and clarity. That is when wrong knowledge and wrong views hide to make room for right knowledge and right view to appear. That is the power of meditation, its wonderful effects are truly inconceivable.

Each of us individually has boundless delusions. False thoughts flutter like dust particles in the void: Normally our eyes cannot see, but when sunlight passes through, we clearly see each dust particle, seeing them suddenly fly up, suddenly fly down, nothing is certain. Our delusions are the same, we cannot observe them, but with the light of the Buddha's teachings illuminating them, they will reveal their true form. What to do if you have false thoughts? Must sweep them clean. What method to use? Use meditation. Meditation practice will help us eliminate delusions. Practicing meditation requires diligence and patience. After that, further help from giving and maintaining the precepts is needed to complete the mission. These things must all support meditation, so that the practitioner can absorb the body and mind without giving rise to delusions. Even though they are six items and six degrees, they are interrelated, one must support the other.

People who practice religion must have eyes to investigate dharma, knowing clearly what is good dharma and what is evil. This point must be firmly grasped. As for the good dharma, "good beings obey" With evil dharma, "evil beings act." If there is no clear distinction, then right and wrong are not clear, which means it is against the Tao. How to have the eyes of wisdom to investigate the Dharma? The essential thing is to meditate and practice concentration, and use your efforts to the extreme, then wisdom will naturally appear. If you have the wisdom of observing, you can distinguish everything.

Wisdom: First is maintaining the precepts, then cultivating concentration. Only with meditation can there be true wisdom. Everyone who sincerely meditates and meditates, their wisdom mostly has right knowledge and right view. People who don't make the effort to practice meditation, sit still and meditate just for the sake of it. They also have a little wisdom, but most of them have wrong knowledge and wrong views. Why? Because it lacks the basis of wisdom. Wrong knowledge and wrong view is the wisdom of the world, right knowledge and right view is Buddha knowledge.

Is there any way to distinguish between wrong knowledge and wrong views? There are the following six standards:

A. First of all, try to see if someone has the mind to compete for fame and profit. He works hard for fame and fortune, is greedy for wealth and beauty, and is insatiable with greed.

B. Notice if they "polish" themselves. for them? Do they praise themselves? exaggerate yourself?

C. Do they devalue others to enhance their status? As for these people, there is no need to ask to know that they are definitely people with wrong knowledge and wrong views.

D. Consider again whether they are greedy for anything? Talking about people leaving the home life, they eat one meal a day, but there are also people who do not follow this rule and automatically go to the store to buy food. That person has the desire to eat, so the desire for form certainly cannot be abandoned. Just think about it, those actions are all selfish. In general, everyone is selfish, that is, they have greed.

E. Then try to see if they have a mind of self-interest and self-interest?

F. See if they like to lie? If so, they belong to the category of wrong knowledge and wrong views, there is no doubt about it.

Using the six criteria above as a test, you can know whether someone has right knowledge and right view, or belongs to the category of wrong knowledge and wrong view. In short, if everything is drawn to oneself, then that is the type of wrong knowledge and wrong views. If everything is for the happiness of the masses, then that person has right knowledge and right view.

If you want to clearly recognize these six conditions, you must have wise eyes and know the Dharma. Through concentration, wisdom arises. Only after having wisdom can we believe the truth. If it fits the truth, then follow it. If it doesn't fit the truth, no matter who the speaker is, he or she cannot be trusted. There is a sentence: "The right way is to advance, the wrong way is to retreat." Don't follow blindly, don't practice blindly, otherwise it will not only be unhelpful but also harmful.

The world's religions are unified, there should be no division

However, I have not yet told you about the benefits of listening to sutras. Listen to the sutras to understand the truth clearly. Any principles that are not understood will be clarified. Once you understand, then you can practice according to the Dharma and achieve true happiness. Following the four steps of Faith, Understanding, Virtue, and Evidence sequentially, you will have a chance to reach the goal.

If we understand this problem, we must value Buddhism, must support Buddhism, and make Buddhism grow stronger and more glorious every day. Continuing the blessings of Buddhism is the responsibility of Buddhist followers.

Any religion aims at the happiness of sentient beings, not causing trouble. Regarding any religion, we are not prejudiced and never criticize other religions for not being as noble as Buddhism. We must take the phrase "pure path, no overlap" As a principle, we must study the meaning of religions, to know what our strengths and weaknesses are, choose what is good to promote, to follow, otherwise we will be eliminated over time.

Someone asked me: "What religion do you belong to?" I said I belong to the religion of truth, the religion of people, the religion of sentient beings, the religion of the masses. Because sentient beings are humans, humans can become Buddhas, so Buddhism is the religion of humans, that is, the religion of sentient beings.

Buddhism covers the ends of space, all dharma realms. We must accept that all religions are part of Buddhism and are a part of Buddhism. However, religions do not admit that, it is their own matter, we do not have to discuss it. What is needed is for us to expand our minds to include all things. Destroying emptiness and transforming the dharma realm are all manifestations of the truth. Please pay attention! From now on we will not differentiate between this religion and that religion. They make distinctions but we don't make distinctions, we must have such a heart to have happiness in all directions, otherwise, "he says he's good, she says she's good," Arguing together is no good. Truth is not afraid of challenges, the more science advances, the more clearly it proves the truth of Buddhism. People often say: "Pure gold is not afraid of the fire of the furnace," The more you practice, the brighter and more beautiful the water becomes.

tieu_de: Where Dharma Abides
tom_tat: The water of the Ni-la River still flows every day; The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas still preaches the Dharma every day. Because I wish for the Dharma to remain in the world, I wish to transform the end times to become the Dharma, so I have to preach the sutras and preach the Dharma every day...
noi_dung:
Where Dharma Abides

The water of the Ni-la River still flows every day; The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas still preaches the Dharma every day. Because we pray for the Dharma to remain in the world, and we pray to change the end times to become the Dharma, we must preach the sutras and preach the Dharma every day without any pause. To continue the Buddha's life, to propagate Buddha's teachings to glory, to spread the Dharma throughout the world, to bring many living beings many benefits, the Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must stand up to act as Buddha and accept this responsibility. Therefore, the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is the ashram of the Dharma in this world.

Everyone who resides in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must have profound good roots, otherwise they will not be able to reside in this place. Having such good circumstances, we must try to cultivate the Dharma and work diligently to do Dharma work. We must strive to endure suffering, must have an unshakable spirit, must have an iron will, to be able to carry out religious work, and propagate the Dharma in all places, improving people's hearts, that is the mission of the Buddha's followers.

Some people, because their virtues are not enough and their good roots are still thin, after arriving at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, they are filled with delusions every day. They find it too miserable here. They eat only one meal a day, food is meager, the work is heavy, and the rules are strict. They feel they cannot stand it and finally cannot pass the test, so they change their mind and no longer stay, and have to leave this pure place.

The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is the place that turns the wheel of Dharma in the West. There is not a day that is not spent here. Despite the heavy rain and strong winds, we still diligently work on our religious work, never interrupting. People with a spiritual heart, coming here, feel like it is the right place they should go, while people without a spiritual heart coming to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas feel like they are sitting on a carpet of nails, never at peace. Two realms in the same place, just because the good roots are different, some are shallow and some are deep.

People in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas all have the ability to endure suffering, everyone develops Bodhi mind, because they are all true Buddhist followers. Every day they fight with hardships, forgetting themselves for the Dharma. People who specialize in translation work hard all day long, not for fame or profit. Nowadays, at the Avatamsaka Dharma Conference, every evening there is a lecture course on the Avatamsaka Mahayana Buddha

The Sutra (the Dharma Master Heng Sure preaches) never stops. That is the phenomenon of the Dharma remaining in the world.

Some people come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas and feel familiar, like returning to their own home, and do not want to leave. That is also because the Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is the ashram of the Dharma, the place where Dharma joy is abundant. The father of a monk here (lay practitioner Lieu) once said the following: "If you come to this Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, no matter how bad you are, you will become good. If you want to be bad, you can't do it anymore." Only someone with experience in society has to make such comments, which is truly precious!

From April 3 to 9, 1982, at the Ten Thousand Buddha Palace

tieu_de: Mindfulness Then Enlightenment, Enlightenment Then Instant Emptiness
tom_tat: Anyone who resides in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must sincerely practice the Way. Every moment and every moment, he must reflect back and examine his body and mind to see if he has violated the five basic precepts of killing, religion, lust, delusion, and alcohol. Be careful…
noi_dung:
Mindfulness Then Enlightenment, Enlightenment Then Instant Emptiness

Anyone who resides in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must sincerely practice the Way. Every moment and every moment, he must reflect back and examine his body and mind to see if he has violated the five basic precepts of killing, religion, lust, delusion, and alcohol. We must carefully observe the precepts, every hour and every moment, we must earnestly practice and take the story of the two practitioners who bowed in three steps, bowed in every three steps, as an example to learn. Every moment, every moment, you look at yourself, don't let false thoughts arise. There are also times when false thoughts come, but they immediately wake up, realize it is wrong, and immediately recall the false thoughts. "The beginning of mindfulness is enlightenment, the awakening is then emptiness," When you are enlightened and know, there is nothing more.

Why are there false thoughts? Because we have not broken the door of the six sense realms, which are sight, sound, smell, taste, touch and dharma. Therefore, the eyes are polluted by the objects of form, the ears are bewitched by the objects of sound, the nose is enticed by the objects of scent, the tongue is dictated by the objects of taste, the body is captivated by the objects of touch, the mind is moved by the objects of dharma, all are crazy by the six objects. If the mind is enlightened, the root of delusion can be removed. If the mind is not disturbed by the six sense objects, then one can attain Arhatship.

The person who has attained the first fruition, the eyes see form but can change physical objects, the ears hear sounds but can change clean objects, and the same goes for the other senses. The saying "not entering the taste, smell, or touch" meaning is not subject to any fluctuations. At that time, fame cannot be shaken, profit cannot be shaken; towards all things, the heart is not passive, as is the meaning of the sentence: "The eye sense of form and form has no internal existence, the ear hears and hears the mind without knowing," That is, the eyes see shapes but there is nothing inside, the ears hear things but the mind does not know. There is a sentence: Na-gia is always in concentration, without existence or time, there is never a time when external objects make the mind fluctuate, there is never a moment when he is fascinated by external circumstances.

When you reach this realm, you still have to work hard and cannot relax. If there is a bit of laziness, the old illness will recur, so those who practice the Way must continue to work hard, be courageous and diligent, only know how to practice, not give rise to false thoughts, that is the true way to apply effort.

There are people here who don't make the effort to practice and just follow others. That's just a dua. Seeing people chant Buddha, I also chant Buddha. Why should we chant Buddha? Don't know. Seeing people bowing to the Buddha, I also bowed to the Buddha, and then I didn't know why. As far as chanting sutras, reciting mantras, sitting in meditation, I basically don't understand the meaning at all. Such confusion is truly "unrealistic" What a waste of time. Cultivating religion like that, it's pitiful!

tieu_de: Sin Is So High, Repentance Is Gone
tom_tat: Translation: Sin arises from the mind and takes repentance from the mind. If the mind is destroyed, there will be no sin. The mind forgets, sins are eliminated, both are empty. That is called true repentance
noi_dung:
Sin Is So High, Repentance Is Gone

Repentance is an opportunity for the transgressor to repent and make amends. There is a sentence:

The sin of obedience gives rise to the mind of repentance.

When the weak mind is destroyed, sin disappears.

The mind of death and sin is destroyed by two sentences: no.

Market name because of repentance foot.

Translation: Sin arises from the mind and takes repentance from the mind. If the mind is destroyed, there will be no sin. The mind forgets, sins are eliminated, both are empty. That's called repentance.

After repentance, you will never do it again. If you repentance and then commit a crime, then repentance commits a crime again, then it's just a child's joke and has no use. Repentance must be formal, not just say the word repentance in front of everyone and immediately the crime will disappear. It's not that simple, only stupid people think that way. After repentance, you must make vows: "Everything from before is as dead as yesterday, from now on everything is as new." and absolutely do not commit it again in the future, only then can the karma crime be eliminated.

If you repentance without sincerity and good intentions, the crime will not go away but will only get worse. Why? Knowing the precepts and breaking the precepts will increase the crime to one level. If the crime increases to the extreme, it means falling into the endless hell to suffer countless kinds of suffering, forever unable to change the body, which is very dangerous. Gentlemen! You must honestly admit your mistakes, and wholeheartedly make amends. Quickly repent of past mistakes, don't do it lightly like a child's game. I'm not here to make fun of you! Must understand clearly!

tieu_de: Place of Refuge for World Religious Believers
tom_tat: The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is the place where world Buddhism originated, and is also where world Buddhism returned to its source. Avatamsaka Sutra says: "There is nothing that does not originate from this Dharma Realm, there is nothing that does not...
noi_dung:
Place of Refuge for World Religious Believers

The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is the place where world Buddhism originated, and is also where world Buddhism returned to its source. Avatamsaka Sutra says: "There is nothing that does not flow from this Dharma world, there is nothing that does not return to the Dharma world." One root radiates thousands of branches, ten thousand branches return to the root, so the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is the place of return for Buddhist followers around the world. Regardless of whether they belong to Buddhism, or Christianity, Christianity, Islam, Judaism, whoever comes will not stop, whoever goes will not keep, whoever wants to come can just come, whoever wants to go can just go, the Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas will forever leave the gate wide open.

The word "Van" of the Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, speaks of immeasurable meanings. The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is not afraid of many people, nor is it afraid of few people. Now there are ten thousand Buddhas coming to the Bao Dien, in the future the world's religious figures will also come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, so there have been plans for the hall to accommodate up to thousands of people. Currently, the rice hall only has enough room for five hundred people to eat rice at the same time. Therefore, when there is a large Dharma conference, it often happens that there is no room to eat rice (because it is too noon to eat). Therefore, it was necessary to build a hall to accommodate about two thousand people.

The above project is still small, next there will be a large project. In the design program, there is a plan to build the Hoa Nghiem Chanh Dharma Hall, which can accommodate ten thousand people to listen to the Dharma, and be a place to practice the Dharma for ten thousand people. There is also a plan to build the Dai Hung Bao Dien and the Stupa, with a large lake to release animals. The works of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas are endless. The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas opened the mountains and mountains to become a place of refuge for all followers of the world's religions.

Someone said: "Dear magician! Expanding that way would cost a lot of money! Is that going to target us lay people to create favorable conditions?" You can rest assured! I have never bewitched anyone before, so don't be afraid. If you don't believe it, just take it easy, otherwise you'll be blamed later. Anyone who is not afraid of gaining merit should support the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. I would like to tell you frankly, if I say I do something, I will do it, absolutely no empty words. Those who are afraid of being charmed, please leave the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas early. As for me, I will definitely create a place for followers of world religions to return and take refuge.

tieu_de: One Mindfulness of Ignorance Is Falling Samsara
tom_tat: People in the world are all living in a state of dreaming and dying, never waking up to find a way out of samsara. From beginningless time until now, sentient beings are driven by ignorance, walking in the six paths of samsara, living, dying, dying...
noi_dung:
One Mindfulness of Ignorance Is Falling Samsara

People in the world are all living in a state of dreaming and dying, never waking up to find a way out of samsara. From beginningless time until now, sentient beings are driven by ignorance, traveling in the six realms of samsara, living and then dying, dying and then living, wandering up and down without limit.

Life is like a drama. In opera, sometimes he plays the role of king, enjoying glory and wealth; Sometimes he plays the role of a beggar, suffering all kinds of hardships. When you are an emperor, you don't know the hardships of being a beggar; Beggars don't know the joy of being king. The scenes of joy and joy passed by in the blink of an eye, like a spring dream.

Does your karma increase more or less? Not knowing. How much virtue can we cultivate? Not knowing. Not knowing is ignorance, ignorance is the root of birth and death. If there were no ignorance, there would no longer be suffering in samsara. Our goal in cultivating the path is to destroy ignorance, transform consciousness into wisdom, transform alaya consciousness into Great Perfection wisdom.

People have human ignorance, animals have animal ignorance, up to hungry ghosts and hell beings, each species has its own ignorance. In ignorance, living beings search for a way out (out of the three worlds), but the more they search, the more confused they become. They cannot find a way, and still suffer in samsara. Why? Because the mind is mischievous, and does not know how to use the true mind (wisdom) to find a way out.

Ignorance means no wisdom. People without wisdom no matter what they do, they do it in insanity, using wrong as right and vice versa. Knowing clearly what is wrong but still doing it is only because ignorance obscures it and causes us to go astray. "Choose the thorny path" then you will never find the right path.

Those who study Buddha's teachings need to destroy this ignorance so that the nature of the Dharma can be revealed. Because of ignorance, we happily do foolish things. With these types of wrong knowledge and wrong views, self-centeredness and selfishness will arise and cause mischief, losing all fairness and impartiality. From then on, each birth is a downward spiral, until the end is the animal birth, either as an ant, or as a mosquito, at which point only a little awareness remains. Yet still greedy, insatiable with greed, still acting in confusion. You see! All types of animals have natures. Sentient beings inherently have Buddha nature, but not completely, for the reason that "nature turns into spirit," Therefore, they are stupid and often live in ignorance.

Although humans are called the spirit of all things and have wisdom, they create evil karma. Because ignorance obscures their wisdom, they act with false thoughts. There is a verse that talks about the effect of the 'mind', now I summarize it as follows:

Freemasons are like fathers

Please spread the word yourself

Fei Mao tried to start

Buddha's work was spared.

Translation:

The three dots are like stars

The hook curves like the new moon

Bring the feathers from here

Buddha City also came from there.

Freemasonry is like a father: On top of the word "mind" are three dots, like several stars in the sky lined up in a row.

Let's spread the word: Below the word "mind" is a curved hook, like the new moon on the third or fourth lunar day, lying curved in the sky.

Phi mao dong try to start: Flying feathers, small horns, wearing feathers and horns, refer to animals. It's all caused by psychological influences. Being a dog has the retribution of a dog, being a cat has the retribution of a cat, and the same goes for a horse, buffalo, goat, chicken, duck, or goose.

Buddha's work was spared: Becoming a Buddha, becoming a Patriarch, also comes from the mind, so it is said "necessarily created by the mind." Suffering in hell, enjoying blessings in heaven, all are created from thoughts in the mind.

If a good thought arises, the auspicious spirit will protect us. When evil thoughts arise, evil spirits and demons will immediately follow us. The ancients said: "One misstep, hate forever" as well as saying: "One wrong thought is eternal hatred." Good or evil are just a thought apart. Thinking good will go up, thinking evil will go down. The human mind is like a particle of dust, floating in the air, suddenly going to heaven, suddenly going to hell, suddenly an animal, suddenly a hungry ghost, never stopping to create karma and then receive the results, receive the results and then create karma, just like that, the cycle rotates.

When will we understand "the sea of suffering is boundless, turning around is the destination?" Knowing that the sea of karma is vast, without shore or shore, if you quickly turn around, you will reach the shore. Studying Buddha Dharma means learning this, besides that there is nothing magical about it. To put it more simply, breaking habits, breaking the mind of self-interest and self-interest, living without fighting, without greed, without seeking, means grasping the essence of Buddha's teachings.

Listening to the Dharma every day, you must understand the essential meaning of the Dharma. What is the most important part of the dharma? These are the points of not fighting, not being greedy, not seeking, not being selfish, not taking advantage, and not lying. These six standards are the standards that guide us every day in all our actions. If anything is not up to standard, we will know immediately so we can make changes. Correcting it so that it no longer makes mistakes is a merit, and then you are truly a follower of Buddhism. These are also the six principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, we hope that everyone will follow, everyone will be enlightened, everyone will become Buddha.

Life is like a dream, like a photo

There is a verse recited, very ethical, please read it now for reference:

Don't ask for the great path to emerge

Needy and talented women create strong men

Hundred years of light, sound, stone and fire

One's body comes from the water amulet

Use your assets to flatter your friends

Crimes are equally difficult

Interview with the golden pair of mountain music

impermanence will never return.

Do not seek the great path to emerge from the path of delusion (Do not seek the great path to get out of the path of delusion): Our life is like an illusion, like water bubbles, like mist, like lightning, we must contemplate it as such. Human life is impermanence, career impermanence, wealth impermanence, so "joy is the cause of suffering." All pleasures in this world also contain suffering. If you want to leave suffering and be happy, you must cultivate the Way. To cultivate the Way, you must first eliminate habitual tendencies. Except how? On the inside, be disciplined and obedient, on the outside, cut off desire and eliminate love. If both sides work together, you will surely succeed.

People are born by lust, die by lust, that is the common sense of the world, and according to the world, they live and die over and over again. The person leaving the home life goes the opposite way, only by going the opposite way can he become a saint, so what is good for the world is not good for the person leaving the home life; People in the world are greedy, we are not greedy; What the world loves, we do not love; What the world loves, we don't love. If you want to seek the great path, you must get out of the path of delusion.

What is sugar delusion? Because of ignorance, any direction you go in is confusing, and in the end you don't know what to do. Being confused also means losing direction, having to walk the path without realizing it, but getting lost somewhere else. You must know that if you don't seek the way, you won't get out of the path of delusion. If you want to get out of the path of delusion, you must practice the Way.

Cultivating the path requires good knowledge to enlighten your eyes. Good knowledge knows how to teach us how to practice so that we can end the path of birth and death, helping us not to return to samsara. The view and knowledge of good knowledge are correct, in which there is not the slightest bit of wrong knowledge or wrong view.

A needy mother and a talented husband? (If you leave your intelligence behind, you're not a man?): If we do not seek the way, if we do not get out of the path of delusion, we will surely betray our talent, our talent is also our wisdom and virtue. Buddha once said: "All sentient beings have the wisdom and virtue of the Tathagata." If we do not practice, we will not achieve anything. So we have abandoned our talented minds, which means we are no longer men?

Hundred years of light and sound of stone and fire mimic (The light and sound of the past hundred years passes like a flash of fire - from the ignition stone): For example, if you can live for a hundred years, the days and months will pass as quickly as a spark of lightning, extinguished in a flash.

One life's body is like water bubbles (One life, the body is like water bubbles): From birth to death is called a human life. This body is like a bubble on the surface of the water, floating, it is truly an illusion with nothing of substance, in just a moment it disappears. So why miss it? Are you so attached to it?

He had nothing to do with his fortune and his concubine (his property and wife were left behind, he had nothing): When it comes to death, no matter how much money you have, you cannot change your death. All the gold, silver, and jewels he left behind, not a single penny was taken away. At that time, his wife and property were no longer his, he only had his two hands hanging down to worship the King of Hell.

Sins follow the same pattern and are difficult to follow (Sins follow the pattern, one cannot deceive oneself): Any kind of karma, killing, stealing, adultery, lying, drinking alcohol, follows us like a shadow, as the saying goes: "You can't carry anything, only karma can carry you." Crime karma cannot be deceived, because we ourselves create it, so we must definitely receive the retribution, no one can receive it for us.

Question about the pair of golden mountains and mountains (Try to ask if gold is piled up to form a mountain):

Filled with gold and silver, high as a mountain, becoming a king of money and wealth

most people in the world, what is the use of those things when you die? If you leave it to your descendants, if your descendants know it, they won't need it. If your descendants are bad, they will use the money to create bad karma, which is even more serious.

Impermanence will never return (Can you buy the law of impermanence?): Although gold and silver are piled up as high as mountains, can we buy impermanence? Cannot be purchased. Impermanence ghosts are very fair, not biased, do not say favors, and do not accept gifts.

The situation of people in this world is like that. We are the people leaving the home life, that is, overcoming customs, refusing to be imprisoned by customs. If you don't practice seriously now, then when will you wait? We must remember that the goal of those leaving the home life is to end the path of birth and death, to overcome samsara, not to live like a worldly person. Gentlemen! "The general does not lower his horse, all of you are on your way," Please try your best to practice!

Ultimately What Is Religion?

If the Tao is spread out, it covers the six groups; if it is rolled up, it is hidden. The Tao is big, there is nothing outside it, and the Tao is small, there is nothing inside it. There is no individual who is not within the path, no living being can run outside the path. The Tao is the nature, and the nature is the basic essence of sentient beings. Buddha said: "All living beings have Buddha nature and can become Buddha." Regardless of the type, fetal birth, ovule birth, lower birth, transformed birth, birds, fish, animals, plants, in the above four species of birth or in the nine dharma realms of sentient beings (four births and nine existences), all have this complete path.

The Tao Te Ching says: "Sir Van Dao, dong er action chi. Sergeant, weak and weak. Corporal officer of literature, big joke. If you don't smile, you can't help but be virtuous." Lao Tzu talked about morality like that, and after studying it, I found it to be very reasonable. Brief explanation is as follows:

Sergeants write and follow the teachings (Seniors listen to the teachings, feel and follow them): A sergeant is a wise person, a person with deep good roots, a superior person. Hearing the Dharma is hearing the way to practice the Dharma. Confucius said: "Trieu Van Dao, passing away is possible," If you listen to the teachings early in the morning, you can die at night. You don't regret anything anymore. Why? By hearing the Dharma, one becomes enlightened and understands the Dharma. Everyone has it, no one does not have it, and will never leave the Dharma. It's just that we turn our backs on the path and run, and the more we run, the further away we are from the path. What is this religion? That's the rule. Following the rules means cultivating the Way. Not following the rules means not cultivating the Way. What are the rules? Those are precepts. Practicing according to precepts is cultivating the path.

Speaking from the root, the path is the path that leads to birth and death. Cultivating the Way means closing the door to life and death. What is the door of life and death? It is desire. Having a lustful mind is to open the door of birth and death; eliminating the lustful mind is to close the door of birth and death. High class people, when they hear about this religion, think: "?! That's the way it is!" Therefore, feel and follow, to return to the source, to reflect on yourself, to turn away from the mundane world and towards enlightenment, and to practice the path. From morning to night, practice there, like a chicken incubating eggs, like a dragon raising pearls, like a cat watching for mice, concentrating your mind to use your efforts. Just cultivate the Way with one heart, no other delusions.

Sergeant who listens to the teachings, weakly survives and perishes (Sergeant who listens to the teachings, sometimes lives and sometimes dies): This is the middle class, also a normal person. This type of mind is half wise, half foolish. After listening to this teaching, I seem to remember a little, and also seem to forget a little. In short, it is both right and wrong, nothing is certain. Sometimes they accept no, sometimes they accept yes, not decisively.

Corporal officer of literature, big joke. If you don't laugh, you can't help but follow the teachings (The corporal heard the teachings and burst out laughing. Not laughing is not called religion): Corporal refers to the stupid class. If we tell them that eliminating desires and cutting off cravings is cultivating the path, or that keeping rules is cultivating the path, they will immediately answer: "Hey! So that's stupid! You practitioners are truly stupid, why don't you want money, beauty, fame, food, drink, and sleep? That is the pleasure of the five desires, how enjoyable it is! Therefore, when they hear the Dharma, they laugh, thinking that cultivating the Dharma is stupid. If they don't laugh like that, it's not religion.

Every day I preach sutras and sermons to you, but it is still important to emphasize the eradication of lustful thoughts. The Shurangama Sutra says: "If lust is not eliminated, it will not leave this world." We must definitely eliminate thoughts of lust in order to leave the earthly world, so there is a saying: "The lustful heart is not broken, cooking sand to make rice, this cannot happen." Gentlemen! People who practice are not like people in the secular world. Whatever people in the world are greedy for, crave for, love, and like, we need to eliminate. There is a saying: "Escape from this world" That means everything from words to thoughts, practitioners and lay people are not the same. You must pay attention to this point, you cannot be contaminated by the secular stream.

Everyone who resides in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is determined to practice, to keep the rules, and to uphold the precepts. What's the point of leaving the home life if you don't keep the rules and precepts? leaving the home life and laying are not the same. If you leave the home life and still keep secular customs, what should you do when leaving the home life? This point must also be clearly understood.

Why is there an end of dharma? Because of the blessings of thin people, no saints were born, no Dharma remained in the world. I do not rely on my own strength, I am determined to maintain the Dharma in this world, to persevere and not give up in the face of all circumstances. Being so persistent takes effort, but that is my determination. No matter how difficult it is, I still have to complete my mission.

Gentlemen! You are all disciples following me to study Buddhism, so you understand what era this is? Must try to be an exemplary leaving the home life person, a super leader, cannot be contaminated by conventional wisdom, otherwise, the person leaving the home life cannot raise their head.

tieu_de: High Virtue Is Not Virtue, Lower Virtue Accepts Virtue
tom_tat: Ancient Duc said: "Highly virtuous is not virtuous, inferiorly virtuous, clinging to virtue, clinging to virtue, ignorant of morality." Now please explain the meaning
noi_dung:
High Virtue Is Not Virtue, Lower Virtue Accepts Virtue

Ancient Duc said: "Highly virtuous is not virtuous, inferiorly virtuous, clinging to virtue, clinging to virtue, ignorant of morality." Now please explain as follows:

Highly virtuous and unvirtuous: Practice the Bodhisattva path, but do not cling to any records, do good deeds but do not record the records of good deeds. "Virtuous practice of virtue," It's a natural thing, it's our duty, so nothing makes us more arrogant or complacent. It should not be said: "I do merits and blessings, I do good, I do good deeds," and even such thoughts should no longer exist.

People say: "Goodness, if you want to show it to others, is not true goodness; Evil and wanting people not to know is a great evil." A person who truly practices the Bodhisattva path does everything as well as he doesn't do it, everything is without attachment. Whatever merit you do, don't be attached to it, don't acknowledge any merit, and don't be arrogant or complacent towards anyone. That is the meaning of "highly virtuous, not virtuous."

People with true wisdom do not consider themselves wise. People with true morality do not admit that they are moral. A person with true education is not arrogant and does not look down on others. People who practice authentically, without complacency, propagate it for themselves.

Lower virtue and accept virtue: Some ordinary people, if they do a little good, they consider it a lot, wherever they go they advertise what they do, I do this good deed, I do that merit, wherever they go they point it out to deceive people, hoping others will appreciate them.

A virtuous person, although doing meritorious deeds, is not attached to merit. People with low virtue, even though they have done a little merit, are still attached to the merit. Wherever they go, they take advantage of the opportunity to propagate, "I created this pagoda, I built that tower, I printed this sutra, I preached the Dharma like that, in short, I can't run out of merit by talking all the time." That is the behavior of people who have low morals and cling to virtue.

Attachment to virtue: It means being attached to things, roughly

like: I build a bridge on this river, I pave that road, etc.

Moral ignorance: As above, there is no merit. Anyone who has such thoughts does not understand the true meaning of morality.

Self-propaganda for yourself, self-congratulation for yourself, this is a delusion. There is a saying: "Sentient beings do not have a true mind, because they have false minds," False thoughts are false thoughts. A moving thought, such as a thought about killing, or a thought about stealing, for example, is delusion. A thought about sex, lying, or drinking alcohol is all delusion. In general, thoughts that arise are false thoughts. False thoughts are obstacles for practitioners. How to prevent false thoughts from arising? You must meditate, chant sutras and mantras, concentrate your mind, and not have two thoughts in your mind. That is the way to guard against false thoughts.

Why Is It Not Compatible With The Way?

What is the reason for practicing for a long time and still not being in harmony with the religion? It's because of false thoughts. If the mind still has false thoughts, it will destroy morality, concentration, and wisdom. If a mind has delusions, maintaining the precepts is not solid, cultivating concentration is not solid, what can we say about wisdom. When false thoughts arise, the mind immediately follows the conditions and causes that move along with all things. Physical objects are received by the eyes, sounds are heard by the ears, scents are recognized by the nose, tastes are tasted by the tongue, touches are touched by the body, and dharmas are perceived by the mind, all of these combine to create all things. If you stay in the realms of the above things, you will run after all things, so from there, the mind of greed will arise.

In front of something that makes us feel happy in our hearts, greed will arise. Once you are greedy, you will think of a way to take over. After taking over, we still don't know enough, so our greed is still intact. Greed has no bottom, can never be filled with greed, so it is said: "Desire has no end." People who are greedy for money, when they have money, then become greedy for fame, fame, and other things, greedy for houses, greedy for cars, greedy for airplanes, greedy for motorboats, etc. It's all due to greed. If you pray but are not satisfied, troubles arise.
