When there is affliction, many false thoughts come rushing in. Having false thoughts means having sadness, causing the body to suffer, the mind to suffer, presenting before the eyes all kinds of junk and impure thoughts. The relationships mentioned above lead to a situation that is not in accordance with the path, does not lead to the end of the path of birth and death, so we keep wandering around in the six paths of samsara without thinking of a way out. The more you rotate, the further you go, getting lost deeper into the sea of suffering and unable to get out.

The essence of self-nature is the eternal path. What is called the eternal path? It is formless, formless, and has no specific shape. Understanding that way, you can reach that path. If you don't understand like that, you will go downhill every day. If you enlighten this path again, then wisdom will always appear, and the wonderful nature of true suchness will also appear, then it is called compatible with the path.

Why Does His Divine Power Not Show Up?

What is supernatural power? There is a saying: "Unpredictable magic is god, freedom and no hindrance is wisdom." Divine power is a free force, unhindered, unpredictable, it is a realm of countless changes, inconceivable. Where does divine power come from? Simply put, a person who practices the Hinayana method, specializes in cultivating the four truths and contemplating the twelve causes and conditions, when they reach the level of perfection, will then attain supernatural powers.

The supernatural powers of Arhats and Bodhisattvas are not the same. Arhat's divine power is limited, he can only know causes and conditions within the range of eighty thousand eons. Furthermore, they must pay close attention to see. The Bodhisattva's supernatural power has no limit, he can see the entire realm of motes, motes in realms, all Buddhas in countless realms (as many as motes) can hear all Buddhas in all over the same realms speaking the wonderful Dharma; can know all the thoughts of sentient beings in countless lands as numerous as dust particles; You can know causes and conditions beyond the scope of eighty thousand great eons, without needing to enter concentration, just having the thought of observation arise in your mind is enough.

Bodhisattvas who practice the Bodhisattva path, when their merit is complete, they will have the above types of supernatural powers. If we develop Bodhi mind, practicing the Bodhisattva path can also achieve this level of supernatural power. As long as you practice to perfection, you don't need to seek anything, you still have magical powers.

When having supernatural powers, shouldn't a Bodhisattva show off his supernatural powers? That's not true. If a Bodhisattva has supernatural powers, but does not manifest them, then what is the use of those supernatural powers? It is like a person who has a precious pearl but hides it in his clothes, not knowing that it is a priceless treasure. Resigned to poverty, having no food to eat, no clothes to wear, no shelter, but still not knowing how to exchange pearls for money to make ends meet. If you have supernatural powers but don't use them, it's the same.

If you don't have magical powers, you can't use them. That's no different from climbing a tree and catching fish, it's just a foolish person's fantasy. However, if you have magical powers, you must take advantage of them. Educating sentient beings, using miraculous powers to manifest, increasing sentient beings' confidence, thus multiplying the effectiveness. That is also called using skillful means. You should pay attention to this point! Demons also have magical powers, which can cause those who desire magical powers but do not have enough spiritual power to fall into their trap, to the point of destroying their demonic karma and becoming a relative of the demon king. Regarding this point, please pay special attention and cannot be careful.

Nowadays, there are some ignorant people, followers of Buddhism who don't understand anything, and when they see what people say, they do it. Regarding the principles of Buddha Dharma, they seem to know but do not know, do not know the source. Whenever they witness someone displaying supernatural powers, they immediately cry out in surprise: "In the end of the Dharma, people cannot have such magical powers!" To say so is so childish! To put it bluntly, that is the cause of falling into hell. For Buddha Dharma, it does not make any sense at all. Please pay attention! For any matter that we do not know clearly, we should not criticize nonsense, we cannot arbitrarily make decisions about this or that. If you go wrong with cause and effect, you will fall into hell.

Buddhism has true principles, has immutable laws from ancient times, has thousands of golden words spoken by the Buddha himself, derived from his own experience, not a morality that deceives oneself and others. The teachings spoken by the Buddha are the Sutra Pitaka, the teachings expressed by His body are the Vinaya Pitaka, the part commented on by Buddha's disciples is the Abhidharma Pitaka. The three Pitakas and twelve parts of the Sutra are the teachings of truth, the meaning is completely true without exaggeration.

Wherever the truth is, all Buddhas in the ten directions will come to support it. Wherever the truth is, Bodhisattvas from the ten directions come to support it. Wherever the truth is, the Heavenly Dragons and Eight Bodies come to support it. Understanding the truth is a true Buddhist follower; not understanding the truth is a misguided Buddhist follower. You must clearly receive the truth, you must clearly distinguish between right and wrong, don't be confused, believe whatever someone says, that is unacceptable.

Bodhisattvas have all kinds of supernatural powers, and how do they use them? In general, using magical powers as a skillful means to educate sentient beings, causing them to develop Bodhi mind so as not to be contaminated by the worldly stream. Just do whatever you hear, that's a foolish person, not only does not research the truth, but also follows evil paths, listens to evil dharma, slanders the true dharma, those types of Buddhist followers are truly pitiful.

Currently, it is the end of the dharma, there are many great dharmakaya beings, traveling on boats of compassion, to the Saha world to educate sentient beings, causing them to awaken, stay away from wrong knowledge and wrong views, and be close to right knowledge and right view. Buddha said the dharma is righteous dharma, demons said dharma is evil dharma. Following the teachings to practice, following the dharma to practice, strictly maintaining the precepts, practicing the precepts, that is the right dharma, otherwise it is the wrong dharma. Don't do anything that goes against precepts; If it is in accordance with the precepts, then do it with all your might. That is the path of the Bodhisattvas.

Bodhisattva's mind is absolutely not self-interested, absolutely does not care about fame. The Bodhisattva, with his heart of fervent compassion, sweetly coaxes and teaches sentient beings to leave suffering and reach a place of happiness. Bodhisattvas take the benefit of sentient beings as the starting point, not because of their own thoughts of benefit. That is the spirit of the Bodhisattva path. The Bodhisattva's practice does not come from his own feelings but from his compassion. The Bodhisattva's compassion is unconditional, compassion is the same great compassion, there is absolutely no distinction in his heart. Bodhisattva saves all sentient beings, not afraid of hardship, regardless of day or night, to save sentient beings from the ocean of suffering to achieve peace and happiness. Bodhisattvas consider saving sentient beings to be a must, so Bodhisattvas have supernatural powers.

Bodhisattvas have supernatural powers and can display them, so why can't people display their supernatural powers? This is a misunderstanding. Anyone who criticizes like that must have a different intention in their heart. People don't want the Dharma to exist, they don't want you extraordinary people among Buddhist followers to exist.

Currently, there are some followers of Buddhism who do not have wisdom. Wherever they go, they say that in this Dharma-ending age, one should not display magical powers, and no one should have supernatural powers. Why do they propagate like that? Because they are stupid, do not practice diligently, and are often jealous. They don't have magical powers, so they think that other people don't have magical powers either. Not only that, when they meet people with supernatural powers, they also don't recognize them. If a Bodhisattva meets a believer who has right knowledge and right view, and is diligently practicing, then he will show his supernatural powers, making the believer more confident, making them strive to practice the path to liberation.

You are knowledgeable! If there is anyone who has supernatural powers, no one else, if they show off their supernatural powers, I very much welcome them. If it is indeed a sin to say so, I would like to bear it alone. Even if I am sent to hell, I am willing. I bear it alone and have nothing to do with you, so don't worry. The only problem is that you don't have magical powers and can't show off. As for being able to demonstrate miraculous powers, I wholeheartedly support it.

The end of the Dharma really needs you to truly cultivate the Way, it really needs you to be enlightened, it really needs people to attain enlightenment. After achieving the results, I will return to lead my predestined friends, guiding them out of the Three Realms to the eternal realm of Eternal Light. That is my hope for you.

tieu_de: Shurangama Sutra: Symbol Of Dharma
tom_tat: The Buddhist scriptures are all important. The Shurangama Sutra is even more special. Wherever there is the Shurangama Sutra, there is Dharma. If the Shurangama Sutra no longer exists, then the dharma would end. We Buddhist followers...
noi_dung:
Shurangama Sutra: Symbol Of Dharma

The Buddhist scriptures are all important. The Shurangama Sutra is even more special. Wherever there is the Shurangama Sutra, there is Dharma. If the Shurangama Sutra no longer exists, then the dharma would end. We Buddhist followers must bring all our heart, sweat, and tears to support this sutra.

The Dharma Extinction Sutra says: "At the end of the dharma, the Shurangama Sutra will be destroyed first, followed by other sutras." If the Shurangama Sutra is not destroyed, then the Dharma will appear, so we Buddhist followers are determined to use our lives to protect, use our sweat and tears to protect, and use our will to protect the Shurangama Sutra. If the Shurangama Sutra lasts forever in the world, is widely promoted, circulates down to every grain of dust, spreads everywhere in the world, and reaches the ends of space throughout all dharma realms, if it can be like that, then the Dharma is truly bright and brilliant.

Why is it said that the Lang Nghiem Sutra destroys first? Because this sutra teaches very true principles. The demons of pagans couldn't bear it anymore so they found every way to sabotage the sutra and destroy this sutra. First of all, they claim that the Shurangama Sutra was not spoken by the Buddha himself, but was fabricated by later generations, so the Shurangama Sutra is a fake sutra, a pseudo-sutra. Those are the evil tricks of pagans, aiming to use forceful words to seize reason to destroy the Shurangama Sutra.

The Shurangama Sutra is Buddha's body, Buddha's relics, and Buddha's temple tower. In the Shurangama Sutra there are four types of pure teachings, there are twenty-five saints who narrate the experience of enlightenment and there are fifty realms of karma. These dharmas can be compared to a demonic mirror, causing all pagans to reveal their true form, demons and ghosts to have no place to hide, so to protect themselves they have to proclaim that the Shurangama Sutra is a fake sutra and should not be believed.

Some other people, ignorant and not wise enough to distinguish between truth and falsehood, who say whatever they say, also agree with them and say that Shurangama was not spoken by the Buddha. The Shurangama Sutra talks about morality, it is so accurate, so reasonable, so demons and ghosts, like the eagles of the left path, have no place to hide, they have to use such evil tricks to sabotage the sutra. If you do so, you will surely fall into hell.

Recently, some ignorant scholars, and some foolish Buddhist followers, do not have a correct understanding of Buddhism, do not clearly understand Buddhism, in short, know half the truth, criticize the words of saints, and then speak in a haphazard manner.

People who study Buddha dharma should thoroughly understand the meaning of the Shurangama Sutra, so that they can promote this sutra everywhere, praise, explain and uphold this sutra, in order to keep the righteous dharma in the world and let the evil dharma be destroyed. That is the responsibility of all Buddhist followers.

Today I would like to assure all of you that the Shurangama Sutra is the true Sutra. If that is not the case, I would like to go to hell, because I did not have a correct understanding of Buddha's teachings, pretending to be true, I would willingly accept that retribution. As Shurangama is a true sutra, I also make vows that forever and after life I will propagate the Shurangama Dharma, and preach the truth in the Shurangama. Think about it, if this sutra was not spoken by Buddha, then who could say such an accurate Dharma? I hope that someone who criticizes the Shurangama Sutra and says it is a fake sutra will quickly repentance and correct his mistake. If not, you will definitely fall into hell and have your tongue pulled out. I hope that those who recite the Shurangama Sutra, preach the Shurangama Sutra, promote the Shurangama Sutra, and circulate the Shurangama Sutra will soon attain Buddhahood.

tieu_de: To practice the Way, one must cut off desire and eliminate craving
tom_tat: Why do we have afflictions? Because of selfishness (selfishness). Why is there selfishness? Because we have desire, we find every way to keep it, fearing it will disappear. If it is injured, it will cause anger. Why angry? It's because of…
noi_dung:
To practice the Way, one must cut off desire and eliminate craving

Why do we have afflictions? Because of selfishness (selfishness). Why is there selfishness? Because we have desire, we find every way to keep it, fearing it will disappear. If it is injured, it will cause anger. Why angry? It is caused by ignorance and love. Suppose, without ignorance, without love, the angry mind will run 108,000 miles away, and even if you want to find it, you won't be able to find it.

If there is love, there is selfishness. Once you have a selfish mind, you will not use any tricks to reach your goal, you can even sacrifice your life without regretting yourself. Tracing it to the root is because of lust.

If there is no thought of desire, there must be no self-interest. Without selfishness, there is no affliction.

If there is affliction, there must be birth and death; If there is no affliction, there is no birth and death. Everyone knows this meaning, but they just don't practice it. You must know that, without desire, there is no ignorance. If ignorance is destroyed, the dharma nature will appear. When we study Buddha, we first learn to eliminate ignorance and eliminate afflictions. If you work towards perfection, you will attain liberation.

Why don't we have wisdom? Because of ignorance. Ignorance gives birth to desire, desire gives birth to self-interest, self-interest gives birth to afflictions. When we desire something but don't get it, there is trouble. People who are not good to us are also the cause of trouble. Why is there sorrow? Because there is a Self. If it is true that there is no self, then there is no suffering. If we can get to a place where there is no ignorance, no selfishness, then afflictions will disappear. Whether you believe it or not, the reason is like that. Thousand scriptures, talking about it over and over again is just that. Let the ego no longer exist, destroy ignorance, destroy desire, then there will be no selfishness, no afflictions, and you will not be able to find afflictions. Why? Because the root of the problem has been resolved.

You must pay attention! The five desires, wealth, form, fame, food, and sleep (sleep) are all brought about by ignorance and love. If there was no sex, we would see that nothing is important. Because there is sex, we feel that this is not good, that is not good, everything is not right, that is the devil of sex. If we can subdue this sexual demon, then we will quickly enter Tathagata's house, go to Tathagata's throne, wear Tathagata's robes, and preach Tathagata's Dharma.

tieu_de: meditation That teaching
tom_tat: "Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, practices the profound perfection of wisdom, sees the five aggregates of emptiness, relieves all suffering
noi_dung:
meditation That teaching

What is freedom?

"Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, practices the profound perfection of wisdom, sees the five aggregates of emptiness, and overcomes all suffering."

The Lotus Sutra of the Wonderful Dharma was finished last Tuesday. Today, on the occasion of the opening of the winter meditation retreat, I would like to teach the audience the opening verse of the Heart Sutra, which is also the essence of this sutra.

Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara is Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara. He realized that his ear was perfectly clear. How did he testify? He originally practiced the dharma "reflecting the text and nature, achieving the unsurpassed path." The reason is because He knows how to listen back to his own nature that He is free.

It is called freedom when one reaches the realm where there is no other person, no self, no sentient beings, and no recipient. Where is that realm? Where is there freedom? Where is it not available?

In the position of saints, there is freedom, but in the position of ordinary people, there is no freedom. Why is that? Because the saints are no longer entangled in the four appearances, the appearance of the person, the appearance of the self, the appearance of living beings, and the appearance of the recipient, the saints are free. Ordinary people are still entangled in these signs, so they have no freedom.

We are practitioners, but if we cannot practice the four emptiness of those signs, we will never be able to attain freedom, and we must definitely eliminate the three minds and four signs. The three minds refer to the past mind, present mind and future mind. All three minds are unattainable. The past mind cannot be attained! Why can't you grasp it? Because it has passed, where is there anymore to grasp? The present mind, as soon as we finish talking about that mind, it has become the past and cannot be grasped anymore. As for the future mind, because it hasn't arrived yet, it doesn't exist yet, so how can we grasp it? So all three minds cannot grasp it. Then with the four generals, you can also realize the four emptiness, which means you can contemplate freely.

What is the purpose of meditation? To contemplate freedom! Everyone must contemplate freedom. Whoever can be at ease is that person who contemplates at ease. Whoever is not at peace is not at peace. Avalokiteshvara is not the property of Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara, all living beings can be Avalokiteshvara.

We meditate to observe whether we can be free or not. If you are free, you will see that the five aggregates (form, feeling, perception, actions, consciousness) are all empty, that is, you will deeply practice the perfection of wisdom. Once you deeply practice the perfection of wisdom, you will be able to see clearly that the five aggregates are empty. Only then can you overcome all suffering. All suffering has been overcome, only then can one attain freedom.

On the occasion of the 98-day meditation session at the Buddha Teaching Hall,

San Francisco (predecessor of Golden Mountain Temple),

from November 15, 1970 to February 23, 1971.

tieu_de: Let's Return to Our Homeland
tom_tat: Not only Avalokitesvara and us are of the same body, but also all Buddhas of the ten directions and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions are of the same body with us. However, we and all Buddhas are not one. Why like…
noi_dung:
Let's Return to Our Homeland

Not only Avalokitesvara and us are of the same body, but also all Buddhas of the ten directions and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions are of the same body with us. However, we and all Buddhas are not one. Why is that? This meaning is similar to the following passage in the Lotus Sutra:

"There was a guy who was extremely poor. His father was an extremely wealthy businessman. But he left home and wandered far away, and did not see the way back to his hometown, so one day, he met his father without realizing it was his father. Why is that? Because I've been away from my father for so long that when I see him again I don't know it's my father."

The reason we are not one with all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is the same as the case of the poor guy not recognizing his father, as just mentioned. When we cultivate the Way, instead of having to leave our crazy dreams and aim for ultimate Nirvana, we leave our Dharma bodies, which are our parents, and then go out to wander and beg, not being able to find the way back to our hometown, how pitiful it is!

We must remember that we, Buddha and Bodhisattva are family members, that's why Buddha said: "All sentient beings have Buddha nature and can become Buddha." Now we go out and become poor people, forget our parents, forget our homeland, our parents are dharmakaya, Buddha and Bodhisattva. They all hope that we will soon return to our homeland - the Pure Land of Thuong Tich Quang.

Now we meditate - meditate what? It's about finding your dharmakaya parents. Called: "The ocean of suffering is boundless, the beginning of the end is over," This means that just by turning around, you can return to your original hometown. Because of the meaning of returning to one's homeland, there is this 98-day winter meditation course.

tieu_de: One Hundred Days of meditation
tom_tat: A 98-day meditation course in this Western country, although not necessarily unparalleled in the future, is unprecedented up to now. It is: Witness something you've never seen before, hear something you've never seen before...
noi_dung:
One Hundred Days of meditation

A 98-day meditation course in this Western country, although not necessarily unparalleled in the future, is unprecedented up to now. It is: Witness something you've never seen before, hear something you've never heard before! For thousands of years, there really has never been such a strenuous practice! Early in the morning, I started meditating at two o'clock, with an hour's rest in between, and didn't sleep until 12 o'clock at night. So every day you work for a full 21 hours. That's why it's said to be an unprecedented meditation course.

When you participate in this meditation course, you must test and endure, from the beginning to the end, and cannot give up halfway. Otherwise, all the effort you put in will be wasted, you won't get anything, and you will betray many of your wishes from the beginning. There is a saying: "Taste the hardships of suffering, only then will you become a noble person." Only then will one be a superior person among true Buddhists.

This meditation retreat made me happy because there were a few Bhikkhus and Bhikkhunis who developed the mind of "never-single yea," That means when it's time to sleep, they don't return to the room but sit in the meditation chair to rest. Such a way of practicing is truly unprecedented in the West. (The record book records: Now all the shamans at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas make vows to keep "one meal a day, no sleeping at night" (The sun is the same, the night is not the same). Such spirit is admirable.

While in Hong Kong, I attended a ten-week meditation retreat. During the retreat, there was also a bearded elder - Venerable Minh Quan, who also attended. That's an old monk, but I'm not. We sat together for a full seventy days, and the results between us were that no one was better or worse.

tieu_de: Maintain the Correct Meditation Path
tom_tat: The 98 days of meditation are about to begin. Among those leaving the home life, every day there will be a Duy-na, in charge of the work of clearing and calming; There is another ruler to take care of providing tea. Drink tea three times a day, or…
noi_dung:
Maintain the Correct Meditation Path

The 98 days of meditation are about to begin. Among those leaving the home life, every day there will be a Duy-na, in charge of the work of clearing and calming; There is another ruler to take care of providing tea. Drink tea three times a day, or four times, depending on the situation, not certain, "indeterminate" that! Because everyone uses meditation as much as possible, the fire energy rises, so drinking a lot of tea can cool down the fire. However, pay attention! Don't break the tea cup. You must know that Venerable Hu Van in the past dropped his tea cup, heard the sound of the cup breaking and became enlightened, it was just an unintentional thing.

Anyone who intentionally breaks a teacup will never be able to become enlightened, because you did it intentionally. So say: "The conscious mind sees delusion, the unconscious mind perceives." You didn't have the intention of breaking it but it turned out to be broken, that's great!

During meditation, no one is allowed to talk. Each person takes care of his own voice tou and makes his own efforts. If you see anyone, ignore it. Why? Because without you, without me! Whoever comes will come, whoever goes will go, just concentrate and focus on the question "Who is the Buddha?" Within 98 days there will be results.

During this winter meditation retreat, those who are not yet enlightened will be punished for one hundred days of kneeling in front of the Buddha altar. As for those who are enlightened, I would like to set up a great banquet of enlightenment. Whatever food you want to eat will be there, guaranteed to be full for a hundred people. There is a saying: "Heaven's magical offerings, meditation review to-da." That time is considered the most glorious moment in Buddhism. You remember! If we want to be enlightened, we must keep that rule! If you don't want enlightenment, then please do so, no one is forcing you.

tieu_de: Abandon All Jealousy And Pride
tom_tat: Now the meditation session begins. So many things called jealousy and arrogance, you must put them all down. Now I'm testing to see if you truly let go of those things or not. How to check? First is to fight with…
noi_dung:
Abandon All Jealousy And Pride

Now the meditation session begins. So many things called jealousy and arrogance, you must put them all down. Now I'm testing to see if you truly let go of those things or not. How to check? First, hit with incense sticks. Being beaten but not feeling the pain is considered okay and qualifies you to participate in this winter's meditation retreat.

However, if you don't know pain, you are as inert as a table, without perception; Knowing pain means not being able to let it go. So at this point, let's take a look - how?

Now the one who gets beaten and doesn't run away is the real man. Being a great man, he must have a heroic spirit, not afraid of suffering, not afraid of hardships, full of spirit to endure hardship, for a period of 98 days, without turning back, from beginning to end. You must have a determination to consider death as nothing, then you can succeed.

Before entering meditation, I have this verse:

In the spring of the great earth, hundreds of creatures are born, Chalking up the empty space, free from Mr. Tong's desire to not stray from people, egos, and appearances. The Dharma world, however, is extremely tolerant.

Great earth spring returns hundreds of creatures: This meditation retreat is the symbol of spring's return. Hundreds of species joyfully sprouted lushly. Everyone has the opportunity for enlightenment and the light of self-nature to appear.

Chalking up empty space is free of you: Emptiness is inherently invisible. If the result of emptiness were to crumble (disintegrate), then emptiness would no longer exist. 'On your own' At that time, it is truly qualified!

Try not to fall in love with one's ego: From then on, you will no longer be entangled in human appearances, nor will you be entangled in ego appearances. Humanity is empty, dharma is also empty. All human dharmas are empty, so one is free, no longer clinging to self or dharma. Not being attached is liberation.

Although the Dharma world is extremely tolerant: Even though the dharma world is boundless and boundless, we can still embrace the entire dharma world inside, in other words, compared to the dharma world we are even bigger. That is the ability of a great man.

You have to use your own efforts. What elaborate? That is the sentence: "Who is Buddha?" hay tham: "Before my parents were born, what was my original appearance?" or sentence: "What is impossible without!" If you work hard, you will definitely get good news (enlightenment). Now let's get started! Enter! Enter! Enter! The meditation retreat officially begins, no talking is allowed!

tieu_de: You Are All Good Knowledge
tom_tat: Good and knowledgeable people! Why do you call yourself a wise man? If you are not a wise person, you will never come to Prajnaparamita (meditation hall). Everyone who comes to the Prajnaparamita to practice is all good...
noi_dung:
You Are All Good Knowledge

Good and knowledgeable people! Why do you call yourself a wise man? If you are not a wise person, you will never come to Prajnaparamita (meditation hall). Everyone who comes to Prajnaparamita to practice is all good knowledge, that's why we call you good knowledge.

Prajna is Sanskrit (Prajna), translated as wisdom. You are all people of great wisdom who have just come to Prajnaparamita. Why great wisdom? Because in past lives you have sown many good roots, many seeds of Bodhi. Also in the past, you have made offerings Buddha, making offerings Dharma, making offerings Sangha. Having accumulated such merits, today the karma has been achieved and one can attend a meditation course. This is not a small cause, but a great cause, it is also the cause of being born and escaping death, which can also be said to be the cause of becoming a Buddha. Because of the above reasons, I call you a wise man.

Good knowledge is knowing the good path, not knowing the evil path. If one knows the evil way, one must call it evil knowledge. What is good knowledge? Good knowledge is right knowledge, right view, actions in accordance with Buddha Dharma, practice according to Buddha Dharma, every action and gesture corresponds to Buddha Dharma. What is evil knowledge? Evil knowledge is wrong knowledge, wrong views, everything goes against Buddha's teachings, that is, like the saying "apostasy, children maintain," Turn your back on religion and walk away.

Now you gather at the Prajnaparamita hall, meditating single-mindedly to seek enlightenment and great wisdom. If you are truly wise and truly enlightened, you will absolutely not do crazy things again. Such enlightenment and insight are all achieved through diligent practice. Therefore, practitioners should not be afraid of suffering or difficulties. When sitting to meditate, even if your legs hurt, your back is tired, you don't care. You must maintain the spirit of great fearlessness, live and die with meditation, live and die with practice, absolutely cannot surrender because of pain and fatigue, must be a great man, a great hero.

A practitioner must have unwavering patience, a will not to retreat, absolutely not bow down in the face of all adversity, absolutely not be overcome. The more I try to endure the pain in my legs, the more I try to endure my tired back. Sleepy? Open your eyes wide, challenge the ghost to sleep. The sleepier you are the better. Either way, you will be greedy and greedy until the positive energy returns, then the sleep demon will have to run away. If we do not fight the sleeping ghost, then we will forever be its slave, obeying its orders and being controlled by it.

tieu_de: Realizing the Face of the Origin
tom_tat: Our purpose in participating in meditation is to open our wisdom, return to our roots, and absolutely recognize our original presence.
noi_dung:
Realizing the Face of the Origin

Our purpose in participating in meditation is to open our wisdom, return to our roots, and absolutely recognize our original face.

What is our original appearance like? Together with all Buddhas, we are one, no difference. However, we, as sentient beings, do not have wisdom so we do not recognize it, and from that reason we become crazy, turning upside down, living and dying in a chaotic dreamscape, and even appearing more, making the delusion even more delusional, already in the dream, more dreams, in the chaos, even more chaos. Why is it like that? Because I couldn't meet a wise man, I couldn't have anyone tell me the way back to my homeland, that is, the way to find my true future. Now a large number of good and knowledgeable people have gathered here, together heading towards the broad, bright path to find their original vision. It is true:

The ten directions gather together

The period of studying non-action

Try the Buddha market

Mind does not access recursively.

Meaning:

Ten directions gather together

Everyone learns non-action

This is a Buddhist school

The mind does not pass the honor.

Good and knowledgeable people from the ten directions, come to this Prajnaparamita to study the Dharma of non-action together. Prajnaparamita is the Buddha's recruiting school. Whoever reaches the place of no-cause and no-self will be awarded the mark. Whoever cannot let go will be defeated. Who cares? That person passes the Poinsettia. At that time, the brocade shirt returned to the village, resplendent to the ancestors.

If you want to be a great man or a great hero, you have to sit down and practice meditation to be able to achieve your goal. The great hero is the great enlightenment, the great enlightenment is the Buddha. If you sit in meditation and reach the state of selflessness, you won't even notice if your legs hurt, and you won't even know if your back is tired. Inside, I didn't feel my body or mind. Outside, I didn't know there was a world. At that moment, in an instant, I suddenly had great enlightenment: That's how it is!

If it is clear that there is a self, then there is a "self". at this place. You live in this place, who doesn't live in this place? Who is not here? No one is here, no one is not here, so it is called selflessness.

Because there is no existence, there is no self. If there is still existence, then there is also ego existence. If there is existence, it should be self-existence, not self-existence. Freedom cannot have self, if there is self then it is not freedom. Because of the ego, many troubles arise, which cannot be completely explained. Come on, if you don't get enough sleep, your spirit won't be at peace. If you don't eat enough, your stomach won't feel comfortable. If you don't wear enough, your body will get cold. Why do these phenomena exist? Because there is a self. If you want to have no self, there is only one way, which is to go to the meditation hall and meditate, meditate back and forth, meditate until you achieve no self, achieving the realm called: "Non-human and selfless Avalokiteshvara, non-empty and non-form view Tathagata." At that time, you will be extremely free, and you will automatically know what your original appearance is like. However, reaching that realm is not easy. That's why we need to try to be patient and endure all the pain and all the hardships. If you pass through this barrier, you will experience a feeling of joy: is to eat with the joy of meditation, and live in the joy of dharma.

No matter what job you do, the beginning is relatively difficult. Over time, you will get used to it and won't find it difficult anymore. Sitting meditation is the same. In the path of meditation, try to endure. Once you have endured, there will be no more realms to disturb you. So there was a little bit of concentration. Having a little concentration means having a little wisdom power. Accumulating small amounts into great things, when the power of wisdom is complete, enlightenment will automatically occur.

tieu_de: Meditation is maintaining the precepts
tom_tat: We sit in meditation, single-mindedly thinking, "Who is the Buddha?" and maintain this first line, continuously without stopping, intimately without any gaps. So during the time of "reciting Buddha's name, who is it?" Can we cause bad karma?…
noi_dung:
Meditation is maintaining the precepts

We sit in meditation, single-mindedly thinking, "Who is the Buddha?" and maintain this first line, continuously without stopping, intimately without any gaps. So during the time of "reciting Buddha's name, who is it?" Can we cause bad karma? Like killing, stealing, committing adultery or lying, drinking alcohol, is that okay? Absolutely no such things can happen. So maintaining the precepts. There is a saying: "Non-maintenance of maintenance," not intending to maintain the precepts but naturally maintaining the precepts. Maintaining the precepts will give birth to concentration, and concentration will give birth to wisdom. During the time of not meditating, many delusions arise in the mind, causing people to kill, steal, commit adultery, lie, drink alcohol, and even indulge in all sorts of things regardless of the matter. One wrong thought can give rise to many karma sins. Sitting here meditating, there are no more problems, everything is solved, that is the meaning of not intentionally maintaining the precepts but naturally maintaining the precepts.

Sitting here in meditation means cultivating precepts, concentration and wisdom. Cultivating precepts, concentration and wisdom means eliminating greed, anger and ignorance. Therefore, meditation includes all practices, all dharmas are included in meditation. We are greedy, but we must engage in meditation, the more greed we have, the more wisdom we have. Don't be greedy for meditation, the more greedy you become, the more foolish you become. Taking the sun for the moon, isn't that crazy?

tieu_de: Train to Become an Indestructible Diamond Body
tom_tat: We engage in meditation to open up wisdom. When it is not time for wisdom to open, we are bound to encounter suffering. For example, when we use a big fire to refine gold, when we burn it, we will know whether it is real or fake. People say: "The needle's foot is inviolable...
noi_dung:
Train to Become an Indestructible Diamond Body

We engage in meditation to open up wisdom. When it is not time for wisdom to open, we are bound to encounter suffering. For example, when we use a big fire to refine gold, when we burn it, we will know whether it is real or fake. People say: "The foot of the needle cannot be punished by fire." True gold is not afraid of the fire of the furnace. No matter how you refine it, the weight remains the same and the color becomes even brighter. The main meditation hall is a large furnace. You are all real gold, refined into an indestructible diamond body here.

If you want to become an indestructible diamond body, at first you have to suffer. After suffering until the end, only then can you achieve the realm as just mentioned. Everyone try your best to participate! Be greedy! If you are greedy thoroughly, you will become an indestructible diamond body.

Someone said:

This suffering is truly unbearable.

Who knows it's suffering, who knows it hurts. Someone else said:

I know suffering, I know pain.

Who are you? Someone else said:

I am my own body.

Your body is you, so even if you died, would your body still be here? Why hit it, it doesn't feel pain; curse at him, he still endures? Someone else said:

Because I'm dead, there are no more problems!

So, here we are considered dead, so there is a saying: "The lustful demon is immortal, the immortal is alive and dead," Meaning, if you want to become an immortal, first live like a dead person.

Now let me become a dead person, that is, I will have no greed, no anger or ignorance. Why is there greed, anger and ignorance? Because you have not considered your body as a dead body. If you're dead, then what else do you want? What else is there? What else is there? Now, although you are not dead, just act as if you are dead. So who is still greedy? Stadium for whom? Si for whom else? The death of meditation is not real death. If you want to be enlightened, you must die once, then practice to become an indestructible diamond body.

tieu_de: meditation The Way Is Where Saints Are Created
tom_tat: When Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha was cultivating in Tuyet Son, he only ate one sesame seed and one grain of wheat to maintain his life. Because of this story, everyone knows Tuyet Son. Later, Buddha went to the Bodhi tree and sat quietly for 49 days when he attained enlightenment,...
noi_dung:
meditation The Way Is Where Saints Are Created

When Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha was cultivating in Tuyet Son, he only ate one sesame seed and one grain of wheat to maintain his life. Because of this story, everyone knows Tuyet Son. Later, Buddha came to the Bodhi tree and sat quietly for 49 days, then he attained enlightenment and attained Buddhahood, so this place became a holy place, just as the saying goes: "masterpiece of the land." Being called a holy land is also thanks to the saint's reputation. Wherever a saint lives, that place becomes a holy place. Wherever an ordinary person lives, if he wants that place to be a holy place, he cannot become a holy land.

There is an ancient saying: "Heaven's time is not equal to the advantage of the earth, and the advantage of the land is not equal to the harmony of people." In meditation, we practice together, that is harmony. Not bothering anyone, it's called dharma. Only the Dharma place can be like that. Only by having an ashram can there be a place to meditate, and only by practicing quietly can one gain wisdom. If there is no ashram, even if you want to meditate, you can't do it. Now, fortunately we have the ashram, we must seriously practice.

Our holy land is the Prajnaparamita, a place that specializes in creating saints - not ordinary people, but saints, or arahants, or Bodhisattvas. Whoever is a saint is not afraid of suffering or difficulty. Whoever is still afraid of suffering and difficulty, even though he is not a saint now, will still be a saint in the future. What does that mean? Originally, I had making vows: "All disciples who take refuge with me will definitely become Buddhas. If I don't become Buddha, I will wait for them until they become Buddha." I know for sure that in the future they will also become Buddhas, so I say that in the future they will become saints.

For all of you, I have high hopes and hope that you will make every effort, don't be lazy, don't be careless, keep the rules, follow the Dharma and practice, to be determined to become a saint. I hope that within 98 days you will achieve the indestructible vajra sainthood.

The Sixth Patriarch said:

Buddha Dharma in the world

Not separated from the worldly sense

Lying away from Bodhi

Cable is like a bridge.

Translation:

Buddha Dharma in the world

There is no enlightenment outside the world

Find Bodhi outside the world

It's no different than looking for a rabbit's horn.

Based on the above four sentences in the sutra text to analyze, the practitioner must have it, and the dharma protector must also have it. Gentlemen! If you are willing to leave the home life, then practice the Dharma. If you are willing to leave, then protect the Dharma. Everyone fulfills their responsibilities and fulfills their duties. Those who leave the home life sincerely practice, those who lay sincerely protect the Dharma, everyone does their own job!

All dharmas are Buddha dharmas, is there anything to be happy about or not to be happy about? When practicing meditation, you should use effort here, not with a mind of love or hate, but with a normal mind. For example, the water surface of a lake in the spring does not have any ripples, so the mixed substances naturally settle down, making the water surface calm and clear. Greed is the same, without false thoughts, the dharmakaya appears. The above few Dharma sentences are very important, I hope you practice according to that meaning, meaning your wisdom will quickly open. There is a saying: "Theory is the dharma, the practice is the path," that is, saying it is the dharma, doing it is the way. Now, knowing the Dharma but not practicing it is not right at all.

tieu_de: Plow Some Part, Harvest That Part
tom_tat: On the occasion of this meditation session, many people did not believe that there was a place where people practiced so diligently. Some people think we're joking, some people say we're crazy. If not, why don't you sleep, then...
noi_dung:
Plow Some Part, Harvest That Part

On the occasion of this meditation session, many people did not believe that there was a place where people practiced so diligently. Some people think we're joking, some people say we're crazy. If not, why don't you sleep, eat less, and practice 21 hours a day? That's impossible, absolutely impossible! Outside, people criticize like that. However, for us, we will definitely do it perfectly, making them shocked and exclaiming: ?! Really practice!

Be brave and diligent every day, absolutely not retreating, so that everyone can see that we are truly cultivating, while they are left behind, behind. We must move ahead of them, to become their leaders, to lead them on the path of practice. To become a leader, of course, you must practice righteously. During practice, not even a minute is wasted, every hour, every moment, every thought, don't forget "reciting who is Buddha?" The ultimate taboo in spiritual practice is laziness. If you are truly lazy, you won't be able to get there. Where is that place? It's so mysterious that it can't be expressed. That realm is inconceivable, like a person drinking water, whether it is hot or cold, that person automatically knows, outsiders cannot know, they can only experience it themselves.

If we have the opportunity to attend a meditation course, we must attend it. Plan once, reap once. If you don't eat, you can be hungry, but if you don't participate in meditation, you can't; You can endure the cold without a shirt, but if you don't participate in a meditation retreat, you can't. Because all Buddhas in the ten directions must go through that path to become Buddha.

Some people are afraid of suffering and do not dare to participate in meditation, which is a misconception. In the past, we have never encountered meditation retreats like this, so we continue to live and die in samsara. If we have ever participated in meditation, then we are certainly not delusional, certainly not crazy; Regarding the five desires of wealth, form, fame, food, and lobes, absolutely do not be attached; Consider the five desires as five paths leading to hell.

Sitting still in meditation, when the fire pharynx reaches its level, there will be a type of vajra concentration that will keep us from being swayed by the five desires. At that time, there is no desire for wealth, no desire for form, no desire for fame, no desire for food, no desire for sleep, even in dreams there is no longer a single thought of desire, in dreams the mind is also pure, that is the realm that will be reached. Then, by further practicing, the practitioner will reach the dreamless realm to achieve sainthood.

While awake, people can still control themselves. The external environment can tempt you, but with a strong mind and strong concentration, the external environment cannot be shaken. However, in a dream, you cannot control it. When you see a ghost, you are afraid of it. When you see a tiger, you are afraid of a tiger. When you see money, you crave money. When you see beauty, you crave beauty. That means being fascinated by the outside world. If you are lazy, you can control it in your dreams, but you cannot control it when you are sick. Or while illness can control it, when it comes to death, it cannot be controlled. If you want to be in control of life and death, you must practice meditation. Using effort like that, one part of the effort will bring one part of the harvest, ten parts of the effort will bring ten parts of the harvest. There is a saying: "If you practice, you will be certified, if you practice, you will be certified," Whoever practices, he will attain enlightenment. If he does not practice, he will not attain enlightenment. The value of practice must be based on one's own genuine effort. Only then can one travel freely and have peace of mind, because in the world there is no such thing as being achieved without effort.

tieu_de: Suffering is the Foundation of Buddhist Practice
tom_tat: Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha became a Buddha countless lives in the past. However, because of His great compassion, he wants to save sentient beings, especially those who do not have a long-term mind, do not have a strong and sincere mind, therefore...
noi_dung:
Suffering is the Foundation of Buddhist Practice

Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha became a Buddha countless lives in the past. However, because of His great compassion, He wanted to save sentient beings, especially those who did not have a long-term mind and did not have a strong and sincere mind, so He manifested as Buddha to guide them.

To point out the basic factor, for six years he practiced asceticism at Tuyet Son. Why practice hard? Because austerity is the foundation to become Buddha. For example, when we build a high-rise house, the first job is to make a solid foundation, then build a high floor. If the foundation is not strong, it is impossible, it is like building a house on a sandy beach.

We meditate in this meditation hall, which is much better than at Tuyet Mountain. Even though he didn't eat well, he wasn't hungry enough to be as thin as a stick. How much more pleasant it is compared to the Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha in Tuyet Son! Now, we have enough opportunities like this, and there are ashrams that organize meditation practices like this, we must definitely cheer ourselves up and try our best to practice meditation. We must imitate the behavior of Bodhisattva Vi-da, majestic and majestic, holding the vajra to subdue the sleeping demon, not to surrender to it. The head bowed down in front of the stomach is not the correct posture for someone participating in meditation. Also, don't learn the habit of a black turtle, pulling your head and neck back, that is not the dignity of a person practicing meditation.

You should not use too much effort in meditation or do it too weakly, one way is excessive, the other is inadequate. Practicing practice means keeping the middle way, avoiding bias, so there is a saying: "to be patient, to be bold, to be brave, to be brave, to succeed," means:

If you fold it, it will be tight, if you loosen it, it will overlap. If you don't fold or loosen, then you will succeed. Just like that, work hard every day, every hour, don't rush, don't relax, gradually you will reach success and success means reaching an inconceivable realm. Achieving that realm is not too happy, but not achieving it is not too sad either. If we are too happy, the demon of joy will come and disturb us, making us lose concentration, causing us to giggle from morning to night, no longer looking natural. Has anyone asked what to laugh about? Don't know. I don't know why but I laugh like a crazy person, that's a crazy ghost. If we let our compassion go too far, the ghost of grief will come and disturb us, making us lose our concentration, causing us to sob and cry from morning to night, in an abnormal way. Ask why cry? Say: "Sentient beings are so miserable! So pitiful! I want to save sentient beings." If we cannot save ourselves, how can we save sentient beings? That is the phenomenon of ghosts being possessed by someone.

At the meditation hall, we concentrate on meditation, even if our feet hurt, we must endure it. Patience to the extreme will stop the pain. Why? Because suffering comes to an end, then comes goodness, so it is said that suffering is the foundation for attaining enlightenment. The following sentences describe the meaning of this suffering:

Unexpectedly, the bone chilled for a moment

Cham dac apricot flower phac ty incense.

Translation:

Haven't tasted the bone-chilling cold yet. Where can I enjoy the scent of apricot blossoms?

tieu_de: What is called the Bodhi Sea Diamond?
tom_tat: What is a diamond? Diamonds carry the meaning of indestructibility. What is called Bodhi Sea? That is the meaning of the ocean of great enlightenment. In fact, this meaning is deeper and wider than the sea. This ocean of enlightenment is truly immense...
noi_dung:
What is called the Bodhi Sea Diamond?

What is a diamond? Diamonds carry the meaning of indestructibility. What is called Bodhi Sea? That is the meaning of the ocean of great enlightenment. In fact, this meaning is deeper and wider than the sea. This ocean of enlightenment is truly vast and boundless, in short, inconceivable. We practice the diamond method, practicing so that our self-nature is as clear as a diamond, so that our mind and body are as solid as a diamond, and so that our body is as indestructible as a diamond.

We meditate at the Prajnaparamita Hall, which is cultivating the great diamond dharma, that is, using the fire of prajna samadhi to burn away all habitual energies, burning the three poisons of greed, anger, and ignorance, cultivating them into wisdom and concentration. How to burn? That means using patience - tenacity, using success - sincerity, using constant - durability to burn. Practice continuously, day by day, day by day, there will come a time when your clear self-nature will appear. That meaning is like the sunlight melting the snow, each day it melts a little bit, over time the snow will disappear.

Meditating in the meditation hall is melting the snow in one's own nature. This snow has accumulated over many lifetimes, now we use wisdom to melt it. That snow is ignorance and affliction. It is an obstacle that causes the practitioner's mind to lose its purity, so if it is not eliminated, it will not be possible. Still with it, there are many afflictions, such as feeling miserable, feeling pain, feeling uncomfortable, for example. If you practice meditation and practice concentration, you will definitely have concentration, then your legs will not feel pain, your back will not feel tired, your head will not feel sore. If all suffering is no longer felt, then one can break through the barrier of birth and death, and attain the Bodhi Sea of diamonds.

To reach this diamond sea of Bodhi is to become one with the Dharma Realm. How big and wide is the Dharma realm? I can't say it all, I can't even think of it, it's so huge. The Shurangama Sutra says: "Voidness is born from great enlightenment, like a foam in the sea" (Without giving birth to great enlightenment, one is like a sea of seagulls developing). How big and wide is this nothingness? Truly there is no shore or shore, no one knows. Today, although scientists have clearly presented it, there is still no scale to measure emptiness. The vastness of real nothingness is indescribable and immeasurable. Yet to the ocean of great enlightenment, it is just a foam. Emptiness is born from the ocean of great enlightenment, so it is said that the ocean of great enlightenment is the mother of emptiness.

We must return to the source, to the origin, all the way to the Bodhi Sea. That's why there is a magazine published by us called "Diamond Bodhi Sea." Our meditation hall is called "Diamond Bodhi Hai Zen Hall," We take the name Diamond Bodhi Hai Nhan. Later, when he becomes an arahant, he will be named Vajra Bodhi Sea Arahant; When he becomes a Bodhisattva, he will be called Vajra Bodhi Sea Bodhisattva, then when he becomes Buddha, he will be called Vajra Bodhi Sea Buddha. In short, the five words Vajra Bodhi Sea are our trademark.

When we meditate, we return to the Bodhi Sea. Right now all the Buddhas in the ten directions along with the Bodhisattvas and Arhats are there waiting for us. We must try our best, be diligent and courageous, so that we can quickly reach our destination - the ocean of great enlightenment, and not let all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas be disappointed.

All sentient beings have their roots in the ocean of great enlightenment, but because of ignorance, they became deluded, and because of deludement, they created so much karma that they suffered the retribution of samsara. The situation is like a small speck of dust floating in the air, sometimes above, sometimes below, sometimes east, sometimes west, floating aimlessly. We are just like that small speck of dust, floating in samsara, suddenly ascending to heaven, suddenly falling into hell, suddenly becoming a human, suddenly becoming an asura, suddenly being an animal, suddenly a hungry ghost. When you are confused and do not have enlightenment, you will be lost in the six realms of samsara. If enlightenment and delusion are eliminated, then that is the path to life and escape from death.

Why are we delusional but not enlightened? Because we are heavily poisoned, that is, the three poisons of greed, anger, and ignorance, we cannot be enlightened. If you want enlightenment, you must practice meditation. Meditation without confusion is the path that leads us out of the three worlds.

Before enlightenment, everything you see is false, especially when it comes to money, lust, fame, eating, drinking, sleeping. You are attached to everything and cannot let it go. If it were enlightenment, then everything would become an illusion, like the image of a flower in the mirror, the shadow of the moon in the water, all are illusions, not real.

Our own nature is also inherently pure, it can be compared to clear water, not cloudy, looking down you can see all the way to the bottom of the water. However, from a single thought of ignorance, afflictions arise, like clear water that turns cloudy. The water is not clear, the moon does not appear, just like when you are ignorant, the light of wisdom does not appear.

The arising of ignorance can be compared to cold air causing water to turn into ice. For example, if you take a bowl of water and throw it on someone's face, that person will not be harmed. But if that water turns into ice, that person will definitely have a bleeding head injury, which can even be life-threatening. The same object produces two types of effects, so there is a saying: "Defilement is Bodhi." Ice symbolizes afflictions, water symbolizes Bodhi. Melting ice into water will benefit all living things.

tieu_de: One Thought Does Not Give Birth to Complete Manifestation
tom_tat: The above mentioned realm is the image of the practitioner's efforts. The effort is so elaborate that it can be compared to the moon shining in the sky, the wind blowing right on the water's surface, but not even the slightest ripple. What a peaceful sight…
noi_dung:
One Thought Does Not Give Birth to Complete Manifestation

The origin of the moon and heavenly mind

Wind and water are unconscious

One ancient sound with strange taste

The trick is to gain the least knowledge

The above mentioned realm is the image of the practitioner's efforts. The effort is so elaborate that it can be compared to the moon shining in the sky, the wind blowing right on the water's surface, but not even the slightest ripple. It is truly a scene that is both pure and gentle, with a strange meaning that not many people know.

By working hard to reach a place where there is no self, no people, no sentient beings, no receiving beings, inside there is no feeling of body or mind, there is no world outside, then one can grasp the meaning of this mystery. There is something that very few people know, because only through personal experience can we know.

Cultivating the Way means cultivating yourself, applying yourself for yourself. It's not about cultivating for others, it's not about using effort for others. There is a saying: "The matter of one's own birth and death is resolved by oneself; If you eat it yourself, you'll be full yourself." If you practice, you can completely escape birth and death. If you don't practice, of course you cannot liberate birth and death.

We must practice to become a mindless person, that is, the emptiness of the body and mind, the emptiness of the world outside, and emptiness are the same thing. That is the time when accepting people is also not, and accepting the dharma is also not. How to witness that realm? Must practice meditation. To practice meditation, one must have a calm mind, concentrate one's thoughts, and not think wildly. Like a cat watching for mice, like a chicken incubating eggs, like a dragon raising pearls, you must wholeheartedly preserve, pay attention, and concentrate only to reach your destination.

We consider: "Who is Buddha?" The word "who" is the mouse and this greedy seat is also the mouth of the mouse hole, so do not be negligent every moment. If a loophole lets the mouse run away, how can we catch "who?" That's why there is a saying: "A single thought does not produce complete manifestation; as soon as the six senses move, they are covered by clouds." When a single thought does not arise, the entire "great use" appears, the root of wisdom is revealed, but once the six senses, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, stir, it is like when the sky is clear but clouds come and cover the sun.

When a thought does not arise, there is no body or mind inside, and no world outside. Meditating in this realm will no longer breathe, although you will not die. On the outside, there is no more respiration, but on the inside, respiration is still active. If the thought arises that: "A! I'm out of breath!" then breathing naturally resumes. A single thought does not arise, breathing stops, that is turning the invisible wheel of Dharma, singing a song of no birth!

tieu_de: Cultivating the Way cannot give rise to anger
tom_tat: Previously, there was a person who practiced concentration called the land of non-perception, and wanted to be born in the heavens in the land of non-perception. He sat as a monk by the seashore. Just as he was about to meditate, he heard a noise coming from the water. He looked down and saw a fish...
noi_dung:
Cultivating the Way cannot give rise to anger

Previously, there was a person who practiced concentration called the land of non-perception, and wanted to be born in the heavens in the land of non-perception. He sat as a monk by the seashore. Just as he was about to meditate, he heard a noise coming from the water. He looked down and saw a fish swimming underwater. He then continued his practice, paying no attention to the fish. However, underwater there was a loud, continuous noise. He opened his eyes and looked down. It turned out that the same fish was swimming back and forth in front of him. An angry thought arose in his heart, so he said to the fish: "If you still prevent me from entering my concentration, I will eat you and swallow you whole!" The fish heard that and swam away, not daring to come back again.

The above-mentioned practitioner entered the samadhi of non-perception, and the next day was born in the heavenly realm of non-perception, enjoying blessings lasting eighty thousand great kalpas. When the blessings run out, he falls into the animal world, becomes a seabird (fisherman), catches fish every day to eat, and fulfills his wish. When Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha attained enlightenment, when he preached Dharma to seabirds, that person attained liberation. In the next life, this person became a human, followed Buddha leaving the home life and attained Arhatship. According to this koan, we see that ordinary people who practice the Way must absolutely avoid anger. If you are not careful and let anger arise, there will be consequences in the future. We should remember to be vigilant.
